items.desc: At Flexion, we're building the intelligence layer powering the next generation of humanoid robots. Our mission is to accelerate the transition from fragile prototypes to real-world humanoid deployment. We are founded by leading scientists in robot reinforcement learning (ex-Nvidia, ex-ETH Zürich), and backed by leading international VC firms. In just months, we’ve gone from our first line of code to deploying real humanoid capabilities. The role As our VLA/WAM Research Engineer, you'll develop the foundation models that power our humanoid robots, spanning model architecture, large-scale pre-training, adaptation, and post-training. You will work across the model lifecycle: designing VLA and World-Action Model architectures, training foundation models on large and diverse embodied datasets, developing methods for efficient adaptation to new tasks and embodiments, and using robot experience to continuously improve model capabilities. In particular, we are looking for researchers and engineers with deep experience in one or more of the following areas: VLA/VLM or multimodal model architecture, large-scale foundation-model pre-training, world models and predictive learning, robot learning, or post-training and continual learning. If you have strong depth in one of these areas and are excited to work across the broader problem of building general-purpose robot foundation models, you will be a strong fit for the role. Key responsibilities VLA/WAM Architecture: Design and develop multimodal foundation models combining vision, language, robot state, actions, and temporal context for general-purpose robotic control. Foundation Model Pretraining: Develop and execute large-scale pretraining across diverse robot embodiments, teleoperation, egocentric human data, and simulated experience. Training Recipes & Scaling: Improve data mixtures, training objectives, optimization strategies, and distributed training workflows to deliver increasingly capable foundation models on a regular cadence. World-Action Models: Develop predictive world and action models for representation learning, future-state prediction, planning, and robot policy improvement. Adaptation & Mid-training: Develop methods to efficiently adapt pretrained models to new tasks, environments, embodiments, and capabilities. Post-training & Reinforcement Learning: Improve models using real-world and simulated robot experience, including imitation learning, RL, reward/value-guided learning, and specialist-to-generalist distillation. Continual Learning: Develop methods to learn from autonomous rollouts, failures, interventions, and recoveries while retaining existing capabilities and avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Evaluation & Research: Design rigorous experiments, evaluate models in simulation and on real robots, and use results to guide architecture and training decisions. Requirements Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with hands-on experience developing and training modern deep-learning models. Research or engineering experience in one or more of the following: VLA/VLM architectures, multimodal foundation models, world models, large-scale pretraining, robot learning, or RL/post-training. Experience owning substantial model development or training experiments, including architecture choices, training objectives, optimization, and evaluation. Solid understanding of modern deep-learning architectures, representation learning, and the relationship between data, training objectives, and model performance. Ability to design rigorous experiments, diagnose training failures, and use empirical results to guide research decisions. Familiarity with large-scale datasets, model training workflows, and the challenges of generalization across tasks, environments, or embodiments. Ability to critically evaluate recent research and translate promising ideas into working models and experiments. Comfortable working across model architecture, training, and adaptation while bringing particular expertise in at least one of these areas. Additionally, the following are a plus but not required: Experience training VLA, VLM, diffusion, flow-matching, video/world models, or other multimodal generative architectures. Experience with distributed training, multi-node GPU systems, large-scale data mixtures, and foundation-model training optimization. Experience with reinforcement learning, offline RL, reward/value learning, specialist distillation, or continual learning. Experience with predictive world models, video generation, latent dynamics, or self-supervised representation learning. Experience with multi-embodiment robot learning, action representations, or adapting policies across different robot platforms. Experience working with teleoperation, egocentric video, simulation, autonomous rollouts, or other large-scale embodied datasets. Experience evaluating learned policies on real robots, particularly humanoids or dexterous manipulation systems. Benefits Competitive compensation …

items.desc: StellDirVor is an independent consulting, trade and technology company specializing in immersive technologies for healthcare. We support organizations in implementing digital innovations — Virtual, Augmented and Mixed Reality as well as AI — particularly for learning, training and real-time assistance in clinical and care environments. By combining technology and healthcare, we help optimize processes, improve knowledge transfer and enhance quality of care. Supported by a Germany (ZIM) and Taiwanese (GIPIP) partnership grant, we are currently developing ARAIAS — an AR- and AI-based hands-free training and assistance system for chronic wound care. Using AR smart glasses, the system enables 3D capture, AI-supported analysis, and standardized remote expertise and documentation directly at the point of care. As our ML Engineer (Computer Vision & ML Ops), you will build the AI capabilities at the core of ARAIAS: evaluating and fine-tuning computer vision models on smart glasses data, running the ML operations behind them, and applying generative AI to create synthetic medical images for education. We're at an early stage — moving from concept to working prototype — so the near-term focus is on validating models and building toward a proof of concept we can test in real education and clinical settings. As part of a small team, you will own the full data lifecycle end to end — from sourcing, consent and annotation to preparation — alongside model development and deployment. We welcome candidates at different experience levels. What matters most is a solid ML foundation and genuine awareness of the medical imaging domain. items.desc: Build the Physical AI powering the next generation of home robots. The next major technological wave is approaching: Robots for the home. Technology is moving beyond the digital world and starting to take action in our physical lives – finally taking on the everyday tasks that smartphones and apps have barely been able to simplify. Mana Robotics develops autonomous robots for everyday life, with the ambition of becoming Europe's leading home robotics brand: innovative, beautifully designed, trustworthy, and relentlessly focused on real-world usefulness. Our first product tackles one of the most time-consuming household tasks: preparing meals every day. Our ultra-compact, autonomous cooking robot "Mana One" prepares meals from fresh ingredients entirely on its own – the biggest leap forward in household convenience since the invention of the dishwasher. After several years of development, research in Physical AI, and eight generations of hardware tested in real-world environments, we are now bringing this new product category to market. At the heart of our technology is a fundamental challenge: Teaching robots to perform complex physical tasks reliably in the real world. From handling ingredients and manipulating kitchen tools to adapting to unfamiliar situations, we believe learning-based robotics will be key to making truly autonomous home robots a reality. That's where you come in! Your Role As a Machine Learning Engineer – Robotics , you will develop, train, and deploy learning-based models that enable our robots to perform complex manipulation tasks autonomously. You'll work at the intersection of Robot Learning, LLMs, and real-world robotic systems , turning cutting-edge research into capabilities that work reliably on our proprietary physical hardware. Together with our robotics and engineering team, you'll take ownership of the full Robot Learning pipeline – from collecting and preparing training data to experimenting with model architectures, evaluating performance, and deploying policies on our robots. An ideal role for someone who is passionate about cutting-edge AI, enjoys solving challenging technical problems, and wants to see their models do more than generate predictions – actually interact with the physical world. What You'll Do You will initially focus on developing and advancing the skills of our autonomous cooking robot, with the opportunity to expand your work to entirely new categories of home robots as we grow. Your responsibilities will include: Robot Learning & Model Development: Research, implement, train, and improve learning-based models for robotic manipulation, including approaches such as Imitation Learning, Behavior Cloning, Diffusion Policies, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and whatever groundbreaking approaches emerge next. Data Collection & Training Pipelines: Expand and improve workflows for collecting robotic demonstrations, processing multimodal sensor data, and creating high-quality datasets for model training. Model Training & Experimentation: Design, run, and evaluate experiments with modern learning architectures, pre-trained models, and fine-tuning techniques to improve robotic capabilities. Real-World Robot Deployment: Deploy trained policies onto our robotic systems and bring models from the lab to real-world user environments. Evaluation & Performance Optimization: Develop systematic evaluation methods, analyze model failures, and continuously improve the robustness, generalization, and reliability of learned behaviors. Robotic Manipulation: Work on challenging real-world tasks involving object manipulation, tool use, visual perception, and contact-rich interactions. Research & Innovation: Stay close to developments in Physical AI and Robot Learning, evaluate promising research, and translate new approaches into practical improvements to our product together with a hand-selected passionate team. You'll work closely with our interdisciplinary and technical founding team, with substantial freedom to shape our technical approach to Robot Learning. What You Bring We're looking for an engineer with a strong foundation in Machine Learning who enjoys hands-on experimentation, thinks independently, is driven to understand problems from first principles, and is excited about bringing AI into the physical world. Ideally, you bring: A degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Robotics , or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong practical experience in Machine Learning , including training, evaluating, and improving neural network models. Proficient programming skills in Python and practical experience with modern ML frameworks. Familiarity with the full ML development workflow, from dataset preparation and experimentation to model evaluation and deployment. A structured, independent, and first-principles thinking approach to solving complex engineering problems. Curiosity, initiative, and a genuine interest in robotics and Physical …

items.desc: About Teton Teton is building the foundational data layer for the point of care, using real-time, multimodal AI to generate a digital twin of the patient and care environment. Our proprietary computer-vision system enables staff to automate documentation, proactively manage resident acuity, and streamline workflows across entire facilities. Our platform delivers unprecedented access to real-time data insights, empowering healthcare providers with actionable intelligence to enhance decision-making and elevate care delivery. The Role We are looking for an AI Research Scientist / Engineer to accelerate the development of Cassandra, our Generative World Model for healthcare. Cassandra is pretrained on sequences of behavioral tokens representing residents' activities, sleep, mobility, vital signs, and care interactions. By learning to predict what happens next, Cassandra learns patterns of human behavior, enabling applications such as predicting falls before they happen and simulating the potential impact of care interventions. Much like large language models, Cassandra learns from large-scale sequential data and exhibits similar scaling laws. However, modeling human behavior introduces unique research challenges, including continuous-time modeling, long-context dependencies, and learning from heterogeneous behavioral signals. Unlike most foundation models trained on publicly available data, Cassandra learns from a proprietary and continuously growing dataset of real-world human behavior. This creates an opportunity to explore fundamental research questions while building technology with direct real-world impact. We are looking for someone with strong technical intuition and hands-on experience training and scaling large sequence models. You will have the opportunity to take ownership of fundamental research challenges and directly shape both the underlying foundation model and the applications built on top of it. Read more about Cassandra: Introducing Cassandra Key Responsibilities In this role, you will own and drive research and development across two main areas: Pre-training and scaling Cassandra. Improve the end-to-end pre-training pipeline, from behavioral data representation and tokenization to model architecture, training objectives, and scaling. Many techniques from the LLM research toolbox are directly applicable, but important challenges remain, particularly around continuous-time event modeling, irregularly sampled data, and long-term dependencies. You will design experiments, develop new approaches, and translate research into improvements in model capabilities. Developing and productionizing downstream applications. Our first application of Cassandra's learned representations is predicting the risk of a resident falling within the next five minutes. You will improve these predictive capabilities and explore new applications, from forecasting changes in resident behavior to simulating the effects of care interventions. The goal is to turn advances in foundation modeling into tangible improvements in personalized, proactive care. What We're Looking For Minimum Qualifications: Hands-on experience training large-scale sequence models, such as Transformers, state-space models, or LLMs. Deep understanding of neural network architectures, optimization, training dynamics, and scaling laws. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience building efficient, reliable training and evaluation pipelines. Ability to independently design experiments, interpret results, and translate research ideas into working implementations. Solid mathematical foundations in machine learning, probability, and statistics. Mindset: Research-driven and hands-on. You enjoy reading papers, challenging assumptions, and implementing ideas yourself rather than stopping at theoretical insights. Strong technical intuition. You can reason about why a model works, identify bottlenecks, and prioritize experiments that are most likely to move the needle. Ownership and autonomy. You are comfortable tackling open-ended problems, navigating uncertainty, and taking ideas from initial hypothesis to production. Pragmatic and ambitious. You care about advancing the state of the art, but ultimately measure success by whether your work enables capabilities that were previously impossible. Time Zone/location: Based in Copenhagen, Denmark, or willing to relocate. Preferred Qualifications: Research or engineering experience with LLM pre-training, including architecture design, data mixtures, training objectives, or scaling experiments. Experience with generative modeling of sequential, temporal, or event-based data. Familiarity with continuous-time models, point processes, time-to-event prediction, or survival modeling. Experience with long-context architectures, such as Mamba, recurrent models, or efficient attention mechanisms. Experience with distributed training, GPU optimization, and performance profiling. A track record of impactful ML …

items.desc: Your mission As an AI Engineer for Large-Scale Pre-Training, you enter as a key member of the early AI team. You will work directly with our AI leadership and researchers to define the infrastructure we use to train large-scale robot foundation models on petabyte-scale datasets across our GPU fleet. This infrastructure is a critical part of our research and development cycle: it must strike the right balance between stability and velocity, enabling fast research iterations based on reliable results. This is a full-time, permanent position. Your profile Key responsibilities Scalable Training Infrastructure: Develop software infrastructure to train multi-billion-parameter robot foundation models efficiently on large video datasets across multi-node GPU clusters. Data Pipelines: Build high-throughput, reliable data pipelines that stream, decode and preprocess petabyte-scale video datasets, keeping our GPUs fully utilized and supporting deterministic, resumable training. Experiment Management: Build the tools to organize, monitor and optimize large training workloads and model sweeps. Remove bottlenecks in our training pipelines and make sure all our runs maintain the highest possible goodput. Your profile We seek people who embrace the empirical nature of AI research and want to accelerate our research velocity with best-in-class tools - so that we can all make breakthroughs faster, together. Experience : 3+ years of hands-on experience training multi-billion-parameter models on multi-node GPU clusters, including supervising long-running experiments, in-flight debugging and optimizing goodput and MFU. Core Skills : Deep expertise in distributed training and training efficiency at scale. In detail: Distributed Training: Data parallelism and sharding (DDP, FSDP/FSDP2, ZeRO), tensor, pipeline and sequence parallelism, and frameworks such as Megatron-Core, DeepSpeed, TorchTitan or JAX/GSPMD. Training Efficiency : BF16/FP8 mixed precision, activation checkpointing, FlashAttention, and profiling with PyTorch Profiler or Nsight Systems. Fault Tolerance : Distributed and asynchronous checkpointing, automatic recovery, and diagnosing NCCL and hardware failures. Core Stack : Python, PyTorch and/or JAX, CUDA, NCCL, and cluster orchestration with Slurm or Kubernetes. Mindset : You balance the agility of a startup with the professional rigor required for a global industrial player. You are a curious builder who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced research environment, and an engineer with a research mindset who understands the workflows of cutting-edge AI research and supports them with rigorous software engineering. A plus : High-throughput data pipelines for large video datasets (WebDataset, Mosaic Streaming, Ray Data, DALI/NVDEC); custom kernels in Triton or CUDA; familiarity with multimodal or robot foundation models (VLAs, video transformers, diffusion/flow-matching policies); experiment tracking and sweep infrastructure (Weights & Biases, MLflow, Hydra). About us We are building a global leader in physical AI, anchored in Europe’s strongest robotics heritage. Founded by entrepreneurs with backgrounds in scaling digital products and advanced robotics, the team is bolstered by senior leadership from top-tier AI research labs and industrial tech companies. Driven by a mission to create versatile and trustworthy embodied AI for physical labor, We fuse deep engineering mastery in AI and mechatronics with a rapid-execution culture. We are addressing the labor shortage by closing the gap to production-grade deployment. This means building the trusted alternative: robots that are safe, secure, and engineered to automotive standards of scale and durability. Our Locations We have two main locations: Munich, Germany and Limassol, Cyprus. This pan-European setup represents our core ambition of building a European technology leader, gives us a great talent base and a strong corporate structure. We are an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all builders.

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




THE ROLE

Mistral AI is seeking Applied Scientists and Research Engineers focused on tabular data. You will design, train, and deploy SOTA models that understand, query, and reason over structured data, and apply them to diverse use cases.

Working cross-functionally with both external and internal science, engineering, and product teams you will deliver high-impact AI solutions. We are made of researchers, engineers, product builders, ex-founders who love tackling the most complex real world problems in the industry.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Run pre-training, post-training and deploy state of the art models on clusters with thousands of GPUs.

 - Generate and curate datasets of tables, spreadsheets and databases, and build evaluators and benchmarks for table understanding, text-to-SQL, and prediction on tabular data.

 - Develop the necessary tools and frameworks to facilitate data generation, model training, evaluation and deployment.

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to tackle complex use cases.

 - Manage research projects and communications with client research teams.
   
   


ABOUT YOU

 - Fluent in English with excellent communication skills — at ease explaining complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Expert with PyTorch or JAX.

 - Experience training or fine-tuning large language models, or tabular foundation models (e.g. TabPFN).

 - Strong background in machine learning on tabular data, including classical baselines (e.g. gradient boosting), and comfortable with SQL, pandas, and messy real-world data.

 - Not afraid of contributing to a big codebase; finds their way around independently with little guidance.

 - Writes clean, readable, high-performance, fault-tolerant Python code.

 - Doesn’t need roadmaps: moves independently and navigates uncertainty with confidence.

 - Low-ego, collaborative and eager to learn.

 - Track record of success through personal projects, professional projects or academia.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Ex-founder or builder

 - PhD / Master in a relevant field (Computer Science, Statistics, Machine Learning) — exceptional candidates from other backgrounds welcome.

 - Experience with text-to-SQL, table question answering, or spreadsheet agents.

 - Experience with reinforcement learning using verifiable rewards (e.g. query execution).

 - Experience working on large code bases or large machine learning models at scale.

 - Contributions to a large open-source or industry codebase.

 - Publications in top academic journals or conferences.

 - Enjoys improving existing code: typing, tests, CI pipelines.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.desc: Labhouse is a Barcelona-based startup studio building AI-powered mobile apps used by hundreds of thousands of people worldwide. Our products — including Invoice Fly and Summary AI — are designed to make everyday tasks faster, smarter, and simpler through a subscription model that puts the user first. We were founded by Andrés Bou and Horacio Martos , the duo behind SocialPoint (acquired by Take-Two Interactive), and we operate with the mindset of a product company: small teams, high ownership, and a relentless focus on building things that matter. Would you like to make an impact as part of a company that builds the best mobile apps used by millions of users worldwide? If so, discover your next challenge below. The Role At Labhouse, AI is not a feature — it's the core of what we build. As our AI Engineer, you will own the development, fine-tuning, and productionization of the models that make our apps work at a high level of accuracy and performance. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will: Research, design, and train models suited to the specific needs of our products Fine-tune existing open-source and foundation models to maximize accuracy and performance Own the full model lifecycle: data curation, experimentation, evaluation, and production deployment Collaborate with mobile and backend engineers to integrate models directly into our apps Define and track the metrics that drive quality — and continuously push them in the right direction About You Academic Background A strong academic foundation matters to us. We're looking for candidates with a degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field. A Master's or PhD in machine learning or a related area is a strong plus — but not a requirement if you can demonstrate equivalent depth through your work. What we are looking for More than years of experience, we care about demonstrated ability to build. You should be able to point to models you've trained, fine-tuned, or shipped — whether in a professional setting, a research context, or on your own. A strong GitHub and/or Hugging Face profile is a significant advantage. Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning deep learning models that are used in production. Strong Python skills and experience with ML frameworks (PyTorch or JAX preferred) Comfort with the full model development cycle: data pipelines, experiment tracking, evaluation, deployment and scaling. Solid understanding of modern model architectures and when to apply them Experience with the Hugging Face ecosystem (Transformers, Datasets, Hub) is a strong plus Ability to work autonomously, make decisions under uncertainty, and ship without waiting for perfect conditions AI Proficiency You actively use AI tools in your own workflow — not as a novelty, but as a genuine productivity multiplier. You stay current with the state of the art and know how to apply the latest research to real product problems. Communication You communicate clearly and directly. You can explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders, flag blockers early, and collaborate effectively in a small, fast-moving team. Nice to Have Experience across multiple model domains (vision, audio, NLP, multimodal) Familiarity with on-device or edge inference optimization (quantization, distillation, ONNX) Experience integrating ML models into mobile or production environments Published research or open-source contributions in ML What we offer Attractive compensation, above market average Hybrid work model based in Barcelona High ownership from day one — you define the direction, not just execute on it Work directly with the founders and a senior, low-ego team A real product with real users — your work will have immediate, measurable impact Hiring Process Initial Interview: Meet with our Talent Acquisition Lead to discuss your background and fit for the role. We’ll also ask you to share your proudest projects. Hiring Manager Interview: A deep dive into your experience and leadership capabilities. Technical Assessment: Showcase your expertise through a practical task. Final Interview: A conversation with our leadership team to align on vision and expectations. Offer: Join our team and lead the development of our future-shaping apps! You should Know: Labhouse is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. However you identify or whatever your journey to this point, we welcome all candidates to apply for the position that inspires them. Come join us and help us build a company that everyone is proud to be part of.

items.title: sEMG / Biosignal ML Scientist
items.card: The role We are looking for a scientist to develop methods for decoding high-density surface EMG (HD-sEMG) into continuous measures of human movement, force and motor intent. A central research question is how much information about forthcoming movement and mechanical output can be extracted from neuromuscular activity before observable movement occurs. You will investigate this temporal relationship experimentally
items.desc: About REVEL REVEL is an AI robotics company developing physical intelligence for general-purpose humanoid robots. We capture the force, dexterity and intent of human work with our Neural Gambit wearable, and use it to train RAI, the intelligence that powers our robots. Our R&D and engineering facilities are in Prague, Czech Republic. This role is on-site with our team in Prague. The intent layer is REVEL's core differentiator: reading neuromuscular signals 30 to 100 ms before motion. We're looking for a scientist to decode high-density surface EMG into force and intent. The role We are looking for a scientist to develop methods for decoding high-density surface EMG (HD-sEMG) into continuous measures of human movement, force and motor intent. A central research question is how much information about forthcoming movement and mechanical output can be extracted from neuromuscular activity before observable movement occurs. You will investigate this temporal relationship experimentally and develop models that can exploit it under realistic conditions. This is a highly experimental role. You will work with real human data, noisy physiological signals, wearable hardware and evolving data-collection protocols, while translating scientific findings into models that can ultimately support robotic intelligence. Responsibilities 3+ years of relevant professional experience Develop signal-processing and machine-learning methods for decoding HD-sEMG into continuous force, joint kinematics and motor intent. Characterise the temporal relationship between neuromuscular activity and mechanical movement, including the potential 30 to 100 ms anticipatory window. Design experiments to quantify the reliability, information content and limits of anticipatory information in sEMG. Develop preprocessing and signal-quality methods for multi-channel EMG, including filtering, artefact handling, normalization and channel-quality assessment. Investigate the effects of sensor placement, electrode contact, motion artefacts, fatigue, physiological variability and session-to-session drift. Evaluate model robustness across operators/subjects, sessions, movements and sensor configurations. Develop methods for cross-operator, cross-session and cross-condition generalisation, including efficient calibration where necessary. Design capture and labelling protocols together with the data-collection team. Define data-quality criteria and experimental metrics that enable reliable downstream ML. Collaborate closely with the robotics ML team to translate biosignal representations and decoded intent into inputs suitable for RAI. Prototype and evaluate models in real-time or near-real-time settings where appropriate. Communicate experimental results clearly and use them to guide the next iteration of the sensing, modelling and data-collection system. Requirements 3+ years of relevant professional experience Hands-on experience with EMG or electrophysiological biosignals, including signal acquisition, preprocessing and quantitative analysis. Strong understanding of signal processing for noisy, non-stationary physiological signals. Experience developing machine-learning models for time-series or sequential data. Strong Python skills and practical experience with PyTorch or JAX. Experience designing, executing and analysing controlled experiments. Ability to reason quantitatively about temporal alignment, latency, prediction, signal quality and model generalisation. Experience working with real-world biological data where signal characteristics vary across people and sessions. Strong scientific judgement and the ability to distinguish genuine physiological information from artefacts, leakage and experimental confounds. Bonus Qualifications PhD or equivalent research experience in biomedical engineering, neuroscience, electrical engineering, biomechanics, computer science, machine learning or a related field; alternatively, an MSc with 2 to 3+ years of highly relevant research or industry experience. Experience with high-density sEMG / electrode arrays. Experience with multi-channel EMG decomposition, motor-unit activity or neuromuscular physiology. Experience decoding force, torque, joint kinematics or motor intention from biosignals. Background in motor control, biomechanics or human movement science. Experience with wearable sensing and human-subject experiments. Experience with domain adaptation, calibration or cross-subject generalisation. Familiarity with real-time inference and latency constraints. Experience deploying ML models outside purely offline research environments. Why REVEL Work That Ships: We capture how skilled humans work, their force, touch, and judgment, and our robots do the work. You put robots on a paying customer's floor, not in a demo loop The Team: Colleagues from NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Neura Robotics, and founders you work with directly. No layers, no process between you and the decisions Your Own Hardware: A top-spec GPU …

Then you will get those models running on the robot. Every
items.desc: About REVEL REVEL is an AI robotics company developing physical intelligence for general-purpose humanoid robots. We capture the force, dexterity and intent of human work with our Neural Gambit wearable, and use it to train RAI, the intelligence that powers our robots. Our R&D and engineering facilities are in Prague, Czech Republic. This role is on-site with our team in Prague. The role We are looking for an experienced computer vision engineer to build the perception that lets our humanoid robot, GENESIS, see and understand its workspace in real time. You will turn REVEL's recordings of skilled human work, captured with several cameras and the Neural Gambit wearable, into models that track hands, tools, and objects in 3D. Then you will get those models running on the robot. Every manipulation skill the robot learns depends on seeing hands, tools, and objects accurately. Perception errors show up as failed grasps on a customer's floor. You will join a small Perception team in Prague and work closely with our Robot Learning and Data Collection teams. Most of the team is early in their careers, so you will help set how we build, evaluate, and ship models, and support the junior engineers along the way. What You'll Do Build hand, tool and object tracking in 3D from our multi-camera and wearable recordings of people doing manual work. Develop detection, segmentation, pose estimation and 3D scene understanding for the robot's manipulation skills. Calibrate and synchronise multi-camera and depth setups in the lab and on the robot, and keep them accurate over time. Build training and evaluation pipelines that anyone on the team can rerun months later: data, labelling, dataset versioning and experiment tracking. Design evaluations around what the robot needs, not only benchmark scores, and find out why a model fails on real data. Get models running in real time on the robot's onboard GPU (ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation or similar). Work with Robot Learning and Data Collection on what to record and what perception the next skill needs. Help set engineering standards in a small, young team. Who We're Looking For 3+ years of hands-on computer vision work in industry or research, with models you trained yourself running on real camera data, not only on benchmarks. Strong Python and PyTorch. Solid Linear Algebra and 3D Computer Vision fundamentals. Deep-learning fundamentals for vision (detection, segmentation, pose estimation or 3D vision) and rigorous evaluation. Experience with real cameras and real-world data: calibration, multi-camera setups, noise, lighting and latency. items.desc:
About us
 Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence
PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.
 The role
 You will own the product capability that lets PhysicsX and its customers improve LLMs for their specific work.
 You will be a hands-on product ML engineer embedded deeply with our Research group and accountable for turning post-training methods into something customers can use. The first goal is to make open models perform strongly on the evals and benchmarks that matter to us. The longer-term goal is a repeatable platform capability through which customers can train models on their own workflows keeping their data, learned behaviour and intellectual property under their control.
 The remit is broader than supervised fine-tuning. You will choose and apply the right post-training methods, including preference optimisation, reinforcement learning, distillation, synthetic data and verifier-based approaches. You will own the capability roadmap and production outcome; Research will be a close partner in developing methods, and platform product teams will be partners in integrating the experience.
 What you will do
 Own the path from a base model and customer workflow to a measured, deployable model improvement.
 Build reliable post-training harnesses covering data preparation, training, evaluation, model artifacts and hand-off to serving.
 Improve open models against PhysicsX's agent and engineering benchmarks, using evidence to decide whether training is better than changes to prompts, tools or the agent design.
 Develop and operate methods spanning SFT, preference optimisation, RLHF/RLAIF, RL with verifiable rewards, distillation, rejection sampling and related techniques.
 Build reproducible synthetic-data and expert-data pipelines, including quality filtering, provenance, licensing and contamination controls.
 Design reward signals, verifiers and rollout workflows while detecting reward hacking, benchmark overfitting, model collapse and unintended regressions.
 Make post-training available through a mix of managed workflows and expert-facing interfaces.
 Ensure customer data and resulting model artifacts can remain within the customer's platform environment across SaaS, VPC and air-gapped deployments.
 Work on cross-product and public benchmarks. Own experiment diagnostics with Research, with shared approval where results support product or external claims.
 Work with the LLM Self-Hosting & Model Routing Lead to move trained models into supported production serving and routing.
 Set the product roadmap for model improvement, balancing research opportunity with customer value, operability and time to production.
 Help determine how this capability should grow and, over time, shape the team around it.
 What you bring
 Where you need to be strongest
 You have measurably improved model behaviour through post-training and turned that work into a capability used in production.
 You are deeply hands-on across data, training, evaluation and debugging; you can take an experiment from hypothesis to deployed artifact.
 You understand modern post-training methods well enough to choose among them based on the task and evidence rather than fashion.
 You have built high-quality training datasets from expert, behavioural or synthetic sources and understand that data design is part of model design.
 You can diagnose training and behavioural failures, including instability, drift, reward exploitation, leakage and overfitting to evals.
 You are product-minded: you start from a user workflow, define success, make trade-offs and build an experience others can operate.
 You can work as the accountable product owner of a technical capability while collaborating closely with research scientists, platform engineers and product teams.
 Foundations
 Strong Python and PyTorch or equivalent model-training frameworks.
 Distributed training, accelerator utilisation, checkpointing, recovery, experiment tracking and reproducibility.
 Evaluation of model and agent behaviour, including controlled experiments and ablations.
 Data governance, privacy, provenance and safe handling of customer-owned training data and artifacts.
 Model packaging and the operational path from training to evaluation and production serving.
 Clear technical writing and communication across research, product, engineering, delivery and …

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




THE ROLE

Mistral AI is seeking Applied Scientists and Research Engineers focused on optimisation and operational research. You will post-train SOTA large language models to formulate and solve optimisation problems, and apply them to diverse use cases.

Working cross-functionally with both external and internal science, engineering, and product teams you will deliver high-impact AI solutions. We are made of researchers, engineers, product builders, ex-founders who love tackling the most complex real world problems in the industry.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Run pre-training, post-training and deploy state of the art models on clusters with thousands of GPUs.

 - Generate and curate datasets for optimisation modelling (LP, MILP, constraint programming, scheduling, routing), and build evaluators and benchmarks for operational research tasks.

 - Use solvers as verifiers to build reward signals for reinforcement learning.

 - Develop the necessary tools and frameworks to facilitate data generation, model training, evaluation and deployment.

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to tackle complex use cases.

 - Manage research projects and communications with client research teams.




ABOUT YOU

 - Fluent in English with excellent communication skills — at ease explaining complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Expert with PyTorch or JAX.

 - Experience training or fine-tuning large language models for reasoning, code, or mathematics.

 - Strong background in operational research or mathematical optimisation, with hands-on experience using solvers (e.g. Gurobi, CPLEX, OR-Tools) and modelling languages (e.g. Pyomo, AMPL).

 - Not afraid of contributing to a big codebase; finds their way around independently with little guidance.

 - Writes clean, readable, high-performance, fault-tolerant Python code.

 - Doesn’t need roadmaps: moves independently and navigates uncertainty with confidence.

 - Low-ego, collaborative and eager to learn.

 - Track record of success through personal projects, professional projects or academia.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Ex-founder or builder

 - PhD / Master in a relevant field (Operational Research, Applied Mathematics, Machine Learning) — exceptional candidates from other backgrounds welcome.

 - Experience with reinforcement learning using verifiable rewards.

 - Experience with LLM-based optimisation modelling (e.g. NL4Opt-style problem formulation).

 - Industry experience in supply chain, logistics, energy, or scheduling.

 - Experience working on large code bases or large machine learning models at scale.

 - Contributions to a large open-source or industry codebase.

 - Publications in top academic journals or conferences.

 - Enjoys improving existing code: typing, tests, CI pipelines.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

You will work directly with our AI leadership and researchers to define the infrastructure we use to post-train our robot foundation models with large-scale reinforcement learning and deploy them as agentic systems across our robot fleet. You own the full loop - from distributed rollouts in simulation and on real robots, through policy optimization, to serving our models on cloud and on-prem infrastructure. The systems you build close the gap between research and deployment, turning real-world experience into better models, fast and safely. This is a full-time, permanent position. Key responsibilities Distributed RL Infrastructure: Develop scalable infrastructure for RL post-training of multi-billion-parameter robot foundation models, coordinating distributed actors, learners and reward models across GPU clusters, simulation and our robot fleet Model Serving: Own our cloud and on-prem serving infrastructure, delivering low-latency, high-throughput inference for both RL rollouts and production robots, including fast weight synchronization between training and inference. Agentic Workflows: Build the infrastructure to orchestrate, evaluate and monitor agentic systems that combine our models with planning, tool use and robot skills to complete long-horizon tasks. Your profile We seek people who embrace the empirical nature of AI research and want to accelerate our research velocity with best-in-class tools - so that we can all make breakthroughs faster, together. Experience : 3+ years of hands-on experience building and operating large-scale RL or post-training systems for large models, including actor-learner architectures, asynchronous rollouts and off-policy correction. Core Skills : Deep expertise in RL post-training and high-performance model serving. In detail: RL Post-Training : PPO, GRPO and related policy-optimization algorithms, reward modeling, and frameworks such as veRL, OpenRLHF, NeMo-RL, TRL or Ray RLlib. Model Serving : Inference engines such as vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM, batching and KV-cache optimization, quantization, and serving platforms such as Ray Serve, Triton Inference Server or KServe. Distributed Systems : Ray, Kubernetes and/or Slurm, fault-tolerant orchestration of heterogeneous workloads, and monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana. Core Stack: Python, PyTorch and/or JAX, CUDA, NCCL, and distributed training with FSDP or Megatron-Core. Mindset : You balance the agility of a startup with the professional rigor required for a global industrial player. You are a curious builder who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced research environment, and an engineer with a research mindset who understands the workflows of cutting-edge AI research and supports them with rigorous software engineering. A plus : Building agentic systems and evaluation harnesses for long-horizon, multi-step tasks; robot learning in simulation and sim-to-real transfer (Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, domain randomization); edge and on-robot inference (NVIDIA Jetson/Orin/Thor, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime) under real-time latency constraints; robotics middleware and data formats (ROS 2, MCAP) Why us? The Team: Work alongside leadership with a proven track record of building unicorn-scale companies and defining global robotics standards. Smart Strategy: We operate as disciplined fast followers. Capital is timed to the deployment inflection point, avoiding early-mover dead ends to scale fast on proven foundations. Resources: We are substantially internally funded and attract top-tier investors to avoid any capital constraints for our mission. Historic Opportunity: Join at the dawn of a new industry comparable to the rise of the automobile. Help shape the European champion in this trillion-dollar market. About us We are building a global leader in physical AI, anchored in Europe’s strongest robotics heritage. Founded by entrepreneurs with backgrounds in scaling digital products and advanced robotics, the team is bolstered by senior leadership from top-tier AI research labs and industrial tech companies. Driven by a mission to create versatile and trustworthy embodied AI for physical labor, We fuse deep engineering mastery in AI and mechatronics with a rapid-execution culture. We are addressing the labor shortage by closing the gap to production-grade deployment. This means building the trusted alternative: robots that are safe, secure, and engineered to automotive standards of scale and durability. Our Locations We have two main locations: Munich, Germany and Limassol, Cyprus. This pan-European setup represents our core ambition of building a European technology leader, gives us a great talent base and a strong corporate structure. We are an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all builders.

items.desc:
Join our Team
 About this opportunity 
 The AI Accelerator within BNEW SAN is on a mission to innovate, incubate, and deliver AI-based solutions that fundamentally redesign Customer Support and Network Deployment — shifting from human-led coordination to composable, agent-centric intelligence. We aim to move beyond simple efficiency gains to create a compounding cycle of optimization, where every interaction generates actionable insights that continuously refine operations, reduce time-to-market, and accelerate the journey toward autonomous network operations.
 We are looking for an LLM Post-Training Engineer to own the process of making foundation models genuinely useful in our domain. Pretrained LLMs are powerful starting points — but it is post-training that transforms a general-purpose model into a reliable, domain-aligned agent capable of operating autonomously in the complex world of telecommunications. You will design and execute the training strategies, reward frameworks, and data pipelines that shape how our models reason, respond, and improve — closing the gap between what a model knows out of the box and what our agents need to do in production.
 What you will do: 
 Domain Knowledge Injection via Fine-Tuning 
 Design and execute supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pipelines that inject domain-specific knowledge into base LLMs across Customer Support and Network Deployment contexts
 Apply parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques — including LoRA, QLoRA, and adapter-based methods — to adapt large models effectively within compute and latency constraints
 Collaborate with the AI & Domain Specialist and AI Data & Integration Engineer to ensure fine-tuning datasets are high quality, domain-representative, and correctly formatted for training objectives
 Maintain a structured catalog of fine-tuned model variants, adapter checkpoints, and associated training configurations to support reproducibility and lifecycle governance
 Policy-Reward Training & Alignment 
 Design and implement policy-reward training pipelines using advanced optimization methods including GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) and SAPO (Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization)
 Define reward models and preference datasets that encode domain-specific quality signals — going beyond generic helpfulness to capture what correct, safe, and operationally appropriate behavior looks like in telco contexts
 Iterate on alignment strategies based on evaluation feedback and production signal — continuously refining model behavior to better match system requirements and domain acceptance criteria
 Stay current with the rapidly evolving post-training research landscape, identifying and assessing new alignment techniques for potential adoption
 Automatic Dataset Curation & Synthetic Data Generation 
 Build and maintain automated pipelines for domain dataset curation — sourcing, filtering, deduplicating, and formatting data at scale for both SFT and reward training
 Design synthetic data generation strategies that augment real-world datasets — producing diverse, high-quality training examples for scenarios where real data is scarce, sensitive, or imbalanced
 Collaborate with domain experts to validate synthetic data quality and ensure generated examples accurately reflect real-world telco operational scenarios
 Implement data quality gates and automated checks that maintain dataset integrity throughout the curation and generation pipeline
 Training Run Management & Experiment Tracking 
 Own the end-to-end management of training runs — including infrastructure provisioning, job scheduling, hyperparameter configuration, and run monitoring
 Maintain a rigorous experiment tracking practice, logging all training configurations, dataset versions, evaluation results, and model artifacts to ensure full reproducibility and informed decision-making
 Define and report on key training metrics — loss curves, reward signal trends, evaluation benchmark scores, and alignment quality indicators — providing clear visibility to the AI System Architect and engineering leadership
 Identify and resolve training instabilities, overfitting risks, and performance bottlenecks across the post-training pipeline
 You will bring: 
 Proven hands-on experience in LLM fine-tuning and post-training, with a track record of adapting large language models for production use cases using SFT, LoRA, or equivalent techniques
 Strong understanding of RLHF, preference optimization, and policy-reward training methods — direct experience with GRPO, DPO, PPO, or similar approaches is highly valued
 Experience building automated data curation and synthetic data generation pipelines for LLM training at scale
 Solid grasp of experiment tracking best practices and tooling — able to maintain a disciplined, reproducible training workflow across multiple concurrent experiments
 Familiarity with distributed training infrastructure, GPU resource management, and compute-efficient training strategies
 …

items.desc: Who we are At Praxa Sense, we are redefining non-invasive health monitoring with our optical innovation ALIS® – a speckle-based biosensor enabling new frontiers in remote vital sign tracking. We are looking for a curious, creative and very sharp Research Scientist who wants to fully understand what the ALIS® sensor measures, from the physics of laser speckle and tissue optics to the underlying physiology. You combine deep understanding with hands-on work: you set up measurements yourself, tinker and explore with the technology, explain what you see, and turn new insights into strong intellectual property. What you will do Deepen our understanding of the physics behind SPG and the Blood Flow Index (BFi): speckle statistics, speckle dynamics, light-tissue interaction and their relation to blood flow. Link the BFi and PPG signals to physiology: microvascular and arterial blood flow, perfusion, and pulse wave characteristics. Design and run experiments with the sensor, on the bench and in-vivo, often against reference methods such as ECG, ultrasound or blood pressure measurements. Analyze the data and explain the observed physical and physiological effects. Develop theoretical and numerical models that link measured signals to physiological parameters. Guide the next steps in IP protection: identify patentable inventions, write invention disclosures and draft patent descriptions and claims together with our patent attorney. Carry out prior-art searches and support freedom-to-operate analyses. What we are looking for Msc or PhD in Physics, Applied Physics, Physical Chemistry or Biomedical Engineering, with a background in photonics, optoelectronics, light-matter interaction or biomedical optics. Experience with speckle, DCS, LSCI or PPG is a strong plus, but not required. Experience translating research into applied health sensing, for example as a research engineer at a medtech or consumer health company. Strong understanding of coherent light scattering and tissue optics, or the ability to master these quickly. Solid knowledge of human physiology, in particular cardiovascular physiology and hemodynamics. Hands-on experimental skills. Data analysis and modelling skills in Python. Demonstrable interest in intellectual property, ideally with experience in invention disclosures or patent texts. Ability to write clear, precise technical text and to separate what is truly novel from what is known. Fluent in English; Dutch is a plus. What we offer Salary matching your experience with potential equity participation. 25 holiday days per year, additional special leave days for big life events such as weddings, moving houses and funerals. 7% of your salary as a contribution to life annuity. Free office lunch on Fridays. Fun company outings, but no unnecessary obligations. If you live more than 5km from the office: travel cost reimbursement of €0,23 per kilometer, also (or especially) when you come by bike. Work-from-home reimbursement so you can also drink quality coffee at home. Hybrid work culture: in-person collaboration at the Groot Handelsgebouw in Rotterdam at least 3 days/week, work from home when you need to focus (or do some laundry). Direct collaboration with experts in optics, signal processing, and data science and very friendly and ambitious colleagues. The satisfaction of contributing to technology that directly improves health monitoring. To apply: Send your CV and motivation to hr@praxasense.com. Submissions without a motivational letter will result in automatic rejection. Join the Computational Music Technologies team, where we build the audio intelligence behind some of Apple’s most distinctive listening experiences. We shipped AutoMix, intelligent DJ-style transitions between tracks, and the Music Understanding Framework, our on-device audio feature extraction system. We’re now building the next generation of generative audio technology, including the foundational models that will underpin a range of new experiences for music lovers and creators across Apple.
Music is our passion, and so is doing the research right: rigorous evaluation, careful attention to artist and listener trust, and a bias toward shipping. Our team sits close to partners in research and engineering across Apple, and we’re given the resources and access to large GPU clusters to enable us to pursue ambitious, foundational work.
As a Machine Learning Researcher on the team, you’ll conduct research in generative audio using diffusion or flow-matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas: voice generation, researching vocal and speech synthesis alongside related audio and signal processing techniques; post-training and alignment techniques to improve output quality, controllability, and adherence to human preference; and realtime generation, developing architectures and distillation methods that bring generation latency down to the point where it can run live, including few-step and streaming approaches.
Alongside this, you’ll help build the foundations that everything above depends on: evaluation methodology, benchmarking against the state of the art, and questions of attribution. You’ll run experiments at scale on our own infrastructure, work closely with engineering, product, and design partners to turn research into real listening experiences, and stay connected to the broader research community.
Is this you? If so, we’d love to hear from you.

Industry experience of coding in Python and PyTorch or JAX
Excellent communication and presentation skills
Deep expertise in one of the following areas: audio generation and editing, post-training of diffusion models, voice synthesis

Love of music

Deine Themen sind Endeffektoren und Werkzeugwechsler, Auswahl und Montage von Sensoren, Kalibrierung, elektrische und Feldbus-Schnittstellen sowie die mechanische Realität der Zelle. Customer Enablement & Support: Du begleitest Nutzer beim Onboarding auf NeuraGym. Du prüfst Trainingspipelines und Skripte, erkennst Probleme in der Datenqualität, analysierst das Modellverhalten und löst hartnäckige Blocker direkt vor Ort. Bereichsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit: Du bist eine zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen dem Cloud- und dem AI-Team. Du sorgst für reibungslose Zusammenarbeit, technische Abstimmung und effiziente Problemlösung über Fachgrenzen hinweg. Evaluation & Zuverlässigkeit: Du baust Eval-Harnesses, Success-Rate-Benchmarks und Regressionstests auf. Sie entscheiden, ob eine Policy bereit für die Übergabe ist, und machen Fehlerbilder sichtbar, bevor der Kunde sie entdeckt. Feedback-Schleife für Produkt & Forschung: Du übersetzt Erfahrungen aus dem Feld und Kundeneinblicke in konkretes Feedback für die NeuraGym-Produkt-Roadmap und die NEURA Core-AI-Roadmap. Was du mitbringst Master oder Promotion in Informatik, Robotik, Elektrotechnik oder einem vergleichbaren Fach. Praktische Machine-Learning-Erfahrung in der Robotik: Du bist stark in mindestens einem der Bereiche vision-basierte Manipulation, Reinforcement/Imitation Learning oder multimodale Modelle und hast Lust, dir den Rest anzueignen. Nachweisbare Erfahrung im Fine-Tuning großer vortrainierter Modelle für Robotik oder eine andere Domäne: PEFT/LoRA und Full Fine-Tunes, Datensatz-Kuratierung, Distillation und Evaluation. Kenntnisse im offenen VLA- und Policy-Learning-Ökosystem (z. B. π0/π0.5, OpenVLA, LeRobot, Diffusion Policies) sind ein großes Plus. Sehr gute Python-Kenntnisse (C++ von Vorteil) und praktische Erfahrung mit PyTorch oder TensorFlow. Nachweisbare Erfahrung in technischen Rollen mit Kundenkontakt (z. B. Solution Engineering, Field AI Engineering, technische Beratung), auch mit mehreren Kunden parallel. Fundiertes Verständnis von Roboter-Hardware: Antriebe und Gelenkmodule, Drehmomentsensorik und Encoder, Endeffektoren, Sensorintegration, Kalibrierung, elektrische und Feldbus-Schnittstellen (z. B. EtherCAT) sowie Konzepte der funktionalen Sicherheit. Vor Ort kannst du damit ein Modellproblem von einem Maschinenproblem unterscheiden. Ausgeprägte Problemlösungskompetenz, die Fähigkeit, mehrere Projekte parallel zu steuern, sowie ein starker Umsetzungswille und hohes persönliches Engagement. Du nimmst Deployments persönlich, lässt dich von Rückschlägen nicht aufhalten und misst dich daran, was beim Kunden läuft. Du kommunizierst klar und übersetzt zwischen Forschenden, Ingenieurinnen und Ingenieuren sowie Endanwendern. Du sprichst gut Englisch und Deutsch (Niveau B2–C1). Bereitschaft zu häufigen Reisen zu Kunden und NeuraGyms (ca. 40–60 %).

Our first supercomputer, Sferical One, is built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD architecture. We’re looking for an experienced LLM training specialist to customize large language models for our partners’ engineering and technical use cases. You’ll join a team whose mission is to drive Sferical AI’s success through workload leadership, helping our customers reach their goals for sovereignty and competitiveness with AI. You’ll also help build Sferical AI into a company that embodies the opportunity AI presents, running on a modern technology platform that integrates our own AI capability, both in our technical mission and in our thought leadership within the Wallenberg sphere. As a Member of Technical Staff, you are: a recognized peer in a highly skilled group with collective responsibility for our platform. expected to contribute across the platform design cycle, from strategy and architecture to design, validation and support, and across every part of the platform where you have experience, from hardware and installation to compute, storage, orchestration and security. expected to take particular ownership of the areas where your expertise is strongest, which for this role means model training and customization. invested in our customers’ success, contributing to integration and troubleshooting, and occasionally acting as lead or single point of contact toward a customer or partner. encouraged to contribute in all areas together with your peers, without being expected to act autonomously in all of them. free to step outside narrow role descriptions such as developer, data scientist or architect, and to grow your skills in line with our customer commitments and the team’s day-to-day work. responsible for producing work your peers can build on, with clear design, architectural consistency, good documentation and solid workmanship. expected to lead by example, speak up and help keep the team psychologically safe. What you’ll own as our Model Training specialist customizing LLMs for engineering and technical tasks that fall outside their original training distribution. training through continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RLVR and RLHF). the data engineering behind this work, on a cloud platform. end-to-end pipelines, from data and training through to inference and evaluation. working closely with use cases and initiatives across our partner companies. What you bring extensive experience customizing LLMs for out-of-distribution engineering or technical task sets. hands-on experience with continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning (RLVR and RLHF). experience with data engineering for model training on a cloud platform. experience building end-to-end pipelines, including inference and evals. experience with the NVIDIA stack, such as Megatron-based frameworks and Nemotron models. fluency in English; Swedish is a strong plus. Swedish citizenship is mandatory. This role is based at our Stockholm office, five days a week. We build best together, and we believe working side by side drives better results.

items.desc:
Who we are
 Helsing is a defence AI company with the mission is to protect our liberal democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. We believe we have a responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI and take this responsibility seriously. 
 We are an ambitious and committed team of software and deployment engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems today.
 We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. 
 The role
 At Helsing you will work at the intersection of machine learning and signal processing on RF data, helping build the AI capabilities inside our electronic warfare systems: models that detect, classify, and reason about RF signals in congested, contested spectrum. The data is messy, irregular, and adversarial. Output runs on real platforms, under hard latency and compute budgets. What you build has to survive contact with the deployment target.
 You will own problems end-to-end: read the literature, prototype on real recorded data, push to the edge, watch it run. You will work in a small research team alongside RF and hardware engineers and the operators using the system.
 Current focus areas include self-supervised representation learning on signal data, deinterleaving and emitter identification, mode recognition, and anomaly detection on embedded hardware.
 You should apply if you
 Hold a PhD (or have an equivalent research track record) in ML, signal processing, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field, with publications at NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICASSP, or similar venues.
 Have shipped non-trivial ML into a real product - not just notebooks. You know what breaks between research and deployment.
 Are comfortable on irregular, noisy sequence data: temporal models, self-supervised or contrastive methods, calibration under distribution shift.
 Write clean Python, and are willing to pick up Rust where the deployment target demands it.
 Read papers and reimplement them. You can tell which results will hold up and which won't.
 Communicate research clearly to ML peers, RF engineers, and end users.
 We don't expect you to arrive with deep RF expertise. A strong ML or physics background and willingness to learn the domain alongside RF colleagues is enough.
 Note: We operate at an intersection where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. 
 Nice to have 
 Experience with EW, SIGINT, ESM/ELINT, RWR, or radar concepts.
 Familiarity with RF signal theory at a level sufficient to talk to RF engineers (modulation, propagation, antenna patterns — see modulation-schemes).
 Experience deploying ML to edge or embedded hardware (ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation, profiling on constrained GPUs).
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world
 Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward
 In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts
 We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. Teams and individual engineers are trusted (and encouraged) to practise responsible autonomy and critical thinking, and to focus on outcomes, not conformity. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about
 What we offer
 Competitive salary and VSOP options 
 Relocation support : up to €2,500 and 4 …

items.desc: At NXAI, we are building the future of AI from our hub in Linz, Austria. Our mission is to turn advanced research into real-world impact, with a focus on next-generation xLSTM models and their industrial applications. Working at the intersection of research and industry, we are creating a leading center for AI innovation in the region. As a Robotics Research Engineer at NXAI, you will take our next-generation sequence models out of the lab and into the physical world. You will work at the intersection of foundation model research and embodied AI, building the perception, reasoning and action pipelines that let robots understand instructions, interpret their environment and act reliably in real world settings. This is a hands-on research role: you will be as comfortable fine-tuning a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model as you are debugging a policy on real hardware. You will work closely with our core research team to explore how xLSTM can push robotic foundation models beyond today's state of the art. Key Responsibilities Own physical robot and workstation uptime, including the integration of new sensors, compute units, and end-effectors, while iteratively modifying setups to improve experimental throughput. Architect and maintain fault-tolerant, high-throughput pipelines for multi-modal data ingestion, incorporating automated data validation, quality scoring, and versioning. Establish standardized, reproducible real-world evaluation protocols and metrics (success rate, task completion time, out-of-distribution robustness) to systematically benchmark policy progression. Conduct end-to-end root-cause analysis across the entire robotics stack, diagnosing bottlenecks spanning physical sensors, actuators, network/communication overhead, inference runtimes, and training distribution shift. Serve as the critical feedback loop between physical deployment and algorithm design, turning empirical hardware failures and edge cases into actionable research directions and data strategy updates. Fine-tune, optimize, and deploy modern learning-based policies (e.g., imitation learning, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models) into real-time, low-latency control loops on physical hardware. What We Ask 2+ years of industry experience training and deploying robot learning models, or an MSc/PhD with research focused on policy learning. Demonstrated track record of deploying and debugging neural network policies on physical robots (manipulators, mobile bases, or humanoids), including managing safety constraints and hardware/sensor calibration. Advanced proficiency in Python and PyTorch.. Practical proficiency with Linux environments, modern robotics communication middleware (ROS 1/2), and containerization tools (Docker, Singularity). Strong foundational understanding of imitation learning paradigms (e.g., Behavior Cloning, Action Chunking with Transformers [ACT], Diffusion Policy) and dataset curation strategies. Discipline in designing reproducible physical benchmarking protocols (success metrics, failure categorization, out-of-distribution testing). Skills That Will Differentiate You: Hands-on work with VLA models or robot foundation models Experience with industrial manipulators or mobile robots in production-like settings Sim-to-real transfer and synthetic data generation (e.g. Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) Experience with linear model, such as state-space models, RNNs, or xLSTM Publications at robotics or ML venues (ICRA, CoRL, RSS, NeurIPS, ICLR) or open-source contributions Success Metrics Physical setups maintain high operational uptime with minimal experimental downtime. Hardware capabilities (sensing, tooling, compute, and mounting) continuously evolve to directly eliminate data-collection bottlenecks and unlock new research investigations. Data collection: a new operator can collect a usable dataset on a robot within a day, with documented setup, synced cameras and joints, and only a small share of episodes discarded for quality issues. Evaluation and baselines: a written eval protocol with a fixed number of trials per task (e.g., 20+), plus success rates reported for a baseline policy and a VLA fine-tune, reproducible when rerun. Benchmark: a defined set of tasks (e.g., 3–5) with baseline numbers for each, used by the team to compare new methods. What You’ll Get Participation in NXAI’s VSOP program Competitive compensation including performance based components Opportunity to shape a category defining applied AI company Klimaticket Hybrid work
