items.desc: Paris, 75, FR ABOUT CFM Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients. We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions. Your Role The Data-Human-Insights team works across a wide variety of structured and unstructured datasets, from time series to graphs, assessing their predictive power and preparing them for modeling. As data scientists, we work closely with the Research team to extract valuable insights from the data. Accurate and efficient time series forecasting is central to CFM's work, and it sits at one of the most important intersections between the expertise and interests of researchers and data scientists. The literature is large and growing, spanning econometrics, operations research, traditional machine learning, deep learning and generative AI. In recent years, time series foundation models have become a performant and popular option for a wide variety of forecasting tasks. The goal of this internship is to survey and evaluate existing time series foundation models against CFM's needs, and to identify where they can improve on the forecasting methods we use today. Building on this evaluation, you will research, propose and implement techniques to adapt these models to our purposes, and help plan and develop their integration into different workloads across the firm. You will be expected to understand, implement, evaluate and operationalize contemporary research on time series foundation models, and to test it as rigorously out of sample as any other model we use Key Responsibilities Survey the academic and industry literature on time series foundation models and identify the most relevant approaches. Benchmark existing models against current forecasting methods, including classical approaches (ARIMA, GARCH, state space models). Propose and implement techniques to improve these models for CFM's use cases (e.g. fine-tuning with LoRA, quantization, architectural adaptations). Evaluate models rigorously out of sample, avoiding look-ahead bias and data leakage. Aggregate and join heterogeneous data sources and process huge datasets efficiently. Help plan and develop the integration of selected models into different workloads. Write clear documentation and reports on your methodology, results and limitations, and present them to the team and, occasionally, to researchers. Your Skills You are in final year of a Master's degree or engineering school program in data science, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field. You are proficient in Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch and Matplotlib. You have experience manipulating and modeling time series, with a solid grounding in classical approaches such as ARIMA, GARCH and state space models. You have experience with modern deep learning and generative AI architectures and techniques, such as transformers, attention mechanisms, positional encodings, fine-tuning with LoRA, and quantization. You understand how to evaluate forecasting models out of sample, including how to avoid look-ahead bias and data leakage. You can aggregate and join heterogeneous data sources and manipulate huge datasets. You can conduct independent literature reviews, propose new ideas, and synthesize results, challenges and proposals. You are proactive, with a drive to experiment and propose original ideas. You communicate results and limitations clearly and concisely. You are fluent in English. You are available for a six-month internship. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT We are continuously striving to be an equal opportunity employer and we prohibit any discrimination based on sex, disability, origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, or religion. We believe that our diversity, breadth of experience, and multiple points of view are among the leading factors in our success. CFM is a signatory of the Women Empowerment Principles.

OUR MISSION

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.



TEAM CULTURE

At Aleph Alpha, we foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose.

We believe a strong engineering culture is the key to model training success. We like Extreme Programming and favor trunk-based development. We often mob-program, which keeps us aligned and means we always learn from each other.





ABOUT THE ROLE

As an AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri. 

 - You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

 - No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

 - We're still building out our training pipeline and infrastructure. Some pieces exist, some do not, and you will have real influence on what gets built and how. Your work directly shapes how quickly we can experiment and improve our models.

 - Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

 - Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates. 
   The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

 - Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

 - We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.


REQUIREMENTS

 - At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

 - As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

 - Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:
   
   - Test Driven Development (TDD)
   
   - Trunk based development
   
   - Continuous integration
   
   - Domain Driven Design


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Most of our code is in Python, there is also the occasional Rust codebase.

 - Large parts of our training pipeline are built on top of Kubernetes.

 - We do not hire for skills in a particular technology or language, but rather ability to learn and mindset, yet experience with these technologies is a plus.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Become part of an AI revolution!

 - 30 days of paid vacation

 - Access to a variety of fitness & wellness offerings via Wellhub https://wellhub.com/de-de/

 - Mental health support through nilo.health http://nilo.health/

 - Substantially subsidized company pension plan for your future security

 - Subsidized Germany-wide transportation ticket

 - Budget for additional technical equipment

 - Flexible working hours for better work-life balance and hybrid working model

 - JobRad® https://www.jobrad.org/ Bike Lease

Note: We welcome applicants at every stage of their career. Your drive and willingness to learn are far more important to us than strict experience requirements.

items.desc:
Come join Analog Devices (ADI) – a place where Innovation meets Impact. For more than 55 years, Analog Devices has been inventing new breakthrough technologies that transform lives. At ADI you will work alongside the brightest minds to collaborate on solving complex problems that matter from autonomous vehicles, drones and factories to augmented reality and remote healthcare.
 ADI fosters a culture that focuses on employees through beneficial programs, aligned goals, continuous learning opportunities, and practices that create a more sustainable future. 
 About Analog Devices 
 Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X .
 About the Role 
 As an Associate Field Applications Engineer within ADI’s Digital Healthcare team, you will begin your career supporting customers developing next-generation healthcare and medical technologies. 
 Working alongside experienced Field Applications Engineers, Field Sales, Business Unit and Technology Teams, you will build expertise in a customer facing role, helping our customers applying ADI’s world leading healthcare semiconductor technology in to healthcare applications such as patient monitoring, wearable health devices, medical instrumentation, biosensing, and connected healthcare systems . 
 You will gain hands-on experience with ADI technologies, support customer evaluations and demonstrations, and help customers integrate sensing, signal-processing, power, and connectivity solutions into their healthcare products. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Learn to understand customer requirements for medical and digital healthcare applications and translate them into technical product requirements. 
 Support customers evaluating ADI technologies for applications such as patient monitoring, wearable devices, biosensing, and medical instrumentation . 
 Assist in developing and delivering product demonstrations, evaluation setups, and basic prototypes. 
 Gain hands-on experience with sensors, analog front ends, data converters, signal processing, embedded systems, power management, and connectivity technologies used in healthcare applications. 
 Support testing and validation of product performance against customer requirements. 
 Participate in customer meetings alongside experienced FAEs to understand technical challenges and application requirements. 
 Help troubleshoot hardware, software, and system-level integration issues. 
 Create clear technical documentation, test reports, presentations, and application material. 
 Collaborate closely with sales, applications, product, and engineering teams to support customers throughout the design cycle. 
 Must Have Skills 
 Strong foundational knowledge of electronics and electrical engineering principles , including analog and/or digital circuits. 
 Basic understanding of signal acquisition, sensors, embedded systems, or signal processing . 
 Hands-on experience through university projects, laboratories, internships, or personal projects involving hardware development, testing, prototyping, or embedded software . 
 Ability to analyse technical problems and approach troubleshooting in a structured manner. 
 Interest in applying electronics and semiconductor technology to healthcare and medical applications . 
 Ability to explain technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. 
 Good written and verbal communication skills. 
 Good presentation skills
 Willingness to develop customer-facing skills and work directly with customers alongside experienced team members. 
 Desirable Skills 
 Experience or academic exposure in one or more of the following would be advantageous: 
 Biomedical electronics or biomedical engineering 
 Biosensors and physiological signal measurement , such as ECG, PPG, EEG or bioimpedance 
 Analog front ends and data acquisition 
 Digital signal processing 
 Microcontrollers and embedded systems 
 Python, MATLAB or C/C++ 
 Wireless or connected health devices 
 University projects relating to medical devices, wearable technology, patient monitoring, or healthcare instrumentation 
 Previous professional healthcare or semiconductor experience is not required .

 Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering , or a closely related technical field.

items.desc: Summary Please note this internship will be a minimum of three months, you must be enrolled as a student on a PhD course and available to start no later than 1st June 2027 Within Apple’s Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning organization (AIML), you can take part in the ongoing revolution that machine learning plays in daily life. Apple’s fully-integrated hardware and software provide unique opportunities to deliver amazing experiences, all while prioritizing user privacy. As an AIML intern, you will get to explore new methods, apply machine learning to solve ambitious problems, advance state-of-the art technology through research and publications, challenge existing metrics or protocols, and develop new theories that will impact the way we understand machine learning and the experiences it can enable. Come collaborate with some of the best in the business and help build the world's most innovative products and experiences. Description In an AIML internship, you will collaborate with researchers, engineers, and program/project managers to tackle innovative challenges. You will also receive technical mentorship and guidance that allows you to learn new things every day, gain practical skills, build real world experience, develop a greater understanding of our industry, and form valuable connections. Together, you and your team will partner to design and implement an innovative solution for a Machine Learning problem that is meaningful. At the end of your internship, you will have the opportunity to meet and present your work to AIML leadership. Where appropriate, you will have the opportunity to submit your work for publication at a suitable conference. We are offering a research internship opportunity to work directly with our research team in Copenhagen, Denmark on projects ranging from multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) to multilingual speech language models (SpeechLMs). The internship topic can be fitted to the candidate's interests, with example topics including language interference and cross-lingual transfer, the effect of training data composition on multilingual generalization, low-resource languages and dialects, efficient adaptation and continual learning, self-supervised and multimodal learning, and interpretability of multilingual speech models. Minimum Qualifications Working towards a doctoral degree in computer science, engineering, data science, applied mathematics, cognitive science, computational linguistics or equivalent. In-depth knowledge of deep learning and statistical machine learning, with strong Python programming skills and experience with ML libraries such as PyTorch or TensorFlow Research experience in multilingual or cross-lingual speech and language processing, such as ASR, speech LMs, or audio language models Interest in Speech and Language Processing Strong demonstrable record of publishing academic research in ML-related peer-reviewed venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML...), including language- and speech-specific ones (e.g. *ACL, Interspeech, ICASSP) Ability to collaborate with others and to deliver ML technologies aligned with Apple's core values: the highest standards of quality, scientific rigour, innovation, and respect for user privacy Preferred Qualifications Experience training or fine-tuning large speech or language models Experience with language interference, cross-lingual transfer, or low-resource languages and dialects Interest in the interpretability and efficient adaptation of speech models At Apple, we believe accessibility is a fundamental human right. You’ll find that idea reflected in everything here — in our culture, our benefits and our digital tools. By welcoming as many perspectives as possible, we help you build a career where you feel like you belong. Learn about accessibility in Apple’s workplace

items.desc: Overview: Certara accelerates the potential of bringing medicines to market and to patients using biosimulation software, technology, and services to transform traditional drug discovery and development. Our clients include more than 2,400 biopharmaceutical companies, academic institutions, and regulatory agencies across 70 countries. Our goal is to enable the life sciences industry’s use of data, modeling, and analytics to make better decisions across the various phases of discovery and drug development. Our software and scientists incorporate modern advances in scientific understanding, drug development experience, data analysis, and AI resulting in significant opportunities to decrease the cost and increase the probability of success for new drug approval and commercialization. The successful candidate is expected to maintain an up-to-date knowledge of the latest scientific developments, disseminate research results, and actively engage with peers and clients within industry, academia and regulatory agencies. The successful candidate will join an internationally recognised, multidisciplinary research team, providing opportunities for further development of knowledge and skills. Communicating with clients and dealing with clients’ queries. Taking part in clients’ site visits and on-site education. Assisting with the research and development of externally funded projects e.g., grants. Maintaining an active interest and awareness of new research and technologies relevant to the field, expanding your field expertise, and disseminating these within the team Qualifications: An MSc with at least 3 years of relevant experience, a PhD with at least 1 year of experience, in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacology, Pharmacokinetics, Biological/Biomedical Sciences, Chemical or Biochemical Engineering, or a related discipline, with a demonstrable background in PBPK modelling. items.desc: Company Neuphonic is building the future of on-device voice AI. We develop ultra-low-latency voice models that enable super-realistic, human-like speech directly on devices. Our focus is on building efficient generative audio models and infrastructure that can run on CPU-constrained hardware, enabling real-time voice interaction without relying on large cloud infrastructure. By dramatically reducing latency and compute requirements, we're making natural conversational AI possible on phones, embedded devices, browsers, and edge systems. This requires building high-performance systems that bridge machine learning, real-time audio processing, and distributed infrastructure. Neuphonic was founded in April 2024 and has raised significant funding from leading European investors. We work with global enterprises across hardware and consumer AI that are building the next generation of voice-enabled products. Our open source models have been downloaded over 4 million times and earned over 6,500 GitHub stars since launch. Our vision is a world where voice becomes the most natural interface for AI, enabling seamless, intuitive interactions that are accessible to everyone. Please review our Hugging Face and GitHub repos before applying, as they’ll be part of the interview discussion. Role We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help advance the state of the art in speech synthesis. You will work on research and development across the full speech pipeline — from model architecture and training to dataset design and production deployment. The role combines applied research with real-world engineering, working closely with a small team pushing the boundaries of real-time speech systems. We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in text-to-speech systems, or multimodal machine learning involving speech and audio. Your work will include: Researching and developing state-of-the-art speech synthesis models Training and optimising models for high-quality, low-latency speech generation Building and curating high-quality proprietary speech datasets Improving model quality, expressiveness, and latency Working closely with engineers to bring research models into production systems Exploring multimodal approaches to speech and conversational AI This role is best suited to candidates who have worked on research-grade machine learning models , rather than purely application-level ML systems. You have An MSc or PhD in machine learning, speech processing, computer science, or a closely related field Strong experience training and evaluating deep learning models using frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow Several years of research or industry experience developing machine learning models (this is not a graduate or entry-level role) In addition, you should have experience in one of the following areas: Text-to-speech (TTS) or speech synthesis, including model architecture, training, or evaluation or multimodal machine learning involving audio, such as models combining speech, text, or audio modalities Experience working in research-oriented ML environments, such as academic labs, advanced research teams, or deep-tech startups Familiarity with state-of-the-art approaches in speech generation, audio modelling, or multimodal systems Experience reading and implementing recent ML research papers Background from top universities, leading research groups, or equivalent research experience A strong interest in speech technology and conversational AI Benefits Help us set the company culture - you’d be joining us as part of our founding team. Help us set and guide the company culture! Competitive salary and equity - we want to make sure you’re rewarded not just in financial terms but also have a sizeable stake in the business as well. We’re in this together. Private health insurance - your health and well-being is paramount. We want to make sure that everyone in the company is supported when it comes to health. Conference, travel and development budget - your development will also grow the business. We want to make sure that you have access to the resources and opportunities you need to be at your best

items.desc: Research Engineer, Reinforcement Learning Seed-stage AI for Science Lab | London (on-site) Compensation: £130k-£220k + equity package Overview RL has pushed coding and maths forward quickly. Biology is harder because evidence is incomplete, feedback is slow, and a model can look like it’s improving while quietly gaming the reward. This role exists to build training setups where that can’t happen. The lab is a small, seed-funded founding team in London. They train frontier models as agents on real scientific work: forming hypotheses, planning experiments, reading results. You’d be one of the first technical hires. There’s no inherited stack, so you’d help set the tooling and research standards. What you’ll do Train agents with RL on multi-step problems across biology, drug discovery and clinical research Build environments where agents query biological data, call scientific tools and act on the output Design reward functions and evals that separate real progress from reward hacking Build rollout, distributed training and eval infrastructure so a few people can run large experiments Own experiments end-to-end, from design through debugging to reproducible results Work with in-house scientists to turn open biological questions into tasks with checkable outcomes What you’ll need Hands-on experience training models or agents with RL A first-principles grasp of reward design, credit assignment, exploration and training stability Strong engineering – you write reliable, fast code and can debug from learning dynamics down to GPU performance Sound experimental judgement: you know why a run failed and what to try next Comfort owning ambiguous problems in a team of a handful of people Willingness to work five days a week in the London office Optional Bonus Agentic systems work: tool use, multi-step reasoning or long-horizon tasks Biology or healthcare background – useful, not expected PhD or publications in RL, post-training or scientific ML Seniority is open, from strong early-career engineers to senior researchers. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted within 48 hours.

Within Apple’s Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning organization (AIML), you can take part in the ongoing revolution that machine learning plays in daily life. Apple’s fully-integrated hardware and software provide unique opportunities to deliver amazing experiences, all while prioritizing user privacy. As an AIML intern, you will get to explore new methods, apply machine learning to solve ambitious problems, advance state-of-the art technology through research and publications, challenge existing metrics or protocols, and develop new theories that will impact the way we understand machine learning and the experiences it can enable. In an AIML internship, you will collaborate with researchers, engineers, and program/project managers to tackle innovative challenges. You will also receive technical mentorship and guidance that allows you to learn new things every day, gain practical skills, build real world experience, develop a greater understanding of our industry, and form valuable connections. items.title: LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer
items.card: responsabilità di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer in questo contesto possono spaziare dal fine tuning e dall'adattamento di LLM open-weight per casi d'uso di sicurezza, interni o rivolti al cliente, al confronto tra approcci di post-training (SFT, tecniche parameter-efficient come LoRA e QLoRA, preference tuning come DPO dove serve, full fine tuning quando giustificato), dalla costruzione e pulizia di dataset di qualità
items.desc: Cos'è Blox Space? Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia tech,in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo dell'AI, del software, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro. Aiutiamo a connettere i talenti con questo ecosistema, operando come Talent Bridge tra le ambizioni di crescita dei professionisti e le opportunità offerte dal nostro network. In questo momento stiamo supportando una delle nostre partner companies nella ricerca di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer , e se pensi di essere il profilo giusto, ci piacerebbe conoscerti. Il Ruolo L'azienda è una startup di cybersecurity italiana che costruisce sistemi di sicurezza autonomi: individuano vulnerabilità sconosciute, prioritizzano il rischio reale e distribuiscono le correzioni senza intervento umano, con un focus sui binari compilati, perché è quello che gira davvero in produzione. È un team early, pre-seed, fondato da ricercatori di sicurezza e accademici di primo piano. Cerchiamo un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer che adatti, valuti e metta in produzione modelli linguistici open-weight, ma piegati a un unico scopo: trovare e capire vulnerabilità. Per questo cerchiamo una persona fortemente orientata alla cybersecurity, che non si limiti ad addestrare modelli ma capisca il dominio su cui lavorano. Non è un ruolo di prompt engineering: è l'intero ciclo di post-training, dal design dei dataset al fine tuning, dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla valutazione, fino al deploy in ambienti locali, privati o ristretti. Non cerchiamo il curriculum perfetto, cerchiamo la testa giusta. Cerchiamo chi sa trasformare un foundation model in un sistema affidabile e specifico per il compito, sa quando il fine tuning è la strada giusta e quando invece conviene prompting, retrieval, orchestrazione o tooling, e porta con sé una vera sensibilità per il mindset di chi attacca. Le responsabilità di un LLM Fine-Tuning Engineer in questo contesto possono spaziare dal fine tuning e dall'adattamento di LLM open-weight per casi d'uso di sicurezza, interni o rivolti al cliente, al confronto tra approcci di post-training (SFT, tecniche parameter-efficient come LoRA e QLoRA, preference tuning come DPO dove serve, full fine tuning quando giustificato), dalla costruzione e pulizia di dataset di qualità e dalla generazione di dati sintetici alla definizione di metodi di valutazione che vanno oltre i benchmark generici, fino all'analisi di regressioni e failure mode e al lavoro con il team di engineering per servire i modelli in ambienti vincolati. Le skill che fanno la differenza Esperienza pratica vera nel fine tuning di LLM: in produzione, in ricerca applicata o in contesti sperimentali seri, con più tecniche di post-training alle spalle, idealmente SFT, LoRA e QLoRA. Orientamento forte alla cybersecurity: capisci (o hai una gran voglia di capire a fondo) threat model, bug hunting e la logica di chi attacca. È il dominio su cui i modelli lavorano, e qui fa la differenza tra un buon fine tuning e uno inutile. Dati prima di tutto: sai costruire, curare e mantenere dataset per training e valutazione, e sai generare, filtrare e validare dati sintetici per migliorare il comportamento del modello, non per gonfiare le metriche. Stack solido: Python forte, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, tokenizzazione, preprocessing e training pipeline sono pane quotidiano. Dimestichezza con i vincoli reali: limiti di GPU, trade-off memoria/performance, workflow quantization-aware e ottimizzazione del training. Mentalità da debugging: sai capire perché un modello è migliorato, è regredito, ha fatto overfit o ha fallito, e la valutazione la imposti su quello che conta davvero a livello operativo, non sui punteggi generici. Autonomia a cavallo tra ricerca, dati ed engineering: ti muovi da solo su tutti e tre i fronti. Sono Very Nice to Have: un background in software security o vulnerability research, esperienza in CTF, deploy in ambienti air-gapped, on-premise o ristretti, inference optimization, quantization, model serving o runtime LLM locali, training distribuito o multi-GPU, eval harness, red-teaming o model safety testing. Ti manca qualcosa rispetto a quello che hai letto? Candidati comunque: siamo a caccia di game-changer, non di checklist da spuntare! Work arrangements Il ruolo ha come sede preferenziale l'hub di Blox Space a Torino, un ambiente cost-effective e ad alta densità di persone tecniche di valore, ma valutiamo candidature da tutta Italia, con modalità operative flessibili da concordare insieme al team. Per il ruolo è previsto un range retributivo di 40.000 – 60.000 € lordi annui, con la disponibilità a valutare anche proposte superiori per profili particolarmente senior o di valore eccezionale. Sono inoltre previsti un contributo di 1.000 € per il setup dell'home office, un piano AI premium a tua scelta e retreat aziendali …

items.desc:
Are you passionate about pushing the boundaries of what robots can do? Amazon is looking for a creative and driven Applied Scientist to help build intelligent robotic manipulation systems powered by reinforcement learning. In this role, you will research, design, and deploy machine learning solutions that enable robots to interact with the physical world in increasingly capable ways. You will tackle complex, ambiguous problems where textbook answers don't exist, working backwards from real-world needs to invent new approaches. Your work will directly influence how automation systems learn, adapt, and perform at Amazon's scale — and you will see your research come to life on real hardware.
Key job responsibilities
- Research and develop reinforcement learning methods for robotic manipulation, advancing the state of the art in sim-to-real transfer, contact-rich control, and adaptive grasping strategies.
- Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and algorithms, leveraging deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow to train policies that generalize across varied manipulation tasks.
- Build and maintain production-quality code that integrates scientific prototypes into larger robotics systems, making thoughtful tradeoffs between complexity, performance, and maintainability.
- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and science teams to define simulation requirements, validate model performance, and iterate on solutions informed by real-world hardware feedback.
- Contribute to the team's scientific roadmap by identifying new research directions, mentoring fellow scientists, and publishing results at peer-reviewed venues when appropriate.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing overnight training runs, analyzing reward curves and failure modes from your latest reinforcement learning experiments. After a quick sync with robotics engineers, you shift to refining a simulation environment to close a gap you spotted between sim and real performance. In the afternoon, you pair with a teammate to design a new evaluation framework, then wrap up by drafting a short write-up of your findings to share with the broader team.
About the team
Our team sits at the intersection of machine learning research and real-world robotics, focused on teaching robots to manipulate objects with precision and adaptability. We combine reinforcement learning, physics-based simulation, and hands-on hardware validation to deliver solutions that work beyond the lab. We value intellectual curiosity, collaborative problem-solving, and a shared commitment to turning ambitious research ideas into tangible impact. If you are excited about building intelligent systems that learn from experience and operate at scale, this is the team for you.
- Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning.
- A minimum of five years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable.
- Strong deep learning fundamentals, including supervised and self-supervised learning techniques, and reinforcement learning, including Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), neural network architectures, policy optimization algorithms, model-based vs. model-free RL, exploration-exploitation strategies, value function methods, transfer learning, domain adaptation, sim-to-real transfer, etc.
- Strong background in robotics including autonomy and/or manipulation.
- Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms.
- Ability to write production-level code in modern C++.
- Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python.
- Strong background in robotic manipulation, including dynamics, grasp synthesis, and trajectory optimization.
- PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience.
- Publications at top-tier conferences (e.g., ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS) specifically focusing on robotic manipulation, grasping, or contact-rich RL.
- Demonstrated experience working with tactile sensing, multi-fingered robotic hands, or bimanual manipulation.

 General Summary:
 At Qualcomm AI Research, we are advancing AI to make its core capabilities – perception, reasoning, and action – ubiquitous across devices. Our mission is to make breakthroughs in fundamental AI research and scale them across industries. By bringing together some of the best minds in the field, we’re pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and shaping the future of AI.
 We have multiple positions available for our 4-month Deep Learning Research internship program.
As a Deep Learning Research Intern, you will develop, prototype, and implement new fundamental and impactful methods in one of our research areas. The internship program gives you a unique opportunity to advance the state of the art in artificial intelligence and publish at scientific conferences. You will join a team of talented and experienced researchers and engineers and become part of our collaborative and interdisciplinary environment.
 Our research areas include:
 Model Efficiency : Advancing efficiency of generative models and architectures with innovations in, e.g., model quantization, compression, sparsity, conditional computation (e.g., mixture of experts), application to LLMs/LVMs/multi-modal models.
 Generative Vision : Research on efficient generative modeling of visual and multimodal data using diffusion, flow-matching, autoregressive methods, Gaussian Splatting, VLMs, and MLLMs.

items.desc: Description Are you passionate about pushing the boundaries of what robots can do? Amazon is looking for a creative and driven Applied Scientist to help build intelligent robotic manipulation systems powered by reinforcement learning. In this role, you will research, design, and deploy machine learning solutions that enable robots to interact with the physical world in increasingly capable ways. You will tackle complex, ambiguous problems where textbook answers don't exist, working backwards from real-world needs to invent new approaches. Your work will directly influence how automation systems learn, adapt, and perform at Amazon's scale — and you will see your research come to life on real hardware. Key job responsibilities Research and develop reinforcement learning methods for robotic manipulation, advancing the state of the art in sim-to-real transfer, contact-rich control, and adaptive grasping strategies. Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and algorithms, leveraging deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow to train policies that generalize across varied manipulation tasks. Build and maintain production-quality code that integrates scientific prototypes into larger robotics systems, making thoughtful tradeoffs between complexity, performance, and maintainability. Collaborate with cross-functional engineering and science teams to define simulation requirements, validate model performance, and iterate on solutions informed by real-world hardware feedback. Contribute to the team's scientific roadmap by identifying new research directions, mentoring fellow scientists, and publishing results at peer-reviewed venues when appropriate. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing overnight training runs, analyzing reward curves and failure modes from your latest reinforcement learning experiments. After a quick sync with robotics engineers, you shift to refining a simulation environment to close a gap you spotted between sim and real performance. In the afternoon, you pair with a teammate to design a new evaluation framework, then wrap up by drafting a short write-up of your findings to share with the broader team. About The Team Our team sits at the intersection of machine learning research and real-world robotics, focused on teaching robots to manipulate objects with precision and adaptability. We combine reinforcement learning, physics-based simulation, and hands-on hardware validation to deliver solutions that work beyond the lab. We value intellectual curiosity, collaborative problem-solving, and a shared commitment to turning ambitious research ideas into tangible impact. If you are excited about building intelligent systems that learn from experience and operate at scale, this is the team for you. Basic Qualifications Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning. A minimum of five years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable. Strong deep learning fundamentals, including supervised and self-supervised learning techniques, and reinforcement learning, including Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), neural network architectures, policy optimization algorithms, model-based vs. model-free RL, exploration-exploitation strategies, value function methods, transfer learning, domain adaptation, sim-to-real transfer, etc. Strong background in robotics including autonomy and/or manipulation. Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms. Ability to write production-level code in modern C++. Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python. Strong background in robotic manipulation, including dynamics, grasp synthesis, and trajectory optimization. Preferred Qualifications PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience. Publications at top-tier conferences (e.g., ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS) specifically focusing on robotic manipulation, grasping, or contact-rich RL. Demonstrated experience working with tactile sensing, multi-fingered robotic hands, or bimanual manipulation. Amazon is an equal opportunities employer. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build. Protecting your privacy and the security of your data is a longstanding top priority for Amazon. items.desc:
About us
 Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence
PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.
 Who We're Looking For 
 As a Data Scientist in Delivery, you are a problem solver and builder who is passionate about creating practical solutions that enable customers to make better engineering decisions. You are someone who can grasp advanced engineering concepts across multiple industries, and you excel at working directly with customers (and often side-by-side with them on-site) to transform cutting edge AI models into tools that are useful and used.
 You’ve worked on difficult problems that require strong foundations in data driven modelling and deep learning techniques, with hands-on experience in probabilistic methods and predictive modelling. Expertise in python, along with proficiency in libraries like NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, TensorFlow and PyTorch, is essential, with the ability to deploy scalable, production-ready models and data pipelines.
 With at least 1 year industry experience (post Masters or PhD) in a commercial, non-research environment, you’re ready to hit the ground running. You’re truly excited about growing your technical expertise and are naturally inclined to take ownership of data science work streams, continuously improving the systems and solutions you work on to ensure they are practical, impactful and meet the evolving needs of our customers.
 This Role 
 In this role, you’ll work closely with our Simulation Engineers, Machine Learning Engineers, and customers to understand and define the engineering and physics challenges we are solving.
 You’ll build the foundations for successful, impactful solutions by:
 Pre-processing and analyzing data to prepare it for use in predictive modelling, building the foundation for machine learning algorithms to be developed.
 Developing and utilizing innovative deep learning models in combination with state-of-the-art optimization methods to predict and control the behaviour of physical systems.
 Taking full responsibility for the quality, accuracy and impact of your work.
 Designing, building and testing data pipelines that are reliable, scalable and easily deployable in production environments.
 Working closely with simulation engineers to ensure seamless integration of data science models with simulations.
 Contributing to internal R&D and product development, helping to refine models and identify new areas of application.
 Engaging in open communication and presentation with both technical teams and customers, helping onboard users and co-develop with customers.
 You'll also have the opportunity to travel to customer sites in North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, for an average of 3-4 weeks per quarter , where you'll collaborate closely with customers to build solutions on-site.
 As the role evolves, there are exciting opportunities for growth as an individual contributor or a technical lead, especially if you’re driven by taking ownership of more complex projects and leading the direction of future solutions.
 Please note, this role is based in London, working 2-3 days per week in our central office. 
 Our delivery teams drive innovation to turn AI models into practical solutions - read our blog to learn more about how you’ll contribute to this exciting journey! 
 What we offer 
 Build what actually matters 
 Help shape an AI-native engineering company at a formative stage, tackling problems that genuinely matter for industry and society. This is work with real-world impact - and something you can be proud to stand behind.
 Learn alongside exceptional people 
 Work with a high-caliber, collaborative team of engineers, scientists, and operators who care deeply about doing great work, and about helping each other get better. We come from diverse backgrounds, but we share a commitment to operating at the highest level and addressing some of the most complex challenges out there. If you’re ambitious, thoughtful, and driven by impact, you’ll feel at home.
 Influence over hierarchy 
 We operate with a flat structure: good ideas win - wherever they come from. Questioning assumptions and challenging the status quo isn’t just welcomed, it’s expected.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Overview Are you a passionate researcher eager to bridge the gap between advanced engineering and clinical practice to tackle a transformative healthcare challenge? We have an exciting opportunity in the School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering for a Research Associate to apply their skills in biomedical engineering to revolutionize haemodialysis and make a profound impact on global health. You will join the Thermofluids Group at the University of Sheffield, working in close collaboration with experts in the School of Medicine and Population Health and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals. As a key member of this interdisciplinary project, you will lead the design, assembly, and clinical validation of a novel dialyser prototype. You will be responsible for testing the prototype using blood-mimicking fluids and, ultimately, human blood to assess cleaning efficiency, clotting risk, and biocompatibility. This role offers a unique opportunity to apply fundamental engineering principles to real-world physiological conditions. You will work in close collaboration with two other Research Associates focusing on numerical simulations and experimental fluid dynamics, contributing directly to a greener, more efficient future for nephrology. Main duties and responsibilities Lead the assembly of the prototype, ensuring tight tolerances for spinning components, robust sealing, and integration of semi-permeable membranes. You will troubleshoot technical issues during assembly to ensure the prototype is ready for testing. Conduct rigorous solute removal efficiency tests using Human Peripheral Simulated Blood Plasma (BZ464). You will measure the clearance rates of key metabolites, including urea, creatinine, and phosphate, to optimize the operational parameters of the dialyser. Manage the ethical procurement and testing of voluntarily donated human blood to assess biocompatibility. You will evaluate the prototype for fibrin strands, check transmembrane pressure, and analyse blood samples for clotting and haemolysis markers, ensuring safety standards are met. Work closely with the fluids engineering PDRAs to translate simulation and experimental results into physiological insights. You will actively participate in weekly meetings with renal clinicians at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals to interpret data and refine the device design based on clinical feedback. Maintain meticulous records of experimental methodologies and results in compliance with clinical governance frameworks. You will contribute to the writing of high-impact journal publications, present outcomes at international medical and engineering conferences, and participate in public engagement events regarding sustainable nephrology. Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post. Person Specification Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply. Criteria Essential or desirable Stage(s) assessed at A PhD (or nearing completion) in Biomedical Engineering, or a closely related physical science/engineering field. Essential Application Hands-on experience in experimental biomedical engineering, with proven expertise in designing, assembling, troubleshooting complex prototype hardware, and testing medical devices or filtration systems. Desirable Application/Interview Hands-on experience handling biological fluids (including blood and blood substitutes), coupled with practical expertise in biochemical analysis and blood compatibility assays such as hemolysis and clotting markers. Desirable Application/Interview Proven ability to conduct high-level scientific research independently. Essential Application/Interview A proven track record of publishing high-quality scientific papers in reputable journals. items.desc: The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: “Taking the pulse of the Earth to safeguard a habitable planet.” For section 1.4 Remote Sensing and Geoinformatics (department “Geodesy”), we are looking for a: Research Scientist (f_m_x) - Radar Remote Sensing of Mining-Induced Deformation and Landslide Hazards Reference Number 11579 Are you an innovative researcher interested in developing next-generation radar remote sensing methods to monitor geohazards? Do you have experience processing and analysing InSAR time series, and are you keen to develop new approaches to evaluate ground-motion hazards related to mining and landslides? Would you like to work with the latest satellite radar missions, including NISAR and ALOS-4, and contribute to developing advanced Earth observation methods for geohazard assessment in Chile? Are you an enthusiastic researcher ready to work in an interdisciplinary and international team? Then we would like to have you on board! Your research will focus on developing and applying advanced radar remote sensing methods to monitor mining-induced ground deformation and landslide hazards in Chile. The project will exploit the rapidly developing capabilities of satellite radar observations, including data from the latest NISAR and ALOS-4 missions, along with established Sentinel-, TerraSAR-X and other SAR datasets for detecting, characterising, and interpreting deformation associated with mining operations and slope instabilities. Your responsibilities: As a researcher, you will develop innovative methods for radar remote sensing of mining-induced deformation and landslide hazards. Your work will include: Processing and analysis of multi-temporal SAR data from NISAR, ALOS-4, Sentinel-1, and other radar satellite missions Development and application of advanced InSAR time-series items.card: The role As our VLA/WAM Integration and Deployment specialist you'll turn our VLA and World-Action Model research into reliable capabilities running on real humanoid robots. You will work across the full deployment loop: integrating foundation models with agentic systems, optimizing inference, collecting targeted real-world data, running principled evaluations, and feeding deployment experience back into training.
items.desc: About Flexion At Flexion, we're building the intelligence layer powering the next generation of humanoid robots. Our mission is to accelerate the transition from fragile prototypes to real-world humanoid deployment. We are founded by leading scientists in robot reinforcement learning (ex-Nvidia, ex-ETH Zürich), and backed by leading international VC firms. In just months, we’ve gone from our first line of code to deploying real humanoid capabilities. The role As our VLA/WAM Integration and Deployment specialist you'll turn our VLA and World-Action Model research into reliable capabilities running on real humanoid robots. You will work across the full deployment loop: integrating foundation models with agentic systems, optimizing inference, collecting targeted real-world data, running principled evaluations, and feeding deployment experience back into training. This is a broad, hands-on role for someone who enjoys making advanced models work as part of a complete autonomous system rather than optimizing a single research component in isolation. Key responsibilities VLA/WAM Deployment: Deploy and validate learned policies across multiple humanoid platforms and real-world tasks. Fast Inference: Optimize model serving, latency, action generation, asynchronous execution, and closed-loop control for real-time robot operation. Agentic Integration: Connect VLA/WAM policies with higher-level agents for task decomposition, policy selection, structured conditioning, verification, recovery, and replanning. In-Situ Data Collection: Develop improved workflows for teleoperation, interventions, autonomous rollouts, failures, recoveries, and targeted post-training data collection. Evaluation & Testing: Develop reproducible real-robot evaluations, regression suites, failure analysis, and principled comparisons between model versions. Deployment-to-Training Loop: Turn real-world successes and failures into datasets and experiments that improve subsequent pre-training and post-training. Requirements Strong Python and PyTorch skills and experience working with modern deep-learning systems. Experience deploying learning-based models in robotics, autonomous systems, or another real-time embodied setting. Familiarity with VLA, VLM, diffusion, flow-matching, video/world-model, or related multimodal architectures. Strong systems intuition around inference latency, model serving, data pipelines, logging, and debugging complex ML systems. Experience designing rigorous evaluation and diagnosing failures in learned systems. Comfort working directly with robots, sensors, data collection, and imperfect real-world hardware. Ability to work across model training, deployment, data, infrastructure, and integration rather than within a narrowly defined research area. Bonus: Experience with agentic AI systems, tool use, hierarchical policies, planning, or closed-loop verification. Experience with TensorRT, torch.compile, quantization, model compression, or other inference optimization techniques. Experience with teleoperation, human-in-the-loop learning, autonomous data collection, or online/post-training workflows. Experience with humanoids, dexterous manipulation, loco-manipulation, or whole-body control. Familiarity with reinforcement learning, continual learning, and sim-to-real. items.desc: As a public weather and climate expert, Météo-France is at your side to contribute to your day-to-day safety and help you make the best decisions in a changing climate. Faced with dangerous weather episodes that are even more intense and more frequent as a result of climate change, our missions in the service of your safety are crucial. We mobilize our expertise and our scientific and technological excellence to help you anticipate and adapt to challenging weather and climate phenomena. Find us online: https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france The DESR brings together the research entities of Météo-France (mainly CNRM, SAFIRE and LACy), the Ecole Nationale de la Météorologie and the shared administrative and IT support services (PGA). The CNRM is a Joint Research Unit (UMR 3589) under the joint supervision of Météo-France and CNRS. The CNRM conducts research in the field of meteorology and climate, from the observation, understanding and modelling of processes to the development of weather forecasting and climate projection systems that can be transferred to Météo-France's operational services. The GMAP (Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision - Modelling and Assimilation Group for Forecasting), based in Toulouse, is one of the CNRM's 6 research groups or centres. Its mission is to maintain and develop Météo-France's operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems and to conduct research in preparation for future versions. Why join us? Embark on a stimulating adventure in the service of all, alongside men and women committed to the daily challenges posed to our society by the weather and climate. And Enjoy The Following Benefits flexible working hours, RTT, telecommuting, administrative restaurant or luncheon voucher, 75% contribution to public transport, contribution to health insurance, sports and cultural associations depending on the site (climbing, gym, pottery, theater, etc.). Other benefits await you, come and discover them! This position is part of the WeatherGenerator european project (https://weathergenerator.eu/) led by ECMWF. The objective of the WeatherGenerator is to improve weather and climate predictions, enhance renewable energy planning, and provide better tools for mitigating the effect of extreme events like floods and heatwaves. It combines the latest machine learning with high performance computing, creating a robust tool for scientific discovery and real-world applications. Building on the key concepts of large-scale representation learning, WeatherGenerator is meant to be a foundation model, trained on multiple datasets, from reanalyses to satellite observations. The resulting model will be accessible through finetuning for a range of applications in the area of Earth system science. Meteo-France is taking part in this international endeavour and aims at applying the WeatherGenerator framework to regional weather forecasting, with a focus on the accurate modelling of under-meso-scale extreme events over metropolitan France. Building on the WeatherGenerator model, the aim of the present position is to evaluate its capabilities for high-resolution weather forecasting over western Europe. The Main Objectives Are The Following Fine-tune the foundation model on Météo-France Arome data ; Evaluate its performances, and benchmark against other weather forecasting models developed byMeteo-France AI-weather forecasting research team ; Implement and evaluate strategies to use the WeatherGenerator in a probabilistic forecasting setting ; Work collaboratively with the international project partners ; Contribute to workshops and hackathons organized by the projet, and more generally take part to dissemination activities (including the production of project deliverables and scientific publications). Additional information This position is open to people with disabilities. Office hours. Fixed-term contract of 18 months. Remote work available: 1 day a week maximum.

This is an excellent opportunity to shape an innovative project and develop a distinctive interdisciplinary profile at the interface of cell and developmental biology, human organoid models, advanced imaging, molecular phenotyping and computational biology. About the project The project combines patient-derived mammary organoids, high-resolution 3D/4D imaging, single-cell transcriptomics and AI-driven analysis and modelling to uncover mechanisms governing epithelial morphogenesis. At its core is a fundamental question: how do polarised cell divisions coordinate luminogenesis with cell fate and differentiation to build and maintain functional epithelial architecture? By addressing this question in physiologically relevant human models, the project aims to define how these mechanisms safeguard epithelial integrity and how their disruption leads to abnormal tissue organisation. You will take a central role in the scientific development of this ambitious programme, including experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. You will use patient-derived human mammary organoids and gene loss-of-function approaches, together with high-resolution 3D/4D fluorescence imaging, fate mapping, advanced quantitative analysis, and single-cell RNA sequencing, to connect molecular and cellular mechanisms with cell fate and tissue architecture. A major strength of the project is the integration of experimental and computational biology. Working with computational researchers, you will integrate multimodal imaging and transcriptomic data into AI-driven mechanistic and predictive models to determine how changes at the level of individual cells influence tissue-level organisation and function. About you You will have a PhD, or be close to completing one, in cell biology, developmental biology, stem cell biology or a related discipline. You will have strong experimental experience across several relevant areas of cell and developmental biology, which may include organoid or mammalian cell culture, epithelial biology, high-resolution fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology. Experience in advanced automated or semi-automated quantitative image analysis would be particularly valuable. An understanding of computational or mathematical modelling would be advantageous, but is not essential. You will be a creative and collaborative scientist with a proactive, analytical approach and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research. You should be able to plan and conduct rigorous experiments, interpret data, troubleshoot methods and communicate findings clearly. Alongside leading the experimental research, you will contribute scientific ideas and interpretation, support collaborative projects, help develop grant proposals, prepare research for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, train colleagues in new methods and advise on scientific protocols. You will bring excellent interpersonal skills and work constructively with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines. What we offer You will join a collaborative, multidisciplinary and supportive research environment bringing together expertise in mammary biology, organoids, advanced imaging, single-cell biology, AI and computational modelling. You will have access to state-of-the-art microscopy, flow-cytometry and high-performance computing facilities, multidisciplinary training and career-development opportunities. The University of Southampton offers a range of benefits, including a generous holiday allowance and additional University closure days. We support flexible working and a healthy work–life balance, alongside access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS), subsidised health and fitness facilities and a range of staff discounts. The post is offered on a three-year fixed-term basis. For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Salah Elias at S.K.Elias@soton.ac.uk. As a university we aim to create an environment where everyone can thrive and are proactive in fostering a culture of inclusion, respect and equality of opportunity. We believe that we can only truly meet our objectives if we are reflective of society, so we are passionate about creating a working environment in which you are free to bring your whole self to work. With a generous holiday allowance as well as additional university closure days we are committed to supporting our staff and students and open to a flexible working …

items.desc: # Junior Research Engineer (Real-world AI Systems) **Salary:** GBP 45,000 per year **Location:** London and customer locations around the UK **Type:** Full-Time, Permanent **Level:** Entry-level ## About Us Advai helps organisations deploy robust AI and make the most of a rapidly evolving information ecosystem that includes AI systems. We work with enterprises, government, and defence organisations to understand how AI performs in the real world, identify where it can fail, and give them the technology to thrive in this new information ecosystem. ## Role Overview We are looking for a Junior Research Engineer to join a team delivering real-world AI systems work for a major defence customer. You will help develop the machine-learning software and experimental tools needed to turn research ideas into working systems. This entry-level role is aimed at recent master's graduates with zero to six months of professional experience. Your dissertation, coursework and personal projects count; no previous full-time role is required. You will work alongside researchers and engineers to implement and evaluate AI methods, work with messy real-world data, and support field experiments. You will receive guidance from the team as you build your engineering skills. You do not need to arrive with experience in every tool or task listed below. The role requires significant on-site work at customer locations, principally in London, with travel elsewhere in the UK several times each year. You must be able to attain UK Developed Vetting (DV) clearance. ## What You Will Actually Be Doing - Help develop, test, and improve Python software for real-world AI systems. - Implement, train, and evaluate machine-learning models with guidance from the team. - Build tools for data processing and model evaluation, and learn to track experiments using tools such as MLflow. - Help investigate performance problems and make longer-running experiments more reliable through logging, checkpointing, and recovery. - Support software deployment in cloud environments and on customer hardware. - Help build simple interfaces so non-technical users can run workflows and review results. - Support field experiments, including setting up cameras or other data-collection devices and securely collecting, transferring, storing, and analysing data. - Work with researchers and engineers to turn technical requirements into tested software. ## Requirements - A relevant master's degree, such as computer science, AI, machine learning, engineering, mathematics, or a related subject, or equivalent knowledge developed through projects or study. - Python programming skills developed through study, a dissertation, personal projects, or work. - An understanding of machine-learning fundamentals, including model training, evaluation, and numerical optimisation. - An interest in or experience implementing and evaluating machine-learning models using tools such as PyTorch. - An interest in or experience using Git, testing, and reproducible workflows to write reliable research software. - A willingness to learn about Docker, cloud deployment, experiment tracking, and secure data handling. - Curiosity about unfamiliar technical problems and a willingness to ask questions and learn. - The ability to explain your work clearly and collaborate with researchers, engineers, and customers. - A strong interest in defence and national security. - Ability to attain UK Developed Vetting (DV) clearance. ## Nice to Have These are optional, not prerequisites. Interest in these areas is welcome, and any experience can come from academic or personal projects. - Interest in or experience with computer vision, signals, or robotics. - Interest in or experience with GPU computing or improving software performance. - Interest in or experience with cloud computing, on-premise hardware, or simple user interfaces. - Interest in or experience with practical experiments, cameras, or other data-collection devices. - Interest in or experience with MLflow or similar experiment-tracking tools. - Interest in AI failure modes, adversarial AI, or robust machine learning. - Availability to start immediately (preferred). ## Benefits - The opportunity to help develop AI systems for real-world use. - Guidance from researchers and engineers as you develop your skills. - Work with a major defence customer on high-impact real-world AI challenges. - Bupa private health insurance and Simplyhealth wellbeing plan. - Bike-to-work scheme. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. We strongly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to apply. ## To Apply Please email your CV and a short explanation of why you would be a good fit to recruitment@advai.com, with "Junior Research Engineer" in the subject line. Academic and personal projects are welcome examples of your work.

items.desc: About Planetek Italia Planetek Italia is an Italian Benefit Company established in 1994, bringing together more than 140 professionals with expertise in Geoinformatics, Space solutions and Earth science. We develop technologies and solutions that transform geospatial data into valuable information, supporting decision-making across environmental monitoring, smart cities, agriculture, defence and security, satellite missions and space exploration. Our expertise spans Earth Observation data processing and analytics, Spatial Data Infrastructures (SDI), satellite software, ground segment systems and cloud-based geospatial services. Among our flagship innovations is Rheticus®, our platform providing continuous geospatial monitoring services to public and private organisations. Planetek Italia is part of the D-Orbit Group, an international Space group combining complementary technologies and expertise across the Space value chain. This creates opportunities to work on ambitious national and international projects, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and contributing to innovative solutions. We believe in combining technological excellence with curiosity, collaboration and a strong sense of responsibility, developing solutions that help organisations better understand our world and contribute to a more sustainable and secure future. Your Responsibilities As “eo Data Science Specialist”. You will contribute to Earth Observation and Data Science projects, developing algorithms and AI-based solutions that transform satellite data into valuable information and operational geospatial products. Working alongside engineers, researchers and domain experts, you will have the opportunity to explore emerging technologies, experiment with innovative approaches and contribute to projects addressing environmental and geospatial challenges. In this role, you will analyze scientific and satellite payload data, contributing to the design and development of processing algorithms that transform raw data into analysis-ready datasets and, ultimately, into value-added products and services. In this role, you will: Analyze and process Earth Observation data from satellite sensors, including optical and radar imagery. Design, develop and optimize data processing algorithms and workflows to transform raw satellite data into meaningful information. Apply machine learning, artificial intelligence and advanced data analytics techniques to Earth Observation applications. Develop and test innovative solutions through rapid prototyping, experimentation and performance evaluation. Contribute to the development of value-added geospatial products and services for environmental monitoring and other application domains. Analyze and process Earth Observation data from optical and radar satellite sensors to address environmental and geospatial challenges. Design, implement and optimize algorithms and software pipelines for satellite data processing, applying strong programming skills and a solid understanding of mathematical and physical principles. Develop, train and evaluate Deep Learning models for Earth Observation applications, including image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation and change detection. Explore and adapt state-of-the-art AI methods, including Geospatial Foundation Models, assessing their accuracy, generalization capabilities and computational efficiency. Develop and validate innovative solutions through rapid prototyping, experimentation and rigorous performance evaluation, translating research outcomes into operational geospatial products and services. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, research institutions and technology partners to define technical requirements, solve complex problems and integrate solutions into broader processing workflows. Support the preparation of technical proposals and tender submissions, including ESA proposals, by contributing to the state-of-the-art review, technical approach, methodology, work plan and validation strategy. YOUR BACKGROUND AND EXPERTISE: You have an MSc or equivalent qualification in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Earth Sciences or a related field, along with practical experience in Deep Learning, Earth Observation and scientific software development. We are looking for someone with: Strong Python programming skills, including the ability to develop, test and maintain reliable scientific software. Practical experience in designing, training and evaluating Deep Learning models using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow. Experience working with Earth Observation data and a sound understanding of remote sensing principles, including optical and radar imagery. A solid foundation in mathematics and physics, particularly linear algebra, probability, statistics, numerical methods and optimization. Experience in image processing and the development of algorithms for analysing complex spatial and temporal datasets. …

items.desc: Fuse Energy is an energy startup on a mission to make energy abundant and affordable, fast. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system. We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber. We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. By selling directly to consumers we cut out the middleman, lower costs and pass the savings on to our customers. We're building a cutting-edge AI team. As an Applied AI Engineer, this role suits someone who is specifically interested in applied AI and how it can improve the energy experience for our customers and our internal operations. You'll work on consumer features (using VLM and LLM tools), and build AI tools and agents that make teams across Fuse more productive, from customer support to warehouses and back office. This is an applied engineering role, not pure research: you'll own what you build, from spec to production.
