items.desc: NestAI builds the adaptive operating system for modern battlefield operations. Most AI systems are built once, validated at deployment, and expected to stay sufficient after that. That assumption holds until conditions change, and in defence, they always do. Our team develops adaptive intelligence for unmanned and command systems: AI that continuously learns from operational data and adapts to changing conditions, deployed in environments where there is no internet, no GPS, and failure is not an option. NestOS, our open, modular, and interoperable platform, enables this at scale and keeps capability evolution under sovereign European control. Founded in 2025 by Peter Sarlin, whose previous company Silo AI became Europe’s largest AI acquisition, NestAI has grown to over 200 engineers and scientists and partners with leading European defence forces and industry. We’re ambitious about what we’re building and honest with each other. The bar is high, and so are the standards we hold ourselves to. But this is also a place built on humility, trust, and looking after each other. If that sounds like the kind of work you want to do, keep reading. Join us as a Forward Deployed Machine Learning & Computer Vision Engineer As a Forward Deployed Machine Learning & Computer Vision Engineer, you’ll work on a customer project in the Tampere region, taking perception models from prototype to production. You won’t just train models and hand them off; you’ll own the full path from a trained model to a reliable, deployed service running in the customer’s environment. This role suits someone who wants both the depth of real CV/ML engineering and the satisfaction of seeing what they build actually run in the field. What you’ll work on You’ll work closely with our AI researchers and the customer’s technical team in Tampere, bridging model development and production-grade deployment. Day-to-day, you will: Design, train, and optimize computer vision and perception models for real-time and embedded use cases, including object detection, tracking, segmentation, and 3D understanding Build and maintain data pipelines covering collection, labeling, and augmentation Package models into robust API layers (Python/TypeScript), containerize them with Docker, and deploy them to Kubernetes Architect and deploy inference services using frameworks like KServe, NVIDIA Triton, or Nuclio, across cloud and on-premise environments Integrate CV models into embedded and edge systems (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson, TensorRT) for real-world performance on site Take ownership of ML Platform components relevant to the project, ensuring governance, traceability, and best-practice workflows What we’re looking for If your background doesn’t match every requirement but the work resonates with you, we’d encourage you to apply. How you think, learn, and take ownership matters more to us than ticking every box. Here is what we are looking for: Strong expertise in computer vision and deep learning (CNNs, vision transformers, 3D perception) Proficiency in Python, with experience in PyTorch or TensorFlow Hands-on experience deploying ML/CV models to production, including Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud-native inference frameworks Experience with OpenCV, ONNX, or similar libraries for model optimization and deployment Familiarity with real-time inference on GPUs, edge, or embedded systems Understanding of camera systems, image calibration, and sensor fusion Experience with data pipelines, CI/CD, and Linux-based development A “DevOps mindset” and the drive to take something from prototype through to production and see it through Willingness to work on-site in the Tampere region as part of the customer project Nice to have: Experience with robotics, autonomous systems, or multimodal perception Background in 3D vision, SLAM, or spatial AI Publications in top computer vision or robotics venues Why join NestAI Work alongside over 200 engineers and scientists, including 60+ PhDs. People who’ve built AI platforms, autonomous systems, and defence technology across Europe. Most of our people say the best thing about NestAI is the people you get to work with. Work with real ownership. You identify what needs building, talk to the right people, and ship. Ownership here is the expectation, not a talking point. Work at a pace where Monday’s idea can be Friday’s deployment. The problems we’re solving are urgent, so the culture reflects it. Work on systems that must operate with no connectivity, no GPS, and no margin for error. The problems we’re solving are technically hard, genuinely novel, and they sit at the intersection of AI and the physical world. Work at a company where the platform, the practices, and the standards are all being built right now. The people here get to define how things work and how they scale. What we offer We offer practical benefits to support your work and wellbeing: The chance to participate in the NestAI Employee Stock Option Program (ESOP) Occupational healthcare …

Hands-on Robotik: Du arbeitest eng mit interdisziplinären Engineering-Teams zusammen, um die nächste Generation intelligenter, KI-gesteuerter Robotersysteme zu entwickeln, aufzubauen und zu optimieren. Customer Enablement & Support: Du unterstützt und onboardest Nutzer bei der Arbeit mit NeuraGym. Dabei überprüfst du Trainingspipelines und Skripte, erkennst Probleme bei der Datenqualität, analysierst das Modellverhalten und hilfst praktisch dabei, hartnäckige Blocker zu lösen. Zusammenarbeit über Teams hinweg: Du bist eine wichtige Schnittstelle zwischen den Cloud- und AI-Teams und sorgst für eine reibungslose Zusammenarbeit, technische Abstimmung und effiziente Problemlösung über verschiedene Bereiche hinweg. items.desc: Your next mission Train the intelligence behind our radars – turning complex signal data into instant, real-world detection. As our Deep Learning Engineer, you develop, optimize, and deploy neural networks that enhance real-time radar performance. You work side-by-side with AI, Software Engineering, Hardware, and Product Management colleagues – translating abstract radar signal modalities into models that spot small airborne objects in noisy environments. You report to the Team Lead AI, and your models directly safeguard critical sites around the globe. What you'll do Model design and architecture: Design, train, and optimize deep learning models for detection, segmentation, and classification. Tailor neural networks to process abstract, non-natural 3D, 4D, and 5D radar imagery. Target classification and tracking: Build advanced neural network architectures to detect and track small objects like birds and drones. Ensure models perform reliably despite real-world background noise and weather. Data engineering and automation: Prepare, preprocess, and augment large-scale radar datasets for training pipelines. Implement automated labeling strategies to streamline data preparation at scale. Edge optimization and deployment: Optimize trained neural networks for high-performance inference on edge computing hardware. Collaborate with Software Developers and Radar Specialists to integrate models seamlessly into production systems. Research and field validation: Evaluate emerging deep learning techniques to continuously lift our radar capabilities. Test model robustness under diverse field conditions and document design choices clearly. What you bring MSc in Data Science, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related technical field 2-4 years of experience in Deep Learning, specifically within Computer Vision Strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience using PyTorch Practical experience with edge deployment and model optimization tools like TensorRT or ONNX Familiarity with non-natural signal modalities such as radar, sonar, LiDAR, or medical imaging Fluent English, both written and spoken A proactive mindset and strong problem-solving skills in a collaborative environment What we offer Working for a Great Place to Work certified company; Comprehensive pension plan; Commuting allowance; 30 days of paid holiday leave (with the possibility to buy 3 additional days); Opportunities to develop your skills even further through training and certifications; High quality laptop/desktop, monitor, headphones, and any other equipment necessary for your role; An international team of 30+ nationalities, full of high performance colleagues you can exchange experiences with and learn from. As well as having a lot of fun in our social events and Friday drinks! Robin Radar is a defence technology leader in detecting, tracking and classifying drones and other small airborne objects. Our radars and software protect military sites, borders and critical infrastructure from drone threats, and also help prevent bird strikes in aviation and reduce the impact of wind farms on wildlife. Our work shows up at defence and security sites, airports and wind farms around the world. We're one of the top 10 fastest-growing companies in the Netherlands, with a crew of bright minds across 30+ nationalities. Growth doesn't mean we lose the plot – eyes on the skies, feet on the ground. Our values keep us grounded: WE TRUST. WE OWN IT. WE AIM HIGH. Want to work on next-level radar tech, solve real problems, and never have to pretend your job has meaning? You'll fit right in – we're saving you a seat.

items.desc:
Who we are 
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. 
 As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously. 
 We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. 
 The role 
 At Helsing we deliver AI-based capabilities and the enabling foundation that allow machines to perceive and assist human decision-making. You will have the unique opportunity to shape AI capabilities in one of the most challenging sectors, where high generalisation capabilities need to be paired with hardware constraints and real-world robustness.
 You will be part of a team pushing the boundaries of autonomous robotics through reinforcement learning. Your work will focus on designing, training and deploying RL-based controllers for robots operating in complex, unstructured, and dynamic real-world environments — where classical control approaches fall short. This includes enabling robots to perceive and understand their surroundings by fusing rich sensory inputs, including vision, to inform robust and adaptive control. You will own the full pipeline from simulation to deployment, ensuring that learned policies are robust, efficient, and ready for real-world operation under tight hardware constraints. 
 You should apply if you 
 Hold an MSc or PhD in Robotics, Machine Learning, Control Engineering, or a closely related field, with a strong focus on reinforcement learning and robot control.
 Have hands-on experience training and deploying RL-based controllers on real robotic hardware, not just in simulation — you have seen your policies fall, iterate, and ultimately succeed on a physical system.
 Are deeply familiar with modern RL techniques for continuous control, including but not limited to: model-free methods (PPO, SAC, TD3), model-based RL, hierarchical RL, sim-to-real transfer strategies, domain randomisation, and curriculum learning.
 Have a solid understanding of robot dynamics, kinematics, and classical control theory (e.g. PID, model predictive control, trajectory optimisation), and know when and how to combine them with learned approaches. 
 Are proficient in building and working with physics-based simulators (e.g. MuJoCo, Isaac Gym/Isaac Lab, PyBullet, Gazebo) for training and validating RL policies.
 Possess solid software engineering skills, writing clean and well-structured code in Python and/or languages like Rust or modern C++, and have experience deploying AI software to production including testing, QA, and monitoring.
 Have excellent communication skills and the ability to report and present research findings clearly and efficiently, both internally and externally.
 Are passionate about keeping up to date with current research and enjoy re-implementing and extending state-of-the-art papers.
 Note: We operate at an intersection where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. 
 Nice to have 
 PhD in Robotics, Reinforcement Learning, Control Engineering, or related fields, with publications in top-tier venues (e.g. CoRL, ICRA, NeurIPS, ICLR, IROS, RSS).
 Experience developing controllers for highly dynamic robotic systems operating under complex contact interactions and demanding environmental conditions.
 Experience with vision-based perception for robotics control, such as depth estimation, visual odometry, or visuomotor policy learning.
 Familiarity with low-level motor control interfaces and real-time embedded systems constraints.
 Experience with online adaptation and meta-learning techniques to enable robots to adapt to changing environmental conditions
 Experience with sensor fusion (IMU, proprioception, exteroception, vision) to inform and enhance learned control policies.
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields 
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns. 
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world.

Description du poste Your role : You will develop and optimise physical-layer and fronthaul processing for an O-RAN 7.2x system,
items.desc: Description de l'entreprise Free Mobile, part of the Iliad group, designs and deploys its own 5G infrastructure, from O-RAN radio units and distributed units to the user plane and Cloud RAN environment. At the heart of the DU, the physical layer and 5G fronthaul operate under hard real-time constraints. Every 0.5 ms slot must be received from the radio unit over eCPRI, processed on GPU, DSP or SIMD CPU, and delivered to the upper layers on time. This role sits at the intersection of 5G signal processing, embedded software and high-performance networking. You will work with real IQ data, radio units and production constraints, not only simulations. AI-assisted algorithms are part of the toolbox, but not the objective by themselves. We use them when they deliver a measurable improvement over classical methods in BLER, throughput or latency. Description du poste Your role : You will develop and optimise physical-layer and fronthaul processing for an O-RAN 7.2x system, from algorithm design and simulation to real-time implementation and integration with radio units. Your responsibilities will include: Developing the 5G uplink receiver chain: channel estimation, interpolation, MMSE equalisation, MIMO detection, LLR computation and LDPC decoding. Implementing PRACH detection, timing estimation and beamforming for massive MIMO. Processing O-RAN 7.2x C-plane and U-plane traffic, including eCPRI timing windows and IQ compression. Implementing real-time L1 functions in C on Linux and accelerating compute-intensive kernels with CUDA, DSP or SIMD. Building the eCPRI datapath with DPDK using poll-mode I/O, rte_flow, dedicated queues, zero-copy buffers and hardware timestamps. Optimising the complete processing chain for latency, memory usage, cache behaviour and compute load within a 0.5 ms slot budget. Validating algorithms through link-level simulations using 3GPP TDL/CDL channel models, then testing them with real IQ captures and O-RAN radio units. Measuring BLER, throughput, latency and CPU, GPU or DSP load to compare classical algorithms with AI-assisted alternatives. Investigating topics such as neural channel estimation and neural receivers when they can outperform an established baseline. Building regression tests and CI to detect performance or accuracy degradation. Contributing to architecture decisions, including GPU versus DSP or SIMD, hardware selection and accelerator integration. Working closely with radio unit, RAN, core network and operations teams. You will progressively own complete technical topics, from the mathematical model and implementation choices to their validation on the DU test bench. You will also contribute to code reviews, design documentation and open-source projects such as DPDK, Linux and U-Boot. Qualifications Your profile : We are open to both experienced engineers and high-potential graduates with strong foundations in mathematics, signal processing or embedded software. You have: An engineering degree, Master of Science or PhD in telecommunications, applied mathematics, embedded systems, computer science or a related field. Strong foundations in linear algebra, probability and digital signal processing. A good understanding of OFDM, MIMO, Fourier transforms, channel estimation, detection or channel coding. C programming skills on Linux, with an interest in memory layout, multithreading, cache behaviour and performance. Python experience with NumPy and SciPy for simulation, testing and data analysis. An interest in at least one of the following areas: 5G/LTE physical layer, O-RAN fronthaul, real-time embedded software, GPU programming, DSP/SIMD optimisation or AI for signal processing. The ability to turn mathematical concepts into code, define relevant metrics and validate the results experimentally. Good written English for reading specifications, documenting designs and reviewing code. French is a plus. Experience with CUDA, cuBLAS, cuFFT, AVX2, AVX-512, Arm NEON/SVE or fixed-point arithmetic is valuable, but you do not need to master all of them. Knowledge of DPDK, eCPRI, PTP, O-RAN 7.2x, 3GPP channel models or massive MIMO is also a plus. What matters most is your ability to understand difficult technical problems, build measurable solutions and explain the choices behind them. items.desc: About the Role As an AI Security Researcher, you bring deep expertise in AI/ML security, software development in Python, backed by a minimum MSc in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related discipline. You have hands-on experience with AI workloads, large language models, training frameworks, advanced optimization algorithms, GPU clusters, and ideally SLURM in HPC environments. You excel at modeling AI threats—model/data poisoning, permission escalation, backdoors, data drift attacks, prompt injection—and translating them into practical security defenses. You will be one of Haste's first AI security researchers pioneering defenses for trillion-parameter AI training environments alongside HPC and quantum workloads. Key Responsibilities Adversarial Threat Research: Investigating emerging attack vectors and developing techniques to uncover vulnerabilities in AI models, data pipelines, and infrastructure. Threat Modeling & Risk Analysis: Mapping and characterizing potential threats across the AI lifecycle—from data ingestion to deployment—to prioritize security investments. Developing Defenses & Guardrails: Designing and implementing detection logic and researching mitigation methods to AI threats. Collaborating with Engineering Teams: Translating research findings into actionable, production-grade security requirements for product teams, ensuring threat detection makes sense. Documentation & Reporting: Creating technical reports, whitepapers, and proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits to document vulnerabilities and share findings within the organization or to the public. Monitoring AI Ecosystem Trends: Staying updated on the latest AI security standards, frameworks (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS), and academic research. Requirements University degree in AI/ML or relevant discipline. Current residence in Germany or Austria. Full-time availability from December 1, 2026, remote from Germany or Austria only.

items.desc: About The Pirbright Institute The Pirbright Institute is a world-leading centre of excellence for research and surveillance of viral diseases affecting farm animals and viruses that spread from animals to humans. Strategically funded by the UK Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), the Institute works to enhance national and international capability to predict, detect, contain, control and eliminate economically and clinically important viral diseases through highly innovative fundamental and applied bioscience. Pirbright’s charitable objective is to conduct and promote scientific research into diseases of animals, including exotic diseases, and to develop appropriate methods for their prevention and control. Our mission is to be the world’s leading innovative centre for preventing and controlling viral diseases of livestock, applying scientific research to protect animal and human health and support the economy. Based on a dedicated campus in Pirbright, Surrey, southwest of London, the Institute employs just over 400 staff, with research supported by 52 PhD students and nine interns from a wide range of backgrounds. We pride ourselves on the diversity of our community and on a culture built around our PRIDE values: Passion for the highest standards of quality, delivery and performance; Reliability in everything we do, including leadership, learning, biosecurity and anticipating and containing unexpected events; Innovation as the driving force behind our fundamental and applied science; Dignity and respect for every member of our diverse community; and Excellence in all aspects of our work, from health, safety and biosafety to scientific research, customer service and environmental protection. Pirbright provides national and international capacity to predict, detect, understand and respond to emerging viral diseases of livestock, as well as endemic viruses circulating within and beyond the UK. Our diagnostics, surveillance facilities and specialist expertise form an important national capability, helping to protect the UK from livestock viral diseases that threaten our borders and enabling us to respond decisively and rapidly in the event of an outbreak. Our fundamental research focuses on viruses, hosts and the complex interactions between them, while our wider science addresses key challenges including protecting the UK and global agriculture from viral threats, increasing agricultural efficiency to improve animal health and welfare, mitigating the growing threat of vector-borne diseases driven by climate change, and improving human health through a greater understanding of vaccine-induced protection. With internationally recognised expertise in virology, immunology, diagnostics and surveillance, Pirbright combines fundamental discovery with practical solutions to tackle today's diseases and prepare for the emerging viral threats of tomorrow. Advancing science to improve the world in which we live. Organisation position & Purpose We are seeking a highly motivated and innovative scientist to join the Mucosal Immunology Group at contributing to a transformative research programme supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and BBSRC Institute Strategic Programme Grants. This post offers a unique opportunity to be part of a pioneering One Health research initiative focused on interrupting the transmission of respiratory viruses such as influenza andcoronaviruses, which remain major public health challenges despite the availability of current vaccines and antivirals. The work will utilise the pig as a large, natural host animal model due to its close physiological, anatomical, immunological, and genetic similarities to humans. Pigs not only serve as natural hosts for influenza viruses highly similar to those in humans, but their lung structure and antibody responses also provide a highly relevant platform for translational research. The postholder will investigate the potential of mRNA-encoded antibodies, interferons, and other innate immune stimulators administered to the respiratory tract to prevent infection and interrupt transmission. This will include evaluating their capacity to reduce viral shedding, limit lung pathology, and disease severity. A central element of the project involves comparing different delivery strategies to determine which offer the most effective expression and protection in vivo. The role will also involve the development of porcine influenza-specific monoclonal antibodies following infection or immunisation, with detailed analysis of their specificity, functionality, and repertoire depending on the route of administration. To achieve these objectives, the postholder will apply a broad range of immunological and virological techniques, including ELISA, microneutralisation assays, virus propagation, plaque assays, molecular cloning, antibody repertoire profiling, and bioinformatics. These methods will be integral to assessing both the immune …

Batch scoring and model integration into data pipelines. Git and solid engineering practices, with scalable solutions mindful of performance and cost. Proactivity, analytical thinking and business-facing communication, including conversion of requirements into technical solutions. Portuguese language. Would Be Great If You Have Azure Machine Learning exposure: training jobs, pipelines, model registry and inference endpoints. Working knowledge of Azure Data Factory. items.desc: Location: Paris, France. We value working in person, and we stay flexible. You may also get the chance to join us on occasional trips to San Francisco. Language: English is required. You do not need to speak French. The role You own two things at Armature: the research we publish and the evals system behind our results. You work on both hand in hand with our forward deployed engineer and our product engineer. The research we publish. Our studies on how coding agents think and choose are how most customers find us. You decide what we study next, you run the studies behind our public leaderboards, and you publish the findings under your name. The evals system. Everything we tell a customer depends on our evals, so they have to be excellent. You research how to design them to get the best results, and you build what works into the product. This field is young, so many of your questions won’t have an answer yet, and what you find will shape how software gets rebuilt for agents. What you will do Published research Design and run studies on how coding agents choose tools, how models and harnesses differ, and how agents use software. Find the next questions worth asking, and new ways to look at the data we already have. Automate the research runs and the analysis, so each study takes less time than the one before. Write up your findings so developers want to read and share them. Evals system Test the latest research on evals against our own data, and keep what improves our results. Turn the questions our customers ask into better evals. Ship what works into the product with our product engineer. Who we look for You’re an engineer from a top school, and if you’re a new grad, your internships show that you can build things. You build through coding agents every day: you split the work, guide the agents and understand what they produce, and this is the skill we value most. You can go from raw data to a finding on your own. You come with your own ideas, and you like to test them. You have high agency: you move forward without waiting for instructions. Not a fit if You want pure research and nothing to ship. You need a fixed scope before you start. You want to train models more than you want to study how they behave. You prefer to write every line yourself over working through coding agents.

We will manage your applications and surface other opportunities that are a fit. The role Most frontier RL labs are racing on the same synthetic coding and math benchmarks. This research lab, backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, is taking those multi-step reasoning methods and directing them at biology, drug discovery, and clinical medicine. Equipped with serious compute and petabytes of proprietary biomedical data, they are engineering grounded environments where models can generate hypotheses, design wet-lab experiments, and interpret real scientific results. As an early Member of Technical Staff in Reinforcement Learning, you will own the full research loop, from designing environments and reward functions to scaling distributed training runs. This is not prompt tuning or wrapping commercial APIs; it is foundational research engineering where you turn messy biological workflows into verifiable tasks and build the rollout infrastructure to support rapid experimentation. The work Build grounded RL environments, reward structures, and evaluation frameworks that force genuine scientific reasoning and actively resist reward hacking. Train agents on multi-step reasoning, tool use, and long-horizon exploration across complex biological datasets. Architect and scale the rollout, distributed training, and evaluation infrastructure required to run high-throughput experiments on large GPU clusters. Partner directly with domain scientists to convert ambiguous biological questions into formal environments with verifiable outcomes. Shape the technical stack, research discipline, and engineering standards as one of the lab's foundational hires. What You Bring Deep, first-principles understanding of reinforcement learning, with demonstrated experience debugging exploration, credit assignment, and reward hacking in large-scale models or complex agents. Strong research engineering instincts, capable of writing performant code and debugging everything from learning dynamics down to distributed systems and GPU performance. Hands-on experience building agentic systems, custom RL environments, tool-use architectures, or training setups for multi-step, long-horizon tasks. Based in or willing to relocate to London, working on-site five days a week in the lab. Why apply through Dex Frontier RL roles tackling genuine scientific problems are exceptionally rare, and separating serious research labs with real compute from superficial AI hype is difficult from job specs alone. Dex gives you unvarnished insight into the team's compute access, culture, and technical roadmap before you enter their pipeline. items.desc:
Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.
 A Day in the Life 
 Medtronic 
 At Medtronic, we value what makes you unique. Be part of a company that thinks differently to solve problems, make progress, and deliver meaningful innovations. 
 Our Purpose 
 The Physiological Sensing R&D team is dedicated to the end-to-end development, continuous advancement, and clinical validation of innovative monitoring technologies that measure, interpret, and leverage physiological signals to improve patient outcomes. Their expertise spans anesthesia and depth of sedation monitoring, respiratory monitoring, pulse oximetry, regional oximetry, and the integration of predictive algorithms and clinical decision support solutions. By focusing on non-invasive, real-time technologies, they empower clinicians with actionable insights in surgery, critical care, and other high-risk settings. 
 A Day in The Life Of: 
 As an Embedded Software Engineer II , you will contribute to the development of embedded software platforms for physiological monitoring solutions that provide clinicians with meaningful insights and support Medtronic’s Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Your work will span the product lifecycle, from early-stage technical evaluation through feature development, product enhancements, and sustainment. You will work independently, with general supervision, on defined and moderately complex assignments while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across different countries.
 Design, develop, test, and maintain embedded software.
 Develop proof-of-concept solutions to evaluate new ideas and technologies.
 Contribute to modular software design and broader technical discussions.
 Participate in code reviews and software testing activities.
 Investigate software issues and implement appropriate solutions.
 Create and maintain software requirements, design documentation, test records, and other development records.
 Contribute to software risk analysis and the implementation of risk-control measures.
 Key Skills & Experience 
 Basic Qualifications
 Level 8 degree and minimum of 2 years of relevant experience OR Master's degree with a minimum of 0 years relevant experience.
 Practical programming experience in embedded C and/or C++.
 Experience developing and testing software for resource-constrained microcontrollers.
 Experience developing software for bare-metal and/or RTOS-based embedded systems.
 Experience working with one or more embedded interfaces and peripherals, such as UART, SPI, I²C, ADC, and PWM.
 Experience debugging embedded software using hardware and software debugging tools.
 Understanding of software-development practices, including modular design, source control, code reviews, unit testing, and integration testing.
 Ability to work independently, with general supervision, on defined and moderately complex software assignments.
 Ability to communicate clearly and work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
 Nice to Have:
 Experience developing embedded software using STM32 or a comparable microcontroller platform.
 Experience developing embedded software using an RTOS such as ThreadX, FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or a comparable RTOS.
 Experience with unit testing, including the use of test frameworks and mocks, or with static-analysis and automated-testing tools.
 Exposure to CI/CD practices for embedded software development.
 Experience developing and debugging software for prototype or early-stage hardware.
 Experience working in a regulated software-development environment, preferably within the medical-device industry.
 Familiarity with IEC 62304, software risk-management practices, or traceability between requirements, implementation, and verification evidence.
 Experience developing Python-based tools for testing, automation, diagnostics, or data analysis.

items.desc:
We Are Waiting for You 
 Hi there! 
 I am Álvaro, the recruiter for this position. Nice to meet you! 
 First, a little bit about what I like the most about working at Zurich Technology Delivery Center : The environment here is incredibly collaborative and innovative. Our tech-driven mindset fosters continuous learning and growth, creating an atmosphere where everyone can thrive. Now, I can't wait to share this exciting journey with you at Zurich ! 
 First of all, THANK YOU for considering our company. We understand that finding the right opportunity can be tough, but I’ll try to make it easier. 
 Who Are We? 
 Let me introduce us. You’re reading about Zurich Insurance Group , a global leader in insurance, but this role specifically pertains to our Technology Delivery Center (TDC). Established in Barcelona in 2006, the TDC operates as an integral part of Zurich Insurance Group, providing cutting-edge technological solutions and support to Zurich's local and global business units. 
 In essence, Zurich TDC is where technology meets the vast reach of a multinational company. We specialize in areas such as software development, data analytics, cybersecurity, and IT infrastructure. Our primary mission is to support Zurich's strategic goals and enhance operational efficiency through innovative technology solutions. 
 If you're considering a role with us, know that you'll be joining a hub of technological excellence dedicated to driving Zurich's success on a global scale. 
 Our Opportunity 
 As Zurich continues to embrace the transformative power of Artificial Intelligence across our global operations, ensuring these technologies are deployed ethically, transparently, and securely is our highest priority. 
 We are looking for a dedicated and passionate AI Governance Specialist to join our Group Responsible AI (RAI) Team. In this critical role, you will be at the forefront of shaping how our organization interacts with cutting-edge AI technologies, safeguarding our customers and stakeholders while actively enabling sustainable business growth. 
 What Can You Expect? 
 And you might be thinking: This is great, what will my day-to-day be like, at TDC? I’m glad you asked. 
 As AI Governance Specialist, your main responsibilities will include: 
 Monitor emerging AI regulations, industry standards, and best practices to strengthen the organization's AI governance framework. 
 Apply AI governance frameworks, policies, and regulatory requirements, including the EU AI Act, to AI use cases and business initiatives. 
 Conduct AI risk and impact assessments to evaluate the responsible use of AI solutions across the organization. 
 Advise business, technology, risk, legal, compliance, and security stakeholders on Responsible AI requirements and governance expectations. 
 Challenge assessments and control decisions by providing independent, evidence-based recommendations and review outcomes. 
 Develop and continuously enhance AI governance processes, controls, standards, and review methodologies. 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure AI solutions are deployed in a compliant, ethical, and risk-aware manner. 
 Review AI and ML systems, assessing methodologies, data usage, model performance, limitations, and associated risks. 
 Produce clear assessment reports, governance decisions, and stakeholder communications that support transparency and accountability. 
 What Makes You a great Fit? 
 While we’re not seeking perfection or expecting you to save the world, we believe that if you meet some of these requirements, you’ll be a fantastic fit for our team. We are waiting for you! 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Data, or a related field. 
 Proven experience in AI Governance, Responsible AI, Model Risk Management, or AI Risk and Compliance, including hands-on experience conducting and reviewing AI risk and impact assessments. 
 Practical knowledge of the EU AI Act and familiarity with AI governance standards such as NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, or similar frameworks. 
 Strong understanding of AI and ML systems, with the ability to assess model design, data usage, performance, limitations, and associated risks. 
 Experience designing, improving, or scaling AI governance frameworks, processes, controls, or operating models in audit, risk, compliance, or other regulated environments; insurance or financial services experience is preferred. 
 Knowledge of Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs). 
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to challenge, influence, and advise technical and business stakeholders. 
 Key Outputs 
 AI Assessment Framework (AIAF): Continuously maintained and optimized risk assessment methodology. 
 AI Catalogue: Group-wide AI use case inventory and tracking system complete and accurate. 
 Guidance Library: Regularly updated documentation on responsible AI topics. 
 Strategic Business Insights: Reports based on AI catalogue data to inform executive leadership. 
 RAI Advisory …

 The Arm Physical AI Solutions team in Munich is looking for a highly motivated software engineering graduate. Positions are in various teams working on projects across the software stack – from embedded software and firmware to complex application and AI workloads.

items.desc: Computer Vision Engineer - Vet Vision AI Improving Animal Welfare With Smarter AI Milford, Derbyshire, UK | Full-Time | Hybrid (2 days/week on-site, 3 days remote) £38,000–£50,000 We're building up our computer vision team and looking for a Computer Vision Engineer. You'll own the models and infrastructure we already have running on real footage of animals: keeping them reliable, measuring how they perform in the field, and steadily improving them. There is room to build new things too, but the first job is making sure what we've shipped keeps working and gets better. About Vet Vision AI Our mission is to improve the welfare of animals through cutting-edge AI, building intelligent monitoring systems that detect health and welfare issues earlier, helping farmers, vets and owners provide better care for animals. We're an experienced team looking to expand so we can deliver more insights to farmers and further improve animal welfare. Our systems are already deployed across the UK on dairy farms and equine yards. Coming up with innovative ideas and turning them into reliable systems is the core of the job. Our Location We're based in Milford, Derbyshire, a village on the edge of the Peak District with strong transport links to Derby, Nottingham and wider midlands area. You'll be on-site 2 days a week and remote for 3. The office is a short walk from the River Derwent and a few minutes from the hills, so lunchtime walks are part of the rhythm here. What You'll Do Maintain and improve the computer vision models we have in production (detection, tracking, behaviour classification) on images and videos from real environments Own the training and inference infrastructure: data pipelines, retraining, versioning, and deployment to cloud and edge devices Monitor model performance in the field, investigate what breaks (lighting, occlusion, camera placement, seasonal change) and engineer around it Build the test sets and evaluation that tell us when a change is safe to ship Work with our annotation specialists to shape labelling guidelines, spot data quality problems early, and close the loop between model failures and the data that fixes them Support new model work as it moves from experiment to production Input on the technical direction of the vision pipeline and the trade-offs between accuracy, cost and deployment constraints What We're Looking For 3+ years in computer vision , with real production experience, not just research or prototyping A relevant degree (Computer Science, Maths, Engineering, or similar) Shipped computer vision work : you've taken models from training into something people actually used, and you can talk about what went wrong Strong Python: clean, tested code; comfortable with the full training and evaluation loop Video and image fundamentals : object detection, tracking and/or segmentation; OpenCV; a working grasp of what cameras, compression and lighting do to your data Evaluation judgement : you know the difference between a good and a bad model, and you build test sets that expose the gap Deployment experience : optimising and deploying models to constrained hardware, edge devices or cloud pipelines (ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation, or similar) Collaborative, honest and direct : you say what you think in review, take feedback, and follow through on what you commit to Care about the mission : an interest in using tech for real-world animal welfare impact Nice to Have Multi-object tracking or behaviour recognition in video Edge or embedded deployment (Jetson, Coral, or similar) Experience designing data strategy: what to label, how much, and when you have enough Experience with agricultural imagery or a related field An interest in agriculture, animals or veterinary science How We Work We're an agile team: clear priorities, honest reviews, and retros that actually change how we work. We're collaborative by default and encourage everyone, across every department, to work closely together and learn from one another. What We Offer £38,000–£50,000 , placed according to experience Hybrid working: 2 days/week on-site in Milford, 3 days remote Real ownership from day one, and a clear path to a senior role A team where your decisions ship and you see them running on sites Meaningful work: your models directly improve animal welfare Why This Role Matters A model that worked in March and quietly degrades by January is a welfare failure nobody notices until it's too late. Your work is what stops that happening. Keep our systems reliable and improving and animals get help earlier and live better lives. If you want your computer vision work to run somewhere real and count for something, we'd love to hear from you. To apply: send a CV and, if you have one, a link to work you're proud of (a GitHub, a write-up, a demo). We'd love to walk you through all the details during the recruitment process! Teltonika’s Telematics
items.desc: We are looking for AI Engineer to join our R&D team in Warsaw, Poland. You will join one of the teams developing our next-generation video telematics devices and be responsible for analyzing, selecting, testing, and deploying machine learning models used for on-device (edge) inference, PC-based validation, and — going forward — cloud-based processing of data collected from our devices. We'd love to walk you through all the details during the recruitment process! Teltonika’s Telematics business unit develops and produces easy-to-use GPS tracking devices for effective fleet management across logistics, agriculture, car sharing, construction, and more. We use the latest technologies to set new standards for the telematics industry. If you want to shape how AI models run at the edge on real embedded hardware, not just in a notebook, this is the team for you! In this role, you will: Analyze, select, and evaluate machine learning models for specific use cases and problem-solving needs (e.g. ADAS/DMS, video/image analysis, sensor and CAN data processing). Test, benchmark, and configure AI models for deployment on embedded edge devices, as well as on PC (Windows, Linux) platforms. Analyze system capabilities (CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, power budget) and contribute to selecting hardware of appropriate specification for AI workloads. Optimize models for resource-constrained edge hardware (quantization, pruning, conversion to inference runtimes such as TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime, or vendor-specific SDKs). Design the data flow between edge-level pre-processing and any future cloud-based models that further process data collected from edge AI devices. Collaborate with embedded software and hardware teams to integrate models into the media/data pipeline of our video telematics devices. Track current and emerging AI/ML trends and evaluate their applicability to company products. Document model performance, testing methodology, and deployment decisions. Participate in Agile/Scrum team processes and decision making. What we expect of you: 2+ years of experience in AI/ML model development, evaluation, or deployment. Solid Python skills and practical experience with ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar). Experience in testing and benchmarking models for accuracy, latency, and resource usage. Understanding of the constraints of running inference on embedded/edge hardware (CPU/GPU/NPU limitations, memory, power). Comfortable working across both Linux and Windows environments. Strong analytical skills and the ability to independently investigate and solve technical problems. Professional working proficiency in English. Ideally, you’ll also have: Experience with edge inference runtimes and toolchains (TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, or vendor NPU SDKs such as NXP, Qualcomm, Mediatek, Rockchip RKNN, or similar). items.desc: # Junior Research Scientist (Real-world AI Systems) **Salary:** GBP 45,000 per year **Location:** London and customer locations around the UK **Type:** Full-Time, Permanent **Level:** Entry-level ## About Us Advai helps organisations deploy robust AI and make the most of a rapidly evolving information ecosystem that includes AI systems. We work with enterprises, government, and defence organisations to understand how AI performs in the real world, identify where it can fail, and give them the technology to thrive in this new information ecosystem. ## Role Overview We are looking for a Junior Research Scientist to join a team delivering real-world AI systems work for a major defence customer. You will help investigate how AI systems perform in operational conditions and explore methods to improve their performance and robustness. This entry-level role is aimed at recent master's graduates with zero to six months of professional experience. Your dissertation, coursework and personal projects count; no previous full-time role or PhD is required. You will work alongside researchers and engineers to understand technical problems, try out research ideas, and design, run, and analyse experiments. You will develop your research skills with guidance from the team lead. You do not need to arrive with experience in every tool or task listed below. The role requires significant on-site work at customer locations, principally in London, with travel elsewhere in the UK several times each year. You must be able to attain UK Developed Vetting (DV) clearance. ## What You Will Actually Be Doing - Help investigate machine-learning methods for real-world AI systems. - Help design, run, and analyse controlled experiments and field trials with guidance from the team. - Evaluate model performance and robustness, investigate failure modes, and understand the limitations of different approaches. - Implement research ideas in Python and work with engineers to test prototypes. - Read relevant research and explore how promising methods could apply to the team's work. - Explain your findings and their limitations clearly to colleagues and customers. ## Requirements - A relevant master's degree, such as AI, machine learning, computer science, mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related subject, or equivalent knowledge developed through projects or study. - An understanding of machine-learning fundamentals, including training, optimisation, generalisation, and model evaluation. - Python programming skills developed through study, a dissertation, personal projects, or work. - An interest in or experience implementing and evaluating machine-learning methods using tools such as PyTorch. - An interest in or experience designing experiments, analysing results, and drawing conclusions supported by evidence. - Curiosity about open-ended technical problems and a willingness to develop research questions with support from the team. - The ability to explain your work and its limitations clearly and collaborate with others. - A strong interest in defence and national security. - Ability to attain UK Developed Vetting (DV) clearance. ## Nice to Have These are optional, not prerequisites. Interest in these areas is welcome, and any experience can come from academic or personal projects. - Interest in or experience with AI failure modes, adversarial AI, or robust machine learning. - Interest in or experience with computer vision, signals, or robotics. - Interest in or experience with practical experiments or fieldwork. - Interest in or experience reading research papers and reproducing their results. - Interest in or experience using Docker, version control, or experiment-tracking tools. - Availability to start immediately (preferred). ## Benefits - The opportunity to help develop AI systems for real-world use. - Guidance from researchers and engineers as you develop your skills. - Work with a major defence customer on high-impact real-world AI challenges. - Bupa private health insurance and Simplyhealth wellbeing plan. - Bike-to-work scheme. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. We strongly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to apply. ## To Apply Please email your CV to ian.martin@advai.com and recruitment@advai.com, with "Junior Research Scientist" in the subject line. Academic and personal projects are welcome examples of your work.

items.desc: Fixed-term contract for 3 years | Full-time, 38.5 hours per week | Salary according to TV-L E13 | Institute of Neuropathology We are UKM. We have a clear social mission and, with our focus on healthcare, research, and teaching, we bear a unique responsibility. To meet our high standards every day, we are looking forward to your expertise in AI and computer vision at the Institute of Neuropathology. We develop deep learning methods that improve the diagnostic yield of brain biopsies – ideally with you on board! RESEARCH PROJECT: DISEASE RECOGNITION FROM REACTIVE CNS TISSUE Brain biopsies may contain only reactive tissue adjacent to a lesion, preventing a definitive diagnosis by conventional histopathological assessment. Our project uses pathology foundation models and weakly supervised deep learning to recognise the underlying disease in such tissue from whole-slide images (preprint: arxiv.org/abs/2609.02390). The project will be carried out in close collaboration with the Computer Vision and Machine Learning Systems group at the University of Münster (Prof. Dr. Benjamin Risse and Dr. Jan Ernsting), providing an interdisciplinary environment for developing and applying advanced AI methods to clinically relevant challenges. Responsibilities Develop machine learning approaches for histological whole-slide image analysis, including weakly supervised classification using pathology foundation models and multiple instance learning (MIL) Build reproducible pipelines for image preprocessing, quality control and feature extraction Evaluate model robustness, bias and generalisation across centres, scanners and frozen sections, and apply interpretability methods Manage the digital pathology infrastructure of the institute (slide scanners, computing servers) Contribute to prospective observational evaluation, reproducible research software, scientific publications and conference presentations Requirements A Master's degree or equivalent qualification in computer science, data science, mathematics, bioinformatics or a related discipline Strong theoretical foundations in machine learning and computer vision Practical experience with Python programming and deep learning frameworks Interest in rigorous statistical evaluation and reproducible scientific research An independent and structured working approach, strong communication and teamwork skills, and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research Good written and spoken English skills Experience with large image datasets, computational pathology, foundation models, multiple instance learning or image registration is an advantage Prior medical knowledge is not required. We Offer Salary according to TV-L E13, extra annual payment, and company pension plan (VBL) 30 days of vacation per year, plus two additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve A wide range of training and professional development opportunities A respectful and appreciative work environment within a diverse team Support and advisory services for health and work-life balance Additional benefits such as sports programs, job ticket, jobrad, company events, cafeteria, and emergency childcare Additional Research Benefits An opportunity to address a clinically relevant challenge at the intersection of AI, computer vision, neuropathology and molecular research, with the potential for meaningful clinical impact Close collaboration with internationally recognised research groups specialising in AI, neuropathology and molecular research, as well as an established network of partner neuropathology centres An interdisciplinary research environment with established analysis workflows and access to extensive histological image datasets Opportunities to develop innovative methodological approaches and shape your own research directions For inquiries, please contact: Prof. Dr. Christian Thomas, Institute of Neuropathology, christian.thomas@ukmuenster.de or Prof. Dr. Benjamin Risse, Institute for Geoinformatics and Department of Computer Science, b.risse@uni-muenster.de Apply now via our career portal.

items.desc: Sous la responsabilité de deux directeurs de recherche et co-encadrants de cette thèse, l’objectif de votre thèse sera de viser à prédire l'expression des gènes chez les plantes, en couplant des modèles de langage génomiques et l'apprentissage sur graphes de régulation génique (projet BioLLM-CRE). Vos Activités Seront Les Suivantes Constituer un jeu de données de référence associant éléments cis-régulateurs et profils d'expression spatio-temporelle chez Arabidopsis et le riz. Évaluer des modèles de langage génomiques, généralistes et spécialisés plantes, pour la prédiction de l'expression, en les comparant à des approches d'apprentissage automatique classiques. Concevoir des modèles d'apprentissage sur graphes (GNN, Graph Transformers) intégrant ces représentations de séquence dans les réseaux de régulation génique. Interpréter les modèles pour identifier les modules régulateurs déterminants, et évaluer leur transfert vers d'autres céréales. Valoriser les résultats : publications, conférences internationales, rédaction du manuscrit de thèse. Diffuser le benchmark, le code et les modèles en open source. Participer à la vie scientifique de l'unité (séminaires, formations doctorales). Votre future équipe Vous rejoindrez un collectif interdisciplinaire de l'UMR DIADE associant bioinformatique et intelligence artificielle (modèles fondationnel en génomique) et biologie du développement racinaire. Vous aurez accès à des moyens de calcul intensif (GPU) et à un environnement de recherche international. Conditions particulières d'exercice Des déplacements ponctuels en France et à l'étranger (conférences, collaborations) seront à prévoir. Le profil que nous recherchons Vous Avez Développé Les Compétences Suivantes Maîtrise de Python et d'un framework d'apprentissage profond (PyTorch). Connaissances en apprentissage automatique et en deep learning (Transformers, apprentissage de représentations). Notions en apprentissage sur graphes (PyTorch Geometric, DGL) et en modèles de langage (Hugging Face) appréciées. Connaissances en génomique et en manipulation de données de séquençage (formats NGS, outils bioinformatiques). Anglais scientifique, à l'écrit comme à l'oral Niveau B2-C1. Esprit d'équipe et aisance relationnelle. Capacités de synthèse et de rédaction. Persévérance et capacité d'adaptation. Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau 7 (Master ou diplôme d'ingénieur) dans les domaines suivants : bioinformatique, informatique (IA, apprentissage automatique), biologie computationnelle. L’institut met à votre disposition un panel d’outils tel que le parcours digital d’intégration, l’accès à la formation permanente, à la promotion et la mobilité. En Rejoignant L’IRD, Vous Bénéficierez De 32 jours de congés + 13 RTT (pour un temps plein à 38h30 hebdomadaire). Une restauration collective. Souscription annuelle (facultative) à l’Association des Œuvres Sociales : prestations vacances-loisirs et sportives-culturelles. D’une affiliation à la protection sociale complémentaire MGEN, offrant une couverture santé et prévoyance de qualité. D’un cadre de travail agréable, proche de la nature, desservi par le Tram ligne 5 et accessible en vélo et bénéficiant d’un système de co-voiturage (convention mobilité signée avec la métropole). Nos recrutements sont fondés sur les compétences, sans distinction d’origine, d’âge ou de genre et tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap.

items.title: LLM Agent Research Intern
items.card: The Role Entails We are hiring a research intern to train LLM agents that play in-game characters. The agent has to stay in persona across multi-turn dialogue, use memory and game context, and keep relationship, tone, and world rules intact. The work sits on a live role-play NPC model: supervised fine-tuning today, with preference optimization and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning as the next training stages.
items.desc: About The Hiring Team Level Infinite is Tencent’s global gaming brand. It is a global game publisher offering a comprehensive network of services for games, development teams, and studios around the world. We are dedicated to delivering engaging and original gaming experiences to a worldwide audience, whenever and wherever they choose to play while building a community that fosters inclusivity, connection, and accessibility. Level Infinite also provides a wide range of services and resources to our network of developers and partner studios around the world to help them unlock the true potential of their games. What The Role Entails We are hiring a research intern to train LLM agents that play in-game characters. The agent has to stay in persona across multi-turn dialogue, use memory and game context, and keep relationship, tone, and world rules intact. The work sits on a live role-play NPC model: supervised fine-tuning today, with preference optimization and verifiable-reward reinforcement learning as the next training stages. Train role-play agents with supervised fine-tuning (SFT), then post-train them with direct preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Iterate on persona consistency, multi-turn coherence, and instruction following. Build and curate SFT, preference, and verifiable-reward data for character dialogue, covering memory injection, relationship stage, language switching, emotion, and out-of-character resistance. Design checks that can be verified automatically, such as format, language, persona boundaries, and safety refusals, and use them both as RLVR rewards and as offline regression tests. Work with game designers and engineers to bring the agent into a live game, and keep latency, cost, and player experience within production constraints. Who We Look For Currently enrolled in a Master's or PhD program in Computer Science, NLP, Machine Learning, or a related field, or recently graduated. Available at least three days per week, with supervisor and university approval where required. Fluent English (written and spoken) and strong communication skills are required. You will work closely with game designers, engineers, and researchers across regions, and must be able to explain experiment results and trade-offs clearly. Hands-on experience with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of LLMs, and with post-training methods including DPO and RLVR (or a closely related verifiable-reward RL method). You should be able to run the loop from data and training config through evaluation and the next iteration. Experience training or evaluating role-play or character-dialogue models, including persona consistency, multi-turn dialogue, and staying in character. Proficient in Python and PyTorch, and comfortable with the Hugging Face / Transformers training stack. Preferred: experience with LLM agents (memory, planning, or tool use), LLM applications in games, or a publication at a major NLP/ML venue (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML). Equal Employment Opportunity at Tencent As an equal opportunity employer, we firmly believe that diverse voices fuel our innovation and allow us to better serve our users and the community. items.desc:
TomTom is a global leader in navigation, mapping, and traffic information. Join our dynamic team and vibrant culture to contribute to shaping the future of location technology.

We are looking for an Applied Scientist to shape how AI understands and uses TomTom's location data. You'll develop machine learning models and design the systems that let LLMs reason accurately over maps, traffic, points of interest and routing. You'll turn open-ended product questions into well-defined scientific problems, validate solutions with rigorous evaluation, and work with AI and software engineers to bring them to production.

What you'll do: :
LLM–data interfaces: Research and design how LLMs access and reason over TomTom's data. This covers retrieval strategies for structured and geospatial data, tool and API designs that LLMs can use reliably, text-to-query approaches, and grounding techniques. 
 Data representation: Develop representations that make location data usable by AI, such as embeddings for geospatial entities, knowledge graphs and structured context formats. 
 Evaluation science: Define how we measure whether LLM-powered systems are right. Build benchmarks, factuality and hallucination metrics, and evaluation datasets for location-grounded tasks, and work with engineers to automate them. 
 Model research and development: Design, train and fine-tune ML and deep learning models, including LLMs, computer vision, time-series and graph-based methods, using large-scale, multi-modal data. 
 Problem framing: Work with product managers and stakeholders to identify high-impact opportunities and turn them into well-defined scientific problems with clear success metrics. 
 Research to production: Write production-quality code and work with AI and software engineers to take solutions from prototype to production, balancing accuracy, latency, cost and scalability. 
 State of the art: Keep up with the latest research in LLMs, retrieval and agentic systems, and adapt promising techniques to TomTom's problems. 
 Knowledge sharing: Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, and help build a strong scientific culture. External publications and patents are encouraged.
What you'll need::
Bachelor’s, Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics or a related quantitative field, or equivalent professional experience. 
 Strong foundations in machine learning, deep learning, statistics and optimization. 
 Hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX, and with the Python scientific stack (NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn). 
 Experience with one or more of: LLMs and generative AI, computer vision, time-series forecasting, graph neural networks, or reinforcement learning. 
 Proven ability to design experiments, define meaningful metrics and draw sound conclusions from data. 
 Experience working with large-scale datasets and distributed computing (e.g., Spark, Databricks, or cloud ML platforms on Azure, AWS or GCP). 
 Ability to write clean, maintainable code and to work with engineers toward production deployment. 
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical ideas to diverse audiences. 
 A track record of publications at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, KDD) is a plus. 
 Experience with geospatial, mapping, mobility or sensor data is a plus, but not required.
What we offer 

A competitive compensation package, of course.  

Time and resources to grow and develop, including a personal development budget and paid leave for learning days, as well as paid access to e-learning resources such as O’Reilly and LinkedIn Learning. 

Time to support life outside of work, with enhanced parental leave plus paid leave to care for loved ones and volunteer in local communities.  

Work flexibility, where TomTom’ers, in agreement with their manager and team, use both the office and home to focus, collaborate, learn and socialize. It’s all about getting the best out of both worlds – we ask TomTom’ers to come to the office two days a week, and the remaining three are free to be worked in either location.

Improve your home office with a setup budget and get extra support with a monthly allowance. 

Enjoy options to work from your home country and abroad for a set number of days each year, to visit family and friends, or to simply explore the world we’re mapping.  

Take the holidays you want with a competitive holiday plan, plus an extra day off to celebrate your birthday. 

Join annual events like our  Hackathon and DevDays to bring your ideas to life with talented teammates from around the world. 

Become a part of our inclusive global culture and have the chance to collaborate with a diverse community – we have over 80 nationalities at TomTom! 

Find out more about our global benefits and enjoy additional local benefits tailored to your location.

items.desc: About VAT Group At VAT, we change the world with vacuum solutions. As the world’s leading supplier of high-performance vacuum valves, we have been driving innovation for more than 60 years. With over 3,200 employees worldwide, we operate from our headquarters in Haag, Switzerland, with manufacturing sites in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania, as well as sales and service hubs around the world. We guided by our passions integrity, teamwork, customer centricity, and innovation – always working together as #oneVAT. Joining us means becoming part of a passionate, international team where your voice is heard, your ideas matter, and your career growth is supported. Your Challenge: Our products are key components in semiconductor processing equipment worldwide. To support the development of intelligent vacuum systems, we are looking for an intern who wants to combine hands-on experimentation with data science and machine learning. During your internship, you will investigate gas dynamics in a vacuum process chamber using advanced sensor technologies. You will contribute to the complete development cycle, including experimental planning, data collection, preprocessing, feature engineering, time-series modelling, and model validation. Your responsibilities will include: Become familiar with vacuum technology, gas dynamics, process chambers, and sensor systems. Support the setup and execution of experiments in our vacuum test laboratory. Plan experiments using a structured Design of Experiments approach. Collect and organize multivariate time-series data from different sensor technologies. Develop data-preprocessing workflows for synchronization, filtering, segmentation, outlier handling, and data-quality assessment. Explore the relationships between sensor signals, gas properties, and process conditions. Develop and compare data-driven methods for: Feature extraction Gas or process-condition classification Prediction and regression Process monitoring Event or anomaly detection Validate the developed methods using independent experiments and different operating conditions. Document experimental procedures, datasets, modelling methods, results, and limitations. Present your findings and potential next steps to engineers and researchers. Your Competencies: Currently pursuing an MSc degree in data science, machine learning, physics, mathematics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, control engineering, mechatronics, or a related field. Basic knowledge of data analysis, statistics, signal processing, or machine learning. Programming experience in Python or MATLAB. Interest in combining experimental work with data-driven modelling. Willingness to work hands-on with vacuum equipment, sensors, and data-acquisition systems. Systematic thinking and enthusiasm for developing innovative technical solutions. Ability to learn independently and collaborate in a multidisciplinary R&D environment. Good written and spoken English. Additional experience is a plus: Experience with time-series data, signal processing, or sensor-data analytics. Familiarity with scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow, MATLAB, or similar tools. Experience with Design of Experiments or laboratory measurements. Knowledge of feature engineering, model validation, or uncertainty estimation. Interest in vacuum technology, gas sensing, process control, or semiconductor manufacturing. What you will learn: Hands-on experience with vacuum systems and advanced sensor technologies. Experimental design and systematic data collection. Preprocessing and analysis of large multichannel sensor datasets. Time-series machine learning for real physical systems. Validation of data-driven models through laboratory experiments. Application knowledge in gas sensing and semiconductor equipment.

items.desc:
At Sonova R&D, we are not just developing hearing devices, we are shaping the future of hearing technology. At the heart of this transformation is the deployment and execution of neural networks on our next-generation embedded platform. This requires innovative tools and firmware infrastructure, giving you the opportunity to directly influence the performance of our products. 
 As our new Embedded Software Engineer, you will join a team bringing cutting-edge AI to our hearing devices. Your focus will be on developing the embedded software stack that forms the foundation of our next-generation hearing instruments, bridging the gap between AI and ultra-low-power embedded systems. 
 Are you excited to explore new technological territory and play a pivotal role in shaping Sonova’s edge AI capabilities? Join us and help rethink how embedded software is built to enhance people’s hearing experience and quality of life. 
 More about the role 
 Design, develop and maintain firmware for a deeply embedded platform operating under strict latency, memory, compute, and energy constraints. 
 Debug complex issues directly on target hardware and simulators. 
 Contribute to the integration and deployment process of neural networks in hearing-device firmware, working with AI and DSP experts. 
 Advise AI developers on tailoring neural networks to the embedded platform’s quantization, memory, compute, and power constraints. 
 Work with other engineering teams to develop prototypes, turn them into production-ready features, and integrate them into our system. 
 Ensure high software quality through clean-code practices, code reviews, testing, documentation, maintenance, and root-cause analysis. 
 More about you 
 Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. 
 Strong hands-on experience developing embedded software in C or C++, including object-oriented design, and practical experience using Python for development tools and automation. 
 Experience profiling embedded software to identify performance bottlenecks and optimizing execution time, memory usage, and energy consumption on resource-constrained systems. 
 Knowledge of embedded tooling (compiler, debugger, simulators, ...). 
 Experience developing and integrating software on resource-constrained embedded systems. 
 Fluent English, with strong written and verbal communication skills. 
 Familiarity with micro-NPU, deployment of neural networks and frameworks such as TensorFlow Lite, ONNX, TVM, or ExecuTorch, is an advantage. 
 Knowledge of audio or digital signal processing is an advantage. 
 Experience in bringing features to products is an advantage. 
 What we offer 
 As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans. 
 Why Join Sonova? 
 At Sonova, we offer more than just a job — we offer a chance to make an impact. You’ll join a collaborative, inclusive environment where your ideas matter and your leadership shapes how we serve our customers. With our modern office spaces, focus on employee development, and strong company values, you’ll be empowered to grow both personally and professionally. 
 Make an impact that resonates. Join Sonova and help us bring the world closer through better hearing.

items.desc: Your mission Our software catches every error on package leaflets and labels. You make it smarter with AI. You bring AI into Text Verification Tool (TVT) – reliably, securely and in a way our regulated customers can trust. TVT verifies text, images, barcodes and spelling deterministically – a mark of quality for pharma and medtech companies worldwide. As our first AI Engineer, you add AI-supported features on top of these checks, for example OCR and multilingual comparison. You work across our existing product teams rather than in a single team, and most of your time goes into TVT product features, another part is contributing to the AI adoption in the company. Evaluate and prioritise AI use cases for TVT together with Product Management Develop production-ready AI features for TVT (OCR, LLMs, NLP, computer vision) Implement, host, monitor and secure AI services in productive environments Support our product teams in integrating new AI features into product portfolio (Desktop, Web, SaaS) Make sure AI features can be validated and are testable and documented for regulated customers (e.g. GxP) Choose the technical approach, models, tools and frameworks within our architecture and security guidelines Automate internal processes for example in Sales, Support and Operations with AI Your profile Degree in Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, computer science, data science or a comparable field At least 3 years of professional experience, including hands-on experience with AI/ML or LLM applications in productive systems Strong programming skills and experience with cloud infrastructure and APIs Experience in implementing, hosting, monitoring and securing AI services Experience with document, text or image processing (NLP, OCR, computer vision) A pragmatic mindset: you think in terms of product value and can explain AI to non-technical colleagues Openness to the challenges that come with regulated industries – experience with GxP or medical device software is a plus Fluent English; German and knowledge of our technology stack (C++, C#) are a plus Why us? A key role with real responsibility: you shape how AI becomes part of TVT from the start A product with purpose: TVT helps make sure patients and consumers receive correct information Hybrid working: 3 days in the office, 2 days remote Workation possibility Spendit card after your probation period Fruit, coffee and water – they simply come with the job Team lunches and team events, both global and local A centrally located office About us Schlafender Hase develops TVT, a content verification platform for regulated industries. TVT verifies text, images, barcodes and spelling across different file formats, languages and layouts, ensuring error-free documentation before you print or publish. Today, more than 440 companies in pharma, medical devices, FMCG/CPG and crop science rely on it. Founded in Frankfurt in 2001 (our name – German for "sleeping hare" – started out as an internal code name), we are now a team of around 40 people, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main with an office in Montréal, Canada. With Maguar Capital joining as a new investor in 2026, we have entered our next phase of growth – and that is where you come in.
