items.desc: About us Greenly was founded in 2019 by Alexis, Matthieu and Arnaud with one mission: make carbon management as essential as financial management . In 2026, Greenly joined forces with the Nordic-founded company Normative. Today, we are a global leader in carbon accounting , proudly B-Corp certified and part of the French Tech 120. Our climate suite combines smart data collection with intuitive automation, helping companies measure, reduce, and report their emissions with ease — supported at every step by our in-house climate experts. We are now a team of 200+ people from 40+ nationalities , based in Paris, Stockholm, London, Barcelona, and New York. To date, we’ve tracked over 200 million tons of CO₂ through our platform. You tell us what we should be doing, including what we haven't thought of yet. GEO and AI video change every three months: we expect you to propose, test and make the call. You report to the VP Marketing and work with the Content & Brand, SEO, Product Marketing, Ads and Web teams. Your responsibilities 1. items.desc: Le contexte du poste Dans le cadre de notre expansion et pour répondre aux besoins de nos clients, nous recherchons un(e) Développeur(se) IA. Une opportunité unique pour intégrer une équipe dynamique, contribuer à des projets ambitieux et faire évoluer nos solutions d'intelligence artificielle. Vos missions Au sein de notre équipe de développement, vous serez en charge de : La conception et le développement de solutions basées sur l'IA Le pilotage de projets spécifiques de développement d'outils avec IA pour les PME L'intégration et le déploiement de modèles d'intelligence artificielle dans des applications existantes et nouvelles L'optimisation et la maintenance des algorithmes en production La veille technologique et la proposition d'innovations en IA La rédaction de documentation technique et le partage de connaissances au sein de l'équipe Votre environnement technique IA/ML : TensorFlow, PyTorch Langages : Python (principal), Node.js ou Java selon les projets Outils : Git, GitHub Infrastructure : API REST, Docker, Kubernetes Votre profil Vous disposez d'un diplôme Bac+5 en informatique, data science ou domaine connexe Vous maîtrisez Python et possédez de solides connaissances en mathématiques appliquées Vous avez une expérience concrète du déploiement de modèles IA en production Vous êtes autonome, force de proposition et capable de mener des projets de bout en bout Vous possédez d'excellentes capacités de communication et appréciez le travail en équipe Qui sommes-nous ? Acteam-IT, bien plus qu’un cabinet d’expertise IT, est le catalyseur de transformations digitales, un architecte de solutions techniques et humaines. Notre histoire a débuté en 2014 par un engagement : celui d'accompagner nos clients dans l'atteinte de leurs objectifs. Qu'il s'agisse de développement, d'administration d'infrastructures, de testing ou de gestion de projets, notre palette de solutions est aussi diversifiée que les défis auxquels nos clients font face. Chez ACTEAM-IT, chaque projet est une aventure, chaque client un partenaire pour qui nous déployons des solutions sur mesure. Au cœur de notre démarche, il y a des valeurs fondamentales : l’expertise, l’exigence et la solidarité. Chaque collaboration est bâtie sur la confiance et le respect mutuel. Le tout, nous permet de créer des liens durables avec nos collaborateurs, nos clients et partenaires. Aussi, entreprise engagée et inclusive, nous avons un attachement profond à la diversité et l’équité. Cela se traduit par notre encouragement à recevoir et considérer les candidatures de tous horizons et tous profils. items.desc: Creating knowledge. Making a difference. Shaping the future. This is what the University of Münster stands for as one of the strongest research-oriented universities in Germany and one of the largest employers in the region. Every day, over 7,000 employees devote themselves to cutting-edge research and excellent teaching. We share more than a workplace. We share the desire to make a real impact – regionally and internationally. Our day-to-day work is distinguished by diversity, openness and space to pursue one’s ideas. Become a part of our team – in academia, a technical or manual trade, or administration. The Department for Quantum Technology of the Faculty of Physics at the University of Münster, Germany, is seeking to fill the position of a Doctoral Research Associate Wissenschaftliche r Mitarbeiter in (salary level E 13 TV-L, 67%) at the earliest possible date. We are offering a fixed-term part-time position (67%) for 3 years. Full-time employees are required to teach 4 hours per week during the semester. Your tasks: Participate in the research activities of the Foundations of Quantum Theory Group at the Department of Quantum Technology, including the planning and execution of scientific projects in the fields of quantum information theory and foundations of quantum theory. Contribute to the development and implementation of collaborative research efforts with group members, students, and international research partners. Publication of original research results in leading scientific journals and presentation of these results at international conferences. Participation in the teaching activities of the Department of Quantum Technology. The position is associated with the completion of a doctoral research project (PhD). Our expectations: A graduate degree (German Diplom or master's degree) in physics is required. Proficiency in spoken and written English is strongly desired. Knowledge in the theoretical foundations of quantum physics and quantum information theory. Research experience in the mathematical structure of quantum theory. You should be team-oriented, have strong communication and organisational skills, scientific writing and presentation skills, and the ability to work independently. Advantages for you: Appreciation, commitment, openness and respect – values which are important to us. Our broad range of diverse work-time models offers great flexibility – also when working from home. If you have family members or young children in your care, our offers concrete support to help you balance your private and professional responsibilities. As an educational institution, we are deeply committed to offering opportunities tailored to your individual needs. From A – Z, Aikido to Zumba, our ensure a healthy work-life balance. As a university employee, you are entitled to numerous benefits afforded to public servants, e.g. an attractive company pension scheme (), an and a position that is shielded from economic fluctuations. The University of Münster strongly supports . We welcome all applicants regardless of sex, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion or worldview, disability, age, sexual orientation or gender identity. We are committed to creating family-friendly working conditions. We actively encourage applications by women. Women with equivalent qualifications and academic achievements will be preferentially considered unless these are outweighed by reasons which necessitate the selection of another candidate. If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Matthias Kleinmann ). Are you interested? Then we look forward to receiving your application by 2026-11-20 via our online application form. Vanaf Amsterdam Centraal, Utrecht Centraal en Gouda ben je in minder dan 20 minuten bij ons. Met de auto? Je kunt gratis parkeren. Wij werken werken hybride, minimaal 50% van de werktijd vanaf kantoor, maandag is onze kantoordag. Wat breng je mee? Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar relevante werkervaring als data scientist met complexe en grote data- en taalmodellen. Dit blijkt zowel uit wetenschappelijke publicaties als toepassingen ervan op organisatieniveau. Je werkt graag zelfstandig, maar zoekt ook actief de samenwerking op met collega’s om tot een goed resultaat te komen. Je bent in staat om complexe (technische) vraagstukken op te lossen en vind het leuk om met je inhoudelijke kennis anderen te begeleiden bij uitdagende projecten. Daarnaast: Heb je een Master of Science (MSc), bij voorkeur (bijna) gepromoveerd in computer science of een andere relevante studierichting. Heb je ervaring met het bewerken en analyseren van grote datasets en het bouwen en beheren van complexe datamodellen en AI-toepassingen. Heb je relevante wetenschappelijke publicaties op het gebied van computer science of aanverwante vakgebieden. Heb je ervaring met de ontwikkeling en invoering van AI-modellen en het verbeteren van bestaande data-infrastructuur. Kun je werken met een of meer van de volgende technieken en systemen: Python, Large Language Models, Machine Learning libraries (pytorch), Microsoft Azure, Linux omgeving en Microsoft Azure. Heb je kennis van kwaliteitsstandaarden, relevante wet- en regelgeving en actuele technische ontwikkelingen op het gebied van AI. Heb je ervaring met het begeleiden van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, het analyseren van onderzoeksresultaten en het schriftelijk vastleggen daarvan. Kun je complexe vraagstukken zelfstandig oplossen, werk je gestructureerd en kun je goed plannen en organiseren. Communiceer je helder en werk je graag samen met collega’s uit verschillende vakgebieden. Heb je affiniteit met suïcidepreventie en wil je met jouw kennis bijdragen aan de ondersteuning van onze hulpverleners. Hoe ziet je agenda eruit? Wie zijn wij? 113 Zelfmoordpreventie streeft naar een land waarin niemand eenzaam en radeloos sterft door zelfdoding. Uit onderzoek weten we dat mensen vaak niet dood willen, maar geen andere uitweg meer zien. 113 is in 2009 opgericht om wel een andere uitweg te bieden door het onderwerp bespreekbaar te maken. 113 heeft een hulplijn; mensen met suïcidale gedachten kunnen dag en nacht anoniem bellen of chatten. Als nationale organisatie voor suïcidepreventie onderzoekt, ontwikkelt en implementeert 113, samen met vele andere organisaties, interventies en campagnes om het aantal zelfdodingen in Nederland omlaag te krijgen. In de zestien jaar dat onze organisatie bestaat, hebben we taboes rondom zelfdoding helpen verminderen en zowel de zorgsector als overheidsinstanties, gemeentes, scholen, families, naasten en uiteraard de hulpvragers hierover geïnformeerd en ondersteund. We zijn trots op wat we hebben bereikt in ons relatief korte bestaan, maar we zijn er nog niet. Wij zijn op zoek naar een Dataspecialist AI. Krijg jij energie van het analyseren van complexe data en het ontwikkelen van slimme AI-oplossingen? En wil je met jouw kennis bijdragen aan het voorkomen van zelfdoding? Bij 113 krijg je de ruimte om onderzoek te doen en AI-toepassingen te ontwikkelen die onze hulplijn helpen verbeteren. Zo verbind je technologie en onderzoek aan een maatschappelijk doel. Wat ga je doen? Als Dataspecialist AI werk je aan belangrijk onderzoek om de 113 Hulplijn klaar te maken voor de toekomst en met nieuwe inzichten de hulpverlening te verbeteren. Je gaat zelf aan de slag met het modelleren en analyseren van complexe data uit onze hulplijn en speelt een belangrijke rol bij evaluatie- en implementatieonderzoek. Samen met een GZ-psycholoog en een senior onderzoeker ben je verantwoordelijk voor de ontwikkeling en invoering van AI-tools die onze hulpverleners kunnen ondersteunen. Je onderzoekt hoe deze toepassingen in de praktijk werken en hoe ze het beste aansluiten bij hun behoeften. Je houdt je onder andere bezig met: Data modelleren en analyseren . Je werkt met …

items.desc: I Posten Bring jobber vi hver dag med å utvikle løsninger som gjør hverdagen enklere og verden litt mindre. Virkelig gode løsninger oppstår når vi klarer å bruke data og maskinlæring til å løse reelle problemer – og få dem helt ut i produksjon. Derfor styrker vi nå vårt data- og maskinlæringsmiljø med en data scientist som vil være med på å utvikle og produksjonssette løsninger som skaper verdi. I Teknologi og sikkerhet blir du en del av sterke fagmiljøer innen teknologi, produktutvikling, data, AI og sikkerhet. Vi jobber tett sammen med forretnings- og driftsmiljøer i konsernet for å levere verdi og resultater for både kolleger og kunder. Området har ansvar for alt fra teknologistrategi, plattformutvikling og arkitektur til digital produktutvikling og sikker og stabil drift. Sammen bygger vi løsninger som ikke blir liggende i en skuff, men som brukes hver dag. Om avdelingen Du blir en del av avdelingen for data og maskinlæring bestående av data scientists, ML/data-ingeniører og dataanalytikere. Kulturen er preget av: Nysgjerrighet og vilje til å lære Åpenhet og samarbeid En pragmatisk tilnærming der vi tester, diskuterer og justerer underveis Vi har ikke alltid fasiten på forhånd – og nettopp derfor er det spennende å jobbe hos oss. Dine viktigste arbeidsoppgaver: Som data scientist hos oss jobber du ende-til-ende med maskinlæringsløsninger – fra idé og analyse til produksjon og videre drift. Du vil blant annet: Jobbe tett med forretningen for å finne og prioritere muligheter der data og ML kan skape verdi Gjøre uklare behov om til konkrete problemstillinger, og vurdere når ML ikke er riktig svar Utvikle, trene og evaluere maskinlæringsmodeller Sette modeller i produksjon og følge dem opp over tid Bygge og bruke datapipelines for analyse og modellering Presentere funn og anbefalinger for ledere og fagfolk uten teknisk bakgrunn Hvem ser vi etter? Vi ser etter deg som har erfaring med å levere maskinlæringsløsninger hele veien fra idé til produksjon. Du har: Minst 3 års erfaring med ML/AI Levert flere ML/AI-løsninger ende-til-ende Erfaring med å drive frem løsninger sammen med forretningen, og med å vise hvilken verdi de har skapt Solid kompetanse innen dataanalyse, eksperimentering og modellutvikling Erfaring med produksjonssetting, monitorering og vedlikehold av modeller God erfaring med Python og relevante ML-biblioteker (f.eks. PyTorch, scikit-learn, pandas, polars) Erfaring med skyplattformer Svært gode muntlige og skriftlige ferdigheter i norsk, svensk eller dansk Det er en fordel om du også har erfaring med MLOps-verktøy, CI/CD, Databricks, Spark, SQL og Terraform. For at du skal lykkes og trives hos oss Har mer fokus på problemet som skal løses og verdien som skal skapes enn på hvilken modell som skal brukes Trives i dialog med folk i forretningen og klarer å forklare komplekse ting på en enkel måte Er nysgjerrig på virksomheten og søker stadig å lære mer om den Tar ansvar for at løsningene faktisk fungerer, også over tid Deler kunnskap og gjerne bygger videre på det andre har laget, i stedet for å starte fra bunne Hva kan vi tilby deg? Store datamengder og høyt potensial for automatisering og verdiskaping Et sterkt fagmiljø med dyktige og hjelpsomme kollegaer En moderne dataplattform tilpasset ML/AI-utvikling Påvirke hvordan vi jobber med data og maskinlæring Fleksibel arbeidshverdag og hybrid løsning Arbeidsplass i Posthuset med Oslos beste utsikt! Konkurransedyktige betingelser og gode forsikrings- og pensjonsordninger Er dette er deg, eller er du klar for å bli denne medarbeideren? Da tilbyr vi deg en stilling der du alltid vil være i utvikling og på vei til nye steder og ansvarsområder. Hos oss vil du få rom til å forme din egen hverdag og karriere. I Posten og Bring tror vi på at når menneskene som jobber her utvikler seg, kan vi som konsern gjøre det samme. Mangfoldet i Posten Bring er vår styrke, og vi mener forskjellighet blant medarbeidere er nøkkelen til nytenkning og innovasjon. Vi ønsker oss derfor et stort mangfold blant søkere. Vår visjon «Vi gjør hverdagen enklere og verden mindre» forteller hva vi strekker oss mot, og ønsker å oppnå for våre kunder. Våre verdier «tar ansvar», «spiller på lag» og «vil mer» gjenspeiler at vi er til å stole på og setter menneskene først. Vi vet at nøkkelen til å lykkes med våre ambisjoner er kompetente og engasjerte medarbeidere.

items.desc: Position Details Department of Immunology and Immunotherapy, College of Medicine and Health Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £37,369 to £46,970, with potential progression once in post to £49,798 Grade 7 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to December 2030 Closing date: 22 nd November 2026 Background A post-doctoral research fellow position is available in the Fungal Immunology Group within the Institute of Immunology & Immunotherapy, College of Medical & Dental Sciences, University of Birmingham , led by Prof Rebecca Drummond. This role is to create and contribute to the creation of knowledge by undertaking a specified range of activities within an established research programme and/or specific research project. We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed scientist to join our project team, which is aiming to better understand organ-specific immune responses against fungal pathogens. The successful candidate will make extensive use of a range of in vivo models of fungal infection and will have access to the wide range of transgenic tools and in vivo immunology techniques established in the Drummond lab. The candidate’s research will focus on characterising immune cells, especially tissue-resident subsets, and how these interact during fungal infection within the central nervous system. This is an exciting opportunity to investigate regulation of antifungal immunity in vivo. As an example of the work the team has previously published, please see Mohamed et al, Nature Communications 2023 and Hain et al, Nature Communications 2025. The position would ideally suit someone with an immunology background with a strong interest in fungal pathogens. The candidate will be based in Drummond lab, which is part of a larger international consortium, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The candidate will join meetings and meet other team members based in Denmark and Uganda. All groups will work closely together during the project. There will be opportunity for additional training for the successful applicant with our collaborators to develop a wide range of technical expertise in immunology, neuroscience and microbiology. Funding for the position is available for 3 years, with possibility of extension. The lab is located within the Institute of Immunology & Immunotherapy at the University of Birmingham, where a collaborative environment exists, rich in immunologists with a range of complimentary research interests. We also closely work with our colleagues in the Institute of Microbiology & Infection who specialise in fungal biology and drug resistance. The candidate should demonstrate a good understanding of immunology and medical microbiology and have excellent written and oral communication skills. They will be expected to help develop new techniques within the laboratory, help supervise project/undergraduate students, and present their data regularly at internal lab meetings and external conferences. All applicants should be ideally proficient with in vivo immunology, flow cytometry, basic tissue culture and molecular biology techniques. Prior experience with microscopy (particularly confocal) and human cell culture would be advantageous. Applicants should be able to demonstrate prior research success; for example, through publications/pre-prints, presentations at conferences and relevant academic prizes/travel awards. items.desc: Job Details Section Human Genetics & Genomic Medicine Location: Southampton General Hospital Salary £37,369 to £45,641 Per Annum Full Time Fixed Term until 23/08/2028 Closing Date: Friday 04 December 2026 Interview Date To be confirmed Reference 3547626AF The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Southampton invites applications for a full-time, fixed-term Research Fellow to join Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar’s interdisciplinary precision-diabetes research programme investigating the heterogeneity of obesity and its impact on type 2 diabetes and related complications. Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate why individuals with similar levels of adiposity differ substantially in their risk of developing type 2 diabetes and its complications. Working alongside genetic epidemiologists, clinicians and data scientists, you will apply statistical genetics approaches, including genome-wide association studies (GWAS), Mendelian randomisation and post-GWAS analyses, to identify genetic determinants, investigate causal relationships and uncover biological pathways linking obesity to metabolic disease. As a Research Fellow, you will: Investigate the genetic and biological heterogeneity of obesity and its relationships with type 2 diabetes and related complications. Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of obesity-related traits, adiposity phenotypes and metabolic outcomes using large-scale genetic and epidemiological datasets. Apply Mendelian randomisation and complementary genetic epidemiological approaches to investigate potential causal relationships between different aspects of adiposity, type 2 diabetes and its complications. Perform post-GWAS analyses, including fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation and pathway enrichment, to identify genes and biological mechanisms underlying obesity-related metabolic risk. Investigate the genetic determinants of different obesity-related phenotypes and their associations with metabolic and cardiometabolic outcomes. Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings. Collaborate with multidisciplinary researchers across genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, genomics, clinical medicine and data science. You will have opportunities to develop your expertise in statistical genetics and genetic epidemiology, contribute to innovative analytical approaches and build your publication record within an internationally collaborative research environment. You will have: A PhD in genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, bioinformatics, biostatistics, computational biology or a closely related discipline. Experience analysing large-scale genetic, genomic or epidemiological datasets, ideally including UK Biobank. Strong computational skills, including proficiency in R and/or Python and experience working in Linux-based computing environments. Knowledge of GWAS methodology, including genetic data quality control, association testing and interpretation of results. Knowledge of Mendelian randomisation methods, including instrumental variable assumptions, sensitivity analyses and interpretation of findings. Knowledge of post-GWAS approaches, such as fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation, colocalisation or pathway analyses. An understanding of genetic epidemiology and statistical methods used to investigate the genetic architecture and biological mechanisms of complex diseases. Evidence of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications. Excellent analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams. Experience in obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiometabolic disease research or the genetic analysis of adiposity-related traits would be advantageous. At Southampton, you will join a supportive, internationally connected research environment at the forefront of genetic epidemiology, data science and metabolic disease research. We offer: Access to large-scale genetic and biomedical datasets, high-performance computing infrastructure and secure analytical environments. Opportunities to investigate the genetic and biological mechanisms underlying obesity heterogeneity, type 2 diabetes and its complications. Collaboration with leading researchers across human genetics, genomics, epidemiology, clinical medicine and computational science. Opportunities for high-quality publications, scientific conferences, professional development and career progression. items.title: GPU Kernel and Performance Engineer
items.card: You will join a small research team and turn new model designs into efficient GPU code, then measure how much time and memory traffic they cost on real hardware. Our training runs on NVIDIA GPUs, and we also expect to work with other AI accelerators, so there is scope to learn new chips and programming models as the work develops. We care more about how well you understand hardware and memory than about ML research
items.desc: CommonAI CIC is a non-profit membership organisation, founded on a belief in collaborative engineering for the safe and responsible development of foundational AI technologies. A place where AI startups, enterprises large and small, public sector bodies and academia can share resources and knowledge, to codevelop and grow businesses, fast. We are led by experienced founders, investors and engineers who believe that collaborative engineering drives faster AI innovation and are backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. The Opportunity We are seeking a GPU Kernel and Performance Engineer to make our research models run fast on real hardware, primarily NVIDIA GPUs. Our research team works on reducing the complexity of large language models while retaining their performance. Some of this work informs our analyses of the trade-offs between training and inference costs when scaling inference workloads. The work runs on the UK's national AI supercomputers and on our own compute nodes. You will join a small research team and turn new model designs into efficient GPU code, then measure how much time and memory traffic they cost on real hardware. Our training runs on NVIDIA GPUs, and we also expect to work with other AI accelerators, so there is scope to learn new chips and programming models as the work develops. We care more about how well you understand hardware and memory than about ML research credentials. What You'll Do Write and optimise CUDA and Triton kernels on NVIDIA GPUs for sparse and structured model components, including block-sparse matrix operations and attention variants. Adapt and extend open-source kernels, such as FlashAttention-style and block-sparse attention, to new model designs. Profile training and inference to find where time and memory traffic go, using tools such as NVIDIA Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute. Optimise for the GH200's memory hierarchy on Isambard-AI and for our own GPU nodes. Build tools that measure data movement per generated token, and check analytic cost models against hardware measurements. Test every kernel against reference implementations before it runs at scale. Work with our training infrastructure engineer to raise training throughput, and with researchers to make new designs fast enough to test. Evaluate how our models map onto other AI accelerators, such as TPUs and dataflow, wafer-scale and compute-in-memory architectures, and port key components to them where it is useful. Contribute improvements back to open-source projects where possible. Requirements Proven experience writing and optimising GPU kernels in CUDA or Triton, ideally on recent NVIDIA architectures. A strong understanding of GPU architecture and memory hierarchies (e.g. shared memory, HBM bandwidth, memory coalescing, occupancy). Hands-on experience profiling and optimising performance with tools such as NVIDIA Nsight Compute or Nsight Systems. Strong Python and C/C++. A rigorous approach to testing numerical code (e.g. comparison against reference implementations, mixed-precision error). Openness to learning new hardware architectures and programming models, often from limited documentation. A strong enthusiasm for using LLMs, coding assistants, and agents as core tools in your own software development process. We also value: Experience with attention kernels (e.g. FlashAttention) or sparse kernels (e.g. block sparsity, mixture-of-experts routing). Experience with NVIDIA Hopper features (e.g. TMA, warpgroup matrix instructions) or libraries such as CUTLASS and CuTe. Experience with multi-GPU communication (e.g. NCCL, NVLink). An understanding of LLM inference performance (e.g. KV caching, memory-bound decoding, quantisation). Experience with other AI accelerators (e.g. AMD GPUs, TPUs with JAX and Pallas, or dataflow, wafer-scale and compute-in-memory architectures). Experience with compiler stacks for AI hardware (e.g. MLIR, XLA, TVM). A background in computer architecture, HPC, graphics or game engine programming. Experience with hardware/software co-design, or with hardware performance modelling and simulation. Contributions to performance-critical open-source projects (e.g. PyTorch, Triton, JAX, vLLM). Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package and pension Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential people from across the tech sector, financial services, and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes' walk away from Cambridge train station CommonAI CIC is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace.

items.desc: Research Engineer (f/m/d) in the field of Translational Surgical Oncology The position is available from November 1st, 2026, on a full-time or part-time basis, and is initially limited to 24 months. Remuneration will be based on the applicable provisions of the institution's collective bargaining agreement and, subject to the candidate's personal qualifications, may be assigned to salary grade U13 . The institute for Translational Surgical Oncology (TSO) at the NCT Dresden conducts research in the area of computer- and robot-assisted surgery. Our focus lies on surgical navigation, robotics, simulation and training. Our group develops AI systems that fuse live endoscopic video streams with preoperative 3D CT or MRI data and display the results in an augmented-reality fashion to the surgeons. The AI methods perform tasks such as segmentation, depth-estimation, feature tracking and registration in real‑time. To control these systems, we are building semi‑automatic methods with intuitive user‑interfaces that are ready to be operated inside the OR. In this context, the current role would aid with the translation of AI‑systems into the operating room. This requires active research topics such as endoscopic video processing, camera calibration, real‑time computing and phantom validation in our experimental operating room. The candidate would help in the translation of current research topics into clean, high‑quality medical applications, which includes the documentation according to requirements by regulatory authorities (no prior knowledge required) and they would help PhD students integrate new AI solutions into the pipeline. Depending on the candidate's preferences, further topics can include rendering, augmented reality and registration, as well as student supervision. Il emploie plus de 11 500 professionnels dont 1 700 médecins sur 3 sites : site Nord (hôpital Michallon et hôpital Couple-Enfant, site Sud, site de Voiron). Il dispose d’un plateau technique performant et dispense des soins hautement spécialisés. Plus de 100 corps de métiers se côtoient chaque jour pour contribuer directement ou indirectement à sa vocation de soin, d’enseignement, de recherche et de prévention. Les 3 Missions Essentielles Du CHUGA Sont Soigner Former Chercher Le Poste Contexte du poste Le CHU Grenoble Alpes (CHUGA) est un établissement public de santé situé à Grenoble au cœur des Alpes. Premier Trauma Center de France, il regroupe de nombreuses spécialités médicales, une activité recherche reconnue, ainsi qu’un entrepôt de données de santé (EDS) PREDIMED, destiné à réutiliser des données récoltées dans le cadre de la prise en charge des patients, notamment, à des fins de recherche. La Cellule d’Ingénierie des Données de Santé du CHUGA (CIDS), regroupant l’Entrepôt de Données de Santé1 (EDS) et les data scientists du Centre d’Investigation Clinique - Innovation Technologique² (CIC-IT) est une structure de recherche du CHUGA. Sa mission est centrée sur l’extraction et l’analyse de données de santé pour l’évaluation des technologies de santé innovantes. Le CHUGA a été lauréat d’un appel à projet visant à l’organisation d’une compétition en sciences des données3 (data challenge). Cette compétition sera ouverte via une plateforme à des compétiteurs extérieurs au CHUGA. La problématique clinique proposée aux participants portera sur la prédiction du besoin de transfusion per-opératoire à partir des données de santé disponibles en consultation d’anesthésie. Pour cela une base de données rétrospective multicentrique entre le CHUGA et les Hospices Civils de Lyon (HCL), partenaire du projet, devra être constituée à partir des entrepôts de données de santé des centres. Elle devra ensuite être anonymisée par des techniques de génération de données synthétiques afin de pouvoir être mise en libre accès, conformément au RGPD. Placé sous la responsabilité du responsable de la CIDS et en lien avec les porteurs du projet, l’Ingénieur.e Data Science recruté(e) aura pour mission de collecter et anonymiser les données nécessaires au projet et mettre en place la plateforme de compétition sur un méso-centre de calcul. Ce travail sera réalisé avec l’appui des experts anesthésistes-réanimateurs des centres participants et des partenaires du projet apportant leurs expertises complémentaires en données massives et analyse (laboratoire TIMC4), confidentialité des données (INRIA, équipe Privatics5) et mise en place de plateformes de data challenge (GRICAD6). Missions principales Élaboration des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle Concevoir, mettre en œuvre et qualifier les algorithmes de génération de données synthétiques afin d’anonymiser les données structurées et non-structurées (traitement automatique du langage) ; Concevoir et mettre en œuvre le protocole d’évaluation de la performance des modèles et de l’anonymisation des données mobilisant les métriques adéquates ; Documenter des modèles (GIT) ; Capitaliser et documenter des résultats et des méthodes d’évaluation de la qualité des modèles. Industrialisation des modèles d’intelligence artificielle dans les applications Industrialiser les modèles de génération de données pour de futurs usages (autres data challenges, offre de services de l’EDS) ; Prendre part aux vérifications lors des mises en production ; Définir les règles de gestion pour la maintenance des modèles. Veille technologique sur les outils de data science Effectuer une veille sur les nouvelles technologies et solutions logicielles de data science ; Rechercher et expérimenter de nouvelles méthodes de modélisation et de data science. Extraction et structuration des données Concevoir et modéliser le jeu de données, avec les variables pertinentes à introduire dans les modèles ; Collaborer étroitement avec les ingénieurs Data de l’EDS pour qualifier et maitriser la qualité des données tout au long de leur traitement ; Collaborer étroitement avec les experts de l’information médicale et les experts des disciplines médicales pour valider la sélection et les filtres des variables du jeu de données . Divers Concevoir, rédiger une documentation technique ; Être force de propositions à des problématiques (techniques, …, autres). Profil Recherché Profil requis pour ce poste Titulaire d’un Diplôme Bac+5 et/ou d’une thèse en Informatique, Mathématiques appliquées ou toute discipline en lien avec la science des données avec un fort attrait pour le secteur de la santé et de la recherche. Expérience requise en traitement automatique du langage (TAL, NLP), en génération de données synthétiques et autres techniques d’anonymisation des données. items.desc: Position: Operations Research/Data Scientist Department: Technology Location: Berlin Ready for a challenge? Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience. Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe. About This Role As an Operations Research/Data Scientist on the Assignments team, you will help build, maintain, and scale the algorithms/models that power our global delivery network. In this role, you will work at the intersection of mathematical optimization, machine learning, and software engineering. You will collaborate closely with senior scientists and software engineers to translate business rules into robust mathematical formulations, build predictive models that inform dynamic parameters, and ship production-ready Python services. You will take ownership of discrete algorithmic components, run historical simulations, and help monitor live system performance to ensure our assignment engine remains fast, reliable, and cost-effective. These are some of the key components to the position: Solid working knowledge of combinatorial optimization concepts, particularly Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) formulations, Vehicle Routing Problems (VRP), and heuristic search methods. Practical experience applying statistical methods and machine learning algorithms (e.g., supervised learning, unsupervised learning) to generate inputs, estimate operational states, or refine optimization parameters. Strong proficiency in Python with a solid grasp of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), design patterns, type hinting, and writing clean, testable, and modular code. Knowledge of Java is a plus. Hands-on experience with Python optimization modeling libraries or solver APIs (e.g., Pyomo, PuLP, OR-Tools) and familiarity with commercial or open-source solvers (e.g., Gurobi, SCIP, HiGHS). Practical experience deploying models or algorithmic services to production, with an understanding of runtime constraints, latency, and setting up basic telemetry to monitor solution quality and performance. Hands-on experience querying relational databases and data warehouses with SQL to pull, clean, and validate data for model training, benchmarking, and offline simulation. Good working knowledge of standard development practices, including version control with Git, automated testing (unit/integration tests), Docker containerization, and participating in code reviews. Experience in the logistics and last-mile delivery domain is highly beneficial. What will you bring to the team? A curious, analytical approach to solving operational problems under real-world constraints (e.g., delivery windows, driver availability, travel times). Growth mindset with an eagerness to learn production OR & DS techniques, system architecture, and trade-offs from experienced peers. Ability to test hypotheses rigorously using historical trace data, evaluating results through clear metric tracking. Collaborative communication style, comfortable explaining model logic, edge cases, and trade-offs to engineers, data scientists, and product managers. Pragmatic mindset focused on shipping clean, working solutions rather than over-engineering. At JET, This Is How We Play Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment. Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side. At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again. Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition. Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day. What else are we delivering? Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET journeys.

items.desc: Your mission Our software catches every error on package leaflets and labels. You make it smarter with AI. You bring AI into Text Verification Tool (TVT) – reliably, securely and in a way our regulated customers can trust. TVT verifies text, images, barcodes and spelling deterministically – a mark of quality for pharma and medtech companies worldwide. As our first AI Engineer, you add AI-supported features on top of these checks, for example OCR and multilingual comparison. You work across our existing product teams rather than in a single team, and most of your time goes into TVT product features, another part is contributing to the AI adoption in the company. Evaluate and prioritise AI use cases for TVT together with Product Management Develop production-ready AI features for TVT (OCR, LLMs, NLP, computer vision) Implement, host, monitor and secure AI services in productive environments Support our product teams in integrating new AI features into product portfolio (Desktop, Web, SaaS) Make sure AI features can be validated and are testable and documented for regulated customers (e.g. GxP) Choose the technical approach, models, tools and frameworks within our architecture and security guidelines Automate internal processes for example in Sales, Support and Operations with AI Your profile Degree in Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, computer science, data science or a comparable field At least 3 years of professional experience, including hands-on experience with AI/ML or LLM applications in productive systems Strong programming skills and experience with cloud infrastructure and APIs Experience in implementing, hosting, monitoring and securing AI services Experience with document, text or image processing (NLP, OCR, computer vision) A pragmatic mindset: you think in terms of product value and can explain AI to non-technical colleagues Openness to the challenges that come with regulated industries – experience with GxP or medical device software is a plus Fluent English; German and knowledge of our technology stack (C++, C#) are a plus Why us? A key role with real responsibility: you shape how AI becomes part of TVT from the start A product with purpose: TVT helps make sure patients and consumers receive correct information Hybrid working: 3 days in the office, 2 days remote Workation possibility Spendit card after your probation period Fruit, coffee and water – they simply come with the job Team lunches and team events, both global and local A centrally located office About Us Schlafender Hase develops TVT, a content verification platform for regulated industries. TVT verifies text, images, barcodes and spelling across different file formats, languages and layouts, ensuring error-free documentation before you print or publish. Today, more than 440 companies in pharma, medical devices, FMCG/CPG and crop science rely on it. Founded in Frankfurt in 2001 (our name – German for "sleeping hare" – started out as an internal code name), we are now a team of around 40 people, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main with an office in Montréal, Canada. With Maguar Capital joining as a new investor in 2026, we have entered our next phase of growth – and that is where you come in.

items.desc: A position exists for a Research Assistant in the Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, to work on an exciting new project developing minimally invasive implantable neural probes for brain interfacing. The project will involve the design, evaluation and characterisation of advanced neural interfaces, supported by computational modelling to investigate their electrical performance and safety. The post holder will be located in the Department of Engineering, The Institute for Biomedical Innovation, 11 JJ Thomson Avenue, Cambridge, CB3 0FF. The key responsibilities and duties are to contribute to the design and evaluation of implantable neural interfaces; undertake electrical characterisation and computational simulations using tools such as Sim4Life or COMSOL; analyse and interpret experimental and simulation results; collaborate with researchers working on device fabrication and electrophysiology; maintain accurate research records; and contribute to research reports, publications and presentations. The skills, qualifications and experience required to perform the role are an undergraduate degree in Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Physics or a related discipline, with a postgraduate qualification in neural engineering, bioelectronics or a related field desirable. Applicants should demonstrate knowledge of neural interfaces, implantable bioelectronic devices or related biomedical technologies, together with relevant research experience in device design, testing, electrical characterisation or electrophysiology. Familiarity with computational modelling tools such as Sim4Life or COMSOL is also essential. The successful candidate will have good analytical, problem solving and communication skills, and the ability to work effectively within an interdisciplinary research team. Salary Ranges: £33,662 - £36,320 Fixed-term: The funding is for 12 months or through until 30 November 2027, whichever of these comes soonest. items.desc: Per un gruppo internazionale leader nello sviluppo di soluzioni di visione artificiale, intelligenza artificiale e automazione industriale, ricerchiamo un AI Engineer (m, f, x), da inserire in una Business Unit dedicata allo sviluppo e all'industrializzazione di soluzioni AI per il settore industriale. La persona entrerà a far parte di un team altamente specializzato e, operando a stretto contatto con le funzioni R&D ed Engineering, sarà dedicata principalmente al deployment e all'industrializzazione di soluzioni AI sviluppate dal team di Ricerca. La risorsa seguirà le diverse fasi di implementazione, dalla raccolta dei requisiti tecnici fino al rilascio e alla validazione presso il cliente, con particolare attenzione alle applicazioni di Computer Vision in ambienti industriali. Monitorare le pipeline di training, testing e validazione dei modelli, contribuendo all'ottimizzazione delle performance. Buona familiarità con i processi di sviluppo, training, testing e validazione dei modelli di Intelligenza Artificiale. Laurea in Informatica, Ingegneria Informatica, Artificial Intelligence o discipline tecnico-scientifiche affini. Ottima conoscenza della lingua inglese. items.desc: Company Description RAISEBOX is a Physical AI R&D company focused on training humanoid robots for real-world industrial work. The team develops advanced dexterous manipulation, navigation, and whole-body control skills for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. These capabilities are learned from human teleoperation demonstrations and high-fidelity simulation environments such as MuJoCo, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, and GR00T, and then transferred to the physical robot. Located in Taguspark, Oeiras, Portugal, RAISEBOX offers a cutting-edge environment for professionals interested in robotics, AI, and applied research in industrial settings. Role Description The Humanoid Robotics and Physical AI Engineer will work on-site in Lisbon (Taguspark, Oeiras) in a full-time capacity, collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary R&D team. Day-to-day responsibilities include designing, implementing, and testing policies for humanoid robot control, perception, and learning, with a focus on dexterous manipulation and navigation in industrial environments. The role involves developing and integrating machine learning models, including neural networks, with robotic hardware and simulation platforms, as well as building robust software components and tools to support teleoperation, data collection, and sim-to-real transfer. The engineer will debug and optimize code, run experiments in simulation and on real robots, analyze performance metrics, and document results to inform iterative improvements. Participation in code reviews, technical discussions, and joint problem-solving sessions will be key, along with maintaining safe and reliable operation of humanoid systems in the lab. Qualifications Strong foundation in Computer Science and related fields, with experience applying Pattern Recognition techniques to real-world problems. Hands-on experience with Neural Networks and modern machine learning frameworks for control, perception, or reinforcement learning in robotics. Proficiency in Software Development, including clean coding practices, version control (e.g., Git), and debugging in languages such as Python and C++. Familiarity with Natural Language Processing (NLP) and its integration with robotic or interactive systems is a plus. Experience with robotic simulation tools (e.g., MuJoCo, Isaac Lab) and sim-to-real transfer methods is highly beneficial. Background in robotics, control systems, or physical AI, preferably with humanoid or legged robots. Ability to work on-site in Lisbon, collaborate in a research-oriented team, and communicate clearly in English; Portuguese is a plus but not required. Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. What we offer Formal employment contract; In-house lab with humanoid robot, NVIDIA DGX Spark cluster and access to the Taguspark and IST ecosystem; real technical autonomy in a startup company; 30.000 EUR gross, possible equity participation. Expected start date: December 2027. Applications to luis@raisebox.io, with CV and, if available, links to code or work.

Grand établissement technologique, Arts et Métiers compte 14 sites et a pour mission principale de former les leaders des industries responsables, qui conçoivent et mettent en œuvre les innovations technologiques et organisationnelles impactantes, indispensables aux transitions énergétiques environnementales et sociétales. Par ses formations, ses 15 laboratoires et sa recherche partenariale, Arts et Métiers est un acteur socio-économique au service des territoires. Environnement du poste Le poste est rattaché au projet COMPOSIA et s’inscrit au sein de l’équipe du Laboratoire Angevin de Mécanique, Procédés et InnovAtion (LAMPA). L’équipe du LAMPA possède une expertise dans la mise en place d’essais pour prédire la durabilité des composites ainsi dans la mise en place de méthodes numériques avancées avec notamment des modèles d’IA basés sur la physique qui permettent de prédire des phénomènes physiques avec un nombre de données expérimentales limitées. Le projet bénéficie d’un double financement Angers Loire Développement et Carnot Arts. Dans ce cadre, l’assistant(e) de recherche contribuera aux activités expérimentales, à la collecte et à l’analyse des données, ainsi qu’au déploiement des outils numériques développés dans le projet. Le projet est mené en collaboration avec l’équipe du PIMM (Procédés et Ingénierie en Mécanique et Matériaux), reconnue pour son expertise en intelligence artificielle appliquée aux matériaux et dans l’étude des mécanismes de vieillissement des composites. L’assistant(e) de recherche évoluera ainsi dans un environnement scientifique multidisciplinaire, au contact de chercheurs, enseignants-chercheurs et ingénieurs, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement lui permettant de développer ses compétences en expérimentation, traitement de données et modélisation des matériaux. Missions et activités principales Le projet COMPOSIA s’inscrit dans le cadre des transitions écologique et numérique. Il vise à développer une méthodologie hybride basée sur des outils d’intelligence artificielle qui combinent données et modèles physiques (IA frugale) pour prédire la durabilité des matériaux composites à matrice thermodurcissable utilisés dans le bâtiment en zone inondable. Dans un contexte de changement climatique et d'augmentation des risques d'inondation en milieu urbain, la surveillance de l'état des ouvrages et la prédiction de leur durée de vie constituent des enjeux majeurs. Le matériau étudié dans ce projet est un composite verre/époxy unidirectionnel, largement utilisé pour le renforcement, la réhabilitation et la réalisation d'éléments structurels grâce à ses bonnes propriétés mécaniques, sa faible masse volumique et sa résistance à la corrosion. items.desc: The role A postdoctoral research position in computational and theoretical photochemistry is available in the School of Chemistry at the University of Bristol, supported by the ERC Consolidator Grant 101229789 In Silico Photochemistry of Atmospheric Molecules in Aqueous Aerosols (ISPAMIA). The project is led by Prof Basile Curchod (University of Bristol, UK). This project will investigate the photochemistry of atmospheric volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in and at the surface of aqueous aerosols. The project will comprise (1) theoretical developments to describe the complex environment created by an aqueous aerosol, from an electronic structure and nuclear dynamics perspective, and (2) the application of these methods to simulate the unimolecular and bimolecular photochemistry of selected VOCs in and at the surface of an aqueous aerosol. This project builds on recent works by our research group on studying the gas-phase photochemistry of atmospheric and complex molecules. The present postdoctoral position will focus on the study of the interaction of selected VOCs with different models of the air-water interface of an aqueous droplet, using machine-learned potentials to accelerate the sampling of ground-state distributions representative of the VOC in different environments. Further details of the In Silico Photochemistry Group can be found at www.in-silico-photochem.com, where a list of the group’s publication can be found as well. What will you be doing? The postdoctoral researcher will be based in the School of Chemistry at the University of Bristol where they will undertake theoretical and computational studies of the interaction of selected VOCs with models of the air-water interface and the bulk of an aqueous aerosol. The key techniques to be employed will involve the training of machine-learned interatomic potentials for the VOC and its interaction with water in different conditions (air-water interface, bulk, but also in the upper part of the 90-10 region of an interface). Ground-state dynamics – quantum-thermostat Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics and path-integral molecular dynamics – will be used to sample the ground-state nuclear distribution for the selected VOCs for the different environments. Photoabsorption cross-sections will be calculated from these distributions following intense benchmarking of the level of electronic-structure theory. You should apply if The position would best suit a talented, motivated, and curious early career researcher with a Ph.D. in Physical Chemistry or Physics and experience in theoretical research of atmospherically related compounds in a complex environment. Some or all of the following skills and experience would be an advantage: experience in using classical molecular dynamics, Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics, path-integral dynamics, and/or development of machine-learned interatomic potentials; experience with coding and scripting for data analysis; ability to communicate complex information clearly and accurately in English, both in written and oral forms; ability to work independently and as part of a team. Additional information Contract type: Open-ended with fixed funding until 31/12/2029 Work pattern: 35 hours/week Grade: I Salary: £40,704 - £45,641 per annum School/Unit: School of Chemistry Shift pattern: Monday - Friday This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on 26th November 2026 For informal queries please contact: Prof Basile Curchod, basile.curchod@bristol.ac.uk Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values.

items.desc: Contract Type Fixed Term Job Type Research Salary Range £39,560 - £46,970 per annum Hours Full Time School/Department School of Education Closing date 20/11/2026 Job ref 5635 Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today. The School of Education is pleased to invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join an exciting new research project focused on supporting children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD often referred to as dyspraxia) in educational settings. We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled researcher to undertake this full-time fixed term appointment for 18 months. You will contribute to research investigating how children with DCD/dyspraxia can be better supported in the classroom and how educational resources can be made more accessible. The post forms part of ‘Lab2School4All’ – an innovative five-year EU Horizon funded project that aims to improve the accessibility of school resources for children with DCD/dyspraxia. Research has shown that many children with DCD/dyspraxia present with persistent challenges related to handwriting and visuospatial organisation, which can create barriers to learning. Working with partners across five countries, the project team will be conducting a range of focus groups, interviews, and targeted experimental studies to explore how primary-aged children with DCD/dyspraxia access and use adapted versions of school textbooks. The findings will inform the development of practical resources and recommendations for AI-based tools that can adapt educational materials for use in mainstream classrooms and specifically create an AI-powered open-source platform designed to automate the adaptation of primary school textbooks. Overall, the project has significant potential for impact in improving accessibility and inclusive education for children with DCD/dyspraxia. You will support the delivery of the ‘Lab2School4All’ strand based at Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU). A key focus of the LJMU team is to investigate effective writing accommodations for children with DCD/dyspraxia. You will lead the recruitment of participants, manage data collection and analysis, and contribute to a predominantly quantitative study evaluating the effectiveness of different accommodations, including handwriting, typing, and speech-to-text. As part of the study, you will administer standardised assessments of motor skills (e.g., the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, third edition) alongside cognitive and literacy measures. You will also conduct interviews with children to explore their experience of using these different writing accommodations. Additional responsibilities will include coordinating research timelines and project meetings, supporting collaboration with project partners in Ireland, France, Italy and Spain, and contributing to the wider management of the project. A unique element of this post is the potential collaboration with other postdoctoral researchers in the partner institutions. The role will also involve dissemination activities, including the preparation of peer-reviewed publications, funder reports, conference presentations, social media engagement, and updates to the project website. In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies. This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. . If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you. items.desc: About SonicPrecision Every year, more than 100,000 patients in the US and Europe undergo catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia, a heart rhythm disorder that can be fatal. Most procedures happen without real-time tissue feedback: the electrophysiologist burns the tissue, ends the procedure, and hopes that the created lesion has reached the source of the arrhythmia. Published one-year recurrence rates run as high as 50%, which is the clinical gap we are closing. SonicPrecision is changing that. We built a near-field ultrasound sensor into the tip of the ablation catheter. The sensor shows the electrophysiologist what happens inside the tissue while the procedure is still running. For the first time, the physician can confirm that a lesion is deep enough before ending the procedure. We are a Philips spin-out, based in Eindhoven, with an exclusive, worldwide licence to the relevant Philips patent families. Our pre-clinical programme runs in partnership with CARIM at Maastricht University. Our next milestone is First-in-Human: the very first use of the device in patients. The role We are looking for a Clinical Engineer / Clinical Scientist to build and execute our clinical evidence strategy. This is a junior to mid-level role for someone with a clinical, biomedical, or life sciences background who wants to work across cardiology, medical device development, and regulatory science. You work directly with the founders and the R&D team: you build our clinical evidence, build relationships with leading electrophysiologists, and turn clinical insights into product and regulatory requirements. You will: Execute and update the clinical evidence roadmap: study design, publication strategy, and reports, from pre-clinical validation through First-in-Human and approval Help design and run pre-clinical studies with CARIM / Maastricht University Medical Centre (MUMC+): protocols, data collection, and endpoints Contribute to the Clinical Evaluation Report (CER) and Clinical Investigation Plan (CIP) for First-in-Human, working with our regulatory advisors on CE marking under the EU MDR and FDA approval for a Class III device Build our clinical network: find and engage senior electrophysiologists (KOLs) who can act as trial investigators, advisory board members, and early adopters Represent SonicPrecision at scientific conferences (ESC, HRS, Europace, EHRA) and contribute to abstracts and posters Turn clinical insights and physician feedback into clear product requirements, together with the engineering team Follow the literature and new technologies in catheter ablation (VT, AF, PFA, RF, cryoablation, contact force, mapping) and feed what matters into our product strategy and evidence plan What we are looking for Education: Master’s or PhD in biomedical engineering, clinical sciences, medicine, or a related life sciences discipline; a background in (interventional) cardiology, electrophysiology, or medical devices is a strong advantage Experience: 1-3 years; we do consider recent graduates with a strong clinical or MedTech graduation project Clinical knowledge: Familiarity with cardiac electrophysiology, catheter ablation, or interventional cardiology, from clinical research, an internship, or a graduation project Regulatory awareness: Basic understanding of EU MDR, clinical evaluation processes, or GCP/ISO 14155 is beneficial; willingness to build expertise in this area is essential Communication: Able to write clearly and present confidently to clinicians, regulators, and investors. Fluent in English. items.desc:
We're building systems that turn research into real-world impact — developing AI-driven detection systems that identify and remediate security access violations across Amazon's global operations, and building ML solutions that leverage product images, text, and tabular data to improve safety and compliance mechanisms across Amazon's entire product catalog. If this sounds interesting to you then we have a range of opportunities for you to explore.
We're looking for Masters students across multiple research domains to invent, design, and implement state-of-the-art solutions for never-before-solved problems. Your work here won't just stay in a notebook — it ships to production and reaches customers worldwide.
Check out the details below including the job responsibilities, team details, and basic qualifications before submitting your application.

Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Science Intern, you will own the design and development of end-to-end systems. You'll have the opportunity to write technical white papers, create roadmaps and drive production level projects that will support Amazon Science.
You will work closely with Amazon scientists and other science interns to develop solutions and deploy them into production. You will have the opportunity to design new algorithms, models, or other technical solutions whilst experiencing Amazon's customer focused culture.
The ideal intern should have the ability to work with diverse groups of people and cross-functional teams to solve complex business problems.
A day in the life
You'll spend your first weeks scoping your project with your mentor, then own the research and implementation end-to-end. 
Your work could involve building graph-based ML models and knowledge graphs that detect and remediate access violations at global scale, developing behavioral pattern clustering and automated reasoning systems for security operations, or researching multimodal and computer vision approaches on product catalog data to improve safety and compliance mechanisms — depending on the team you're matched with. 
Many interns publish at top-tier conferences or see their work deployed to production before the internship ends. Interns may also be considered for a return offer at the end of their internship, subject to performance evaluation and headcount availability. 
Further benefits of an Amazon Science internship include;
- All of our internships offer a competitive salary
- Interns are paired with an experienced manager and mentor(s)
- Interns get invited to different intern program or office events
- Interns can build their professional and personal network with other Amazon Scientists
- Interns can potentially publish work at top tier conferences
About the team
We generally hire interns for multiple teams in Romania, including but not limited to;
• CoSS — Research and develop ML solutions that improve safety and compliance across Amazon's entire product catalog working with tabular, textual, and product image data using deep learning, computer vision, LLMs, and multimodal models
• Monitored Access Detection — Build AI-driven detection and remediation systems that identify global access violations across Amazon — leveraging knowledge graphs, graph modeling, behavioral pattern clustering, generative AI, and reinforcement learning to create a self-improving, closed-loop security system.
You'll submit a single application and we'll match you with science teams best aligned with your research interests. 
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and your application stays active until we find a team match or confirm there are no matches available.
Start dates are available throughout the year for durations of between 3–6 months. Please note, each team has different start date and duration preferences — your recruiter will confirm the preferences of the team you're matched with prior to interviewing.
We offer science internships in multiple locations across the EMEA region and you can indicate your interest in all these locations by applying here (Austria, Estonia, France, Germany, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jordan, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, UAE, and UK).
Please note we do not offer remote internships.

Grow with us
 About this opportunity: 
Our Exciting Opportunity We are seeking a technically curious Data Science Intern to join our applied analytics team. items.desc: Das AIT Austrian Institute of Technology ist Österreichs größte Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . Unser Ziel ist es, wissenschaftliche Exzellenz in Innovation mit Wirkung zu verwandeln. Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnerinnen und Partnern entwickeln wir Technologien und Lösungen für eine nachhaltige, resiliente und digitalisierte Zukunft und stärken damit die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und technologische Souveränität Europas. Unsere internationalen Teams verbinden Spitzenforschung mit hoher Umsetzungskompetenz und schaffen messbaren Nutzen für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft. Unser Center for Energy sucht weitere Ingenious Partner am Standort Wien (Giefinggasse, 1210) . Im Center for Energy entwickeln wir unter Beachtung technologischer, regulatorischer und wirtschaftlicher Anforderungen nachhaltige Lösungen für das zukünftige Energiesystem. Das Themenportfolio orientiert sich an drei zentralen Systemen: Städte & gebaute Umwelt, öffentliche Energieversorgungssysteme und Industrielle Energiesysteme. Die Reduktion von CO2-Emissionen, des Energieverbrauchs und die Nutzung von erneuerbaren Energien sowie der (Weiter-)Entwicklung von energieeffizienten Technologien sind aktuelle Problemstellungen, für die nachhaltige Lösungen umgehend gefunden werden müssen. Unsere engagierten Teams arbeiten an anwendungsorientierten Forschungsprojekten im Bereich der Entwicklung und Systemintegration von Technologien zur effizienten Kühlung großer thermischer Leistungen mit hohen Leistungsdichten wie beispielsweise Rechenzentren und Nutzung der Abwärme in thermischen Netzen, und leisten somit mit unseren Lösungen einen positiven Beitrag zur Dekarbonisierung der thermischen Infrastruktur im Rahmen der Energiewende und der Erreichung von Klimazielen. Research Engineer (w/m/d) Projektleitung – Innovative Kühlung, Energieeffizienz und Abwärmenutzung in Rechenzentren CENTER FOR ENERGY Sie entwickeln und leiten Forschungsprojekte zur Entwicklung und Systemintegration effizienter Kühltechnologien und -konzepte, für hohe Leistungsdichten (z.B. Flüssig- und Immersionskühlung für Rechenzentren) und zur Nutzung großer Abwärmequellen in thermischer Infrastruktur. Mit Hilfe von Simulationsmethoden und Datenanalysen entwickeln Sie optimale, technische Lösungen und ermöglichen die anwendungsnahe Umsetzung von innovativen Konzepten für den Einsatz in Rechenzentren und thermischen Netzen der Zukunft. Sie führen experimentelle Untersuchungen durch, um mittels Prototypen technische Machbarkeiten nachzuweisen, Simulationsmodelle zu validieren, Regelungsstrategien zu entwickeln und Betriebsfenster unter verschiedenen Lastbedingungen zu testen. Sie sind im laufenden Austausch mit Ihren Kolleg:innen, die aus unterschiedlichen Fachdisziplinen kommen, und sind Ansprechperson für unsere Kund:innen und Projektpartner:innen . Sie erhalten die Möglichkeit, Ihre Forschungsergebnisse in Fachzeitschriften zu veröffentlichen und diese auch bei Konferenzen und in internationalen Foren zu präsentieren . items.desc: DESCRIPTION We're building systems that turn research into real-world impact — developing AI-driven detection systems that identify and remediate security access violations across Amazon's global operations, and building ML solutions that leverage product images, text, and tabular data to improve safety and compliance mechanisms across Amazon's entire product catalog. If this sounds interesting to you then we have a range of opportunities for you to explore. We're looking for Masters students across multiple research domains to invent, design, and implement state-of-the-art solutions for never-before-solved problems. Your work here won't just stay in a notebook — it ships to production and reaches customers worldwide. Check out the details below including the job responsibilities, team details, and basic qualifications before submitting your application. You can find more information about the Amazon Science community as well as interview preparation tips via the links below; https://www.amazon.science/ https://amazon.jobs/content/en/career-programs/university/science https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/university-roles/applied-science Key job responsibilities As an Applied Science Intern, you will own the design and development of end-to-end systems. You'll have the opportunity to write technical white papers, create roadmaps and drive production level projects that will support Amazon Science. You will work closely with Amazon scientists and other science interns to develop solutions and deploy them into production. You will have the opportunity to design new algorithms, models, or other technical solutions whilst experiencing Amazon's customer focused culture. The ideal intern should have the ability to work with diverse groups of people and cross-functional teams to solve complex business problems. A day in the life You'll spend your first weeks scoping your project with your mentor, then own the research and implementation end-to-end. Your work could involve building graph-based ML models and knowledge graphs that detect and remediate access violations at global scale, developing behavioral pattern clustering and automated reasoning systems for security operations, or researching multimodal and computer vision approaches on product catalog data to improve safety and compliance mechanisms — depending on the team you're matched with. Many interns publish at top-tier conferences or see their work deployed to production before the internship ends. Interns may also be considered for a return offer at the end of their internship, subject to performance evaluation and headcount availability. Further benefits of an Amazon Science internship include; All of our internships offer a competitive salary Interns are paired with an experienced manager and mentor(s) Interns get invited to different intern program or office events Interns can build their professional and personal network with other Amazon Scientists Interns can potentially publish work at top tier conferences About the team We generally hire interns for multiple teams in Romania, including but not limited to; CoSS — Research and develop ML solutions that improve safety and compliance across Amazon's entire product catalog working with tabular, textual, and product image data using deep learning, computer vision, LLMs, and multimodal models Monitored Access Detection — Build AI-driven detection and remediation systems that identify global access violations across Amazon — leveraging knowledge graphs, graph modeling, behavioral pattern clustering, generative AI, and reinforcement learning to create a self-improving, closed-loop security system. You'll submit a single application and we'll match you with science teams best aligned with your research interests. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and your application stays active until we find a team match or confirm there are no matches available. Start dates are available throughout the year for durations of between 3–6 months. Please note, each team has different start date and duration preferences — your recruiter will confirm the preferences of the team you're matched with prior to interviewing. We offer science internships in multiple locations across the EMEA region and you can indicate your interest in all these locations by applying here (Austria, Estonia, France, Germany, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jordan, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, UAE, and UK). Please note we do not offer remote internships.
