The ability to quickly understand and explain new propositions to senior stakeholders. A highly entrepreneurial and proactive mindset. Experience in startup, scale-up or rapidly evolving environments is a strong asset. What sets you apart Feel comfortable picking up the phone and speaking with prospects you've never met. Can explain a new proposition to a CIO after only a short onboarding period. Are energized by ambitious growth targets. Learn quickly and adapt even faster. Don't become attached to approaches that aren't producing results. Use AI tools daily and understand how they can improve productivity, research and outreach effectiveness. Enjoy operating in an environment where priorities can change quickly. Why Datashift? You'll thrive here if you're excited by building rather than maintaining. If you need a proven script, a well-known brand, and a predictable stream of leads, this probably isn't the right environment. If you enjoy creating opportunities from scratch, testing new ideas and seeing the direct impact of your work, you'll fit right in. A key role in a fast-growing Data & AI consultancy. Direct impact on Datashift's commercial growth. Significant autonomy and ownership from day one. Close collaboration with directors, marketing, AI engineers and business leaders. Strong learning and development opportunities across Data, AI and commercial growth. A clear growth path towards a senior commercial role or team lead position as the team expands. items.desc: Our Mission As humans, there are few things more exciting than meeting someone new. At Tinder, we’re inspired by the challenge of keeping the magic of human connection alive. With tens of millions of users, hundreds of millions of downloads, 2+ billion swipes per day, 20+ million matches per day, and a presence in 190+ countries, our reach is expansive—and rapidly growing. We work together to solve complex problems. Behind the simplicity of every match, we think deeply about human relationships, behavioral science, network economics, AI and ML, online and real-world safety, cultural nuances, loneliness, love, sex, and more. Our Values Take the Lead: We don't ghost our work or each other. Just as users don't leave their matches hanging, we don't let each other down. Move Fast: We have a bias for action and urgency. Something that could be done tomorrow would be better if done today. Better Together: We keep connection at the heart of dating and at the heart of how we work. Just as our users are better when they connect with others, so are we when we collaborate. Real Talk: We say the hard thing the human way. Just as we ask our users to behave with kindness and candor in our community, we expect Team Tinder to do the same. Safety First: We act with integrity, transparency, and consistency so people feel safe—whether they're swiping, matching, or working alongside us. Spark Fun: We have fun to unlock creativity, fuel innovation, and help us build better experiences for daters. Where you’ll work: This is a hybrid role and requires in-office collaboration in Ghent three times per week. The Team or Role: As a Data Scientist Intern on Tinder’s Modes team in Ghent, you’ll help build new ways for people to meet on Tinder, from group and shared experiences to new modes of using the app. You’ll work with product, engineering, and data science partners to understand how members use these experiences, define how we measure success, and turn insights into product decisions. In this role, you will: Design and execute A/B experiments to measure the impact of product features and algorithmic changes. Help build and improve the team’s experimentation and analytics tooling, including AI-assisted workflows, with a focus on standardization, automation, and clear documentation. Take a scoped analysis from question to recommendation, with guidance from your mentor. Collaborate with cross-functional partners in Data Science, Product, and Engineering to translate insights into actionable strategies. Present key findings and project outcomes to Product and Leadership teams during end-of-internship demos. Translate data insights into clear narratives and recommendations that inform product roadmaps and user experience improvements. Explore and analyze large-scale datasets to identify patterns, trends, and opportunities. You’ll Need: Passion for using data and experimentation to solve complex problems. Intermediate to advanced SQL skills for data querying and analysis. Familiarity with / building to proficiency in Python. Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and experimental design (A/B testing, hypothesis testing). Clear written communication and a curious, fast-learning mindset. Comfort using AI tools (e.g., LLM-based coding and analysis assistants) as a regular part of your workflow, and the judgment to check their output. Currently pursuing a BS/BA, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Economics, Statistics, Applied Math, or a related field. As part of our team, you'll enjoy: The hustle of a startup with the impact of a global business Tremendous opportunity to solve some of the industry’s most exciting problems Working with an extraordinary team of smart, creative, fun and highly motivated people Commitment to Inclusion At Tinder, we don’t just accept difference, we celebrate it. We strive to build a workplace that reflects the rich diversity of our members around the world, and we value unique perspectives and backgrounds. Even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications, we invite you to apply and show us how your skills could transfer. Tinder is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace where we welcome people of all sexes, gender identities, races, ethnicities, disabilities, and other lived experiences. items.desc: Robotics Perception & Localization Engineer “Geef onze AGV’s ogen en een richtingsgevoel.” Bij Mabo Engineering & Automation NV bouwen we aan de logistiek van vandaag en morgen. We ontwikkelen, implementeren en ondersteunen autonome vorkheftrucks (AGV’s en AMR’s) en geautomatiseerde intralogistieke oplossingen die onze klanten helpen om hun logistieke processen slimmer te organiseren. Onze voertuigen navigeren zelfstandig door complexe industriële omgevingen, herkennen hun omgeving en detecteren obstakels om goederen veilig en efficiënt te verplaatsen. Jouw functie: Als Robotics Perception & Localization Engineer bouw je mee aan de intelligentie achter onze autonome voertuigen. Je ontwikkelt geavanceerde algoritmes waarmee onze autonome vorkheftrucks hun omgeving waarnemen, hun eigen positie bepalen en objecten nauwkeurig lokaliseren. Je ontwikkelt jouw technologie niet alleen, je ziet ze ook in actie op echte autonome voertuigen. Jouw werkdag: Ontwikkelt en optimaliseert algoritmes voor Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), map matching en robuuste lokalisatie in dynamische industriële omgevingen; Verwerkt en analyseert 2D/3D-puntenwolken afkomstig van LiDAR- en 3D-sensoren voor mapping, segmentatie, objectherkenning en obstakeldetectie; Combineert informatie van LiDAR, camera's, IMU's, wielencoders en andere sensoren (sensor fusion en state estimation) met technieken zoals Kalman Filters (EKF/UKF) voor een nauwkeurige en betrouwbare positiebepaling; Ontwikkelt algoritmes voor ego pose estimation die continu de positie en oriëntatie van het voertuig bepalen, ook in uitdagende omgevingen met beperkte of veranderende referentiepunten; Ontwikkelt oplossingen voor object pose estimation en load detection om pallets, ladingen en andere objecten te detecteren, herkennen en lokaliseren, zodat onze voertuigen deze autonoom en nauwkeurig kunnen opnemen en afzetten; Ontwikkelt real-time perceptiealgoritmes (obstacle detection en environmental perception) voor het herkennen, classificeren en volgen van statische en dynamische obstakels; Onderzoekt en implementeert AI-, computer vision-, machinelearning- en deep-learningtechnieken om de omgevingswaarneming en autonomie van onze voertuigen verder te verbeteren; Vertaalt complexe algoritmes naar efficiënte, robuuste en performante real-time C++-software die draait op onze voertuigen; Test en valideert algoritmes met simulaties, geregistreerde sensordata en praktijktesten op echte autonome vorkheftrucks; Werkt nauw samen met software-, automation- en mechanical engineers om innovatieve algoritmes te integreren in betrouwbare, industriële toepassingen. Jouw professionele troeven: Master in Computer Science, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence of Engineering, of gelijkwaardig door ervaring. Sterke programmeervaardigheden in modern C++; kennis van Python is een plus. Ervaring met of grondige kennis van SLAM, localization en sensor fusion. Sterke wiskundige basis in 2D/3D-geometrie, lineaire algebra en probabilistische algoritmes. Affiniteit met LiDAR, 3D-camera’s, IMU’s en andere sensortechnologieën. Ervaring met ROS2, PCL, OpenCV of Eigen is een plus. Kennis van AI en deep learning voor 2D/3D-sensordata is een plus. Ervaring met AGV’s, AMR’s of andere mobiele robots is een plus. Goede beheersing van Nederlands en Engels. Jouw werkstijl: Analytisch – je bent een analytisch sterke engineer met een passie voor robotica, wiskunde en softwareontwikkeling. Probleemoplossend – je vindt het uitdagend om complexe problemen op te lossen. Betrouwbaar en kwaliteitsgericht – je ontwikkelt oplossingen die ook buiten een gecontroleerde testomgeving betrouwbaar functioneren. Oplossingsgericht – je houdt rekening met nauwkeurigheid, rekentijd en betrouwbaarheid. Autonoom – je werkt zelfstandig aan je opdrachten. Teamgericht – je functioneert uitstekend binnen een multidisciplinair engineeringteam. Jouw winst: Je komt terecht in een innovatieve en groeiende sector, binnen een technologisch vooruitstrevende onderneming: een hechte, familiale en tegelijk professionele organisatie met korte communicatielijnen. Groei, passie, samenwerking en een aangename werksfeer staan er centraal, en je maakt deel uit van een enthousiast team. Je krijgt een voltijds contract van onbepaalde duur, ruimte voor initiatief, technische verdieping en persoonlijke groei, en een uitgebreid opleidingstraject met mogelijkheden tot verdere professionele ontwikkeling. Daarnaast mag je rekenen op een aantrekkelijk salarispakket, aangevuld met extralegale voordelen; Elektronische maaltijdcheques Hospitalisatieverzekering Fietsleasing + fietsvergoeding Een laptop voor professioneel gebruik 6 extra vakantiedagen Bedrijfsfeesten, geschenken en teambuildings Ben je klaar om mee te bouwen? Ben jij gepassioneerd door robotica, autonome systemen en intelligente algoritmes en heb je ervaring met SLAM, 2D/3D-puntenwolken, sensorfusie of computer vision? Dan maken we graag kennis met jou! Stuur je cv en motivatie naar …

items.desc: Data that drives smarter decisions. At Sky, Data Science is central to how we make decisions and connect with customers. Our teams deliver analytics that guide growth strategies, build tools for personalised experiences, and lead experimentation through test-and-learn approaches. As an intern, you’ll learn from industry experts and get support to bring your ideas to life. Impress us, and you could secure a place on our Data Science graduate programme starting in September 2028. What you’ll be doing On our Data Science internship, you’ll work with stakeholders across the business to turn data into insight and action. You’ll learn analytical techniques, apply predictive algorithms, and help deliver meaningful solutions — from building new data products to forecasting customer behaviour or unlocking the value of our content. You’ll join one of our specialist teams in Sky Data: Consumer – Help protect and grow our customer base by enabling smarter decisions and personalised experiences. Content – Optimise how we produce, promote, and position content using viewing data. Product & Operations – Improve internal systems and streamline processes to maximise value and performance. What we’re looking for The one essential requirement is that you're currently studying for an undergraduate degree in any subject, and in your penultimate year. You might be studying maths, statistics, computer science, economics, or physics — or you may have shown your passion for data through personal or university projects. We’re looking for curiosity, drive, and ambition. Skills that will help you thrive: Logical, end-to-end thinking Strong problem-solving, presentation, and IT skills Experience with Python, SQL, R, SAS, or MATLAB Understanding of machine learning (e.g. regression, decision trees, boosting) Enjoy fast-paced, task-focused environments Collaborative and curious about market trends Your application journey Here’s what to expect, step by step: Step 1 – Apply online Tell us a bit about yourself — your details, your degree, and anything else you think we should know (like part-time jobs, volunteering, or cool projects you’ve worked on). Once you hit submit, keep an eye on your inbox (and your junk folder!) — we’ll send you a link to start your digital assessments. Please note, you can only apply to one programme per year. Step 2 – Show us your skills You’ll complete two online assessments designed to help us get to know you better — how you think, what motivates you, and how you might fit into the programme. The coding test includes basic SQL/Python — feel free to use resources during the test. Don’t worry - you’ll get a chance to practice first, and we’ll send you tips to help you feel confident. We understand that you might want to utilise AI to support your preparation for taking the assessments – understanding Sky etc. But we ask that you complete the assessments themselves without the assistance of AI. Want to go a step further? Check out our Preparation Hub — it’s packed with practice exercises, insights into the assessment process, and stories from current grads and apprentices. You’ll even learn more about your values, learning style, and the kind of work that suits you. Step 3 – Virtual Assessment Centre If you make it to the final stage, we’ll invite you to a virtual assessment day. You’ll take part in a range of activities designed to show us how you think, solve problems, and work with others — all while getting a real feel for what it’s like to work in Data at Sky. We'll let you know when to expect a decision once the assessment day has taken place. Need Support? If you need us to make any adjustments to help you complete any stage of your application, let us know when you submit your application and someone from our Early Careers team will get in touch if we need more detail. So why wait? This is your chance to be part of something big. Our internship puts you right at the centre of the action — learning, growing, and helping make the magic of Sky happen every day. No matter your background, interests, or degree subject, there’s space here for your ideas and ambition. A career at Sky is where better begins — and it starts with you. Got questions? We’re here to help. Drop us a line at earlycareers@sky.uk If your application is successful, your offer will depend on passing a Criminal Record Check Application deadline - 15th November 2026. We may close for applications earlier than 15th November due to high volumes, however this programme will not close any earlier than 1st November 2026.

items.desc: Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation. Dans le cadre du projet CARBURE (projet DGA Rapid mené en partenariat avec la société eXO maKina), qui vise l'explicabilité de la prise de décision dans la lutte contre la falsification d'images à partir de réseaux profonds, nous recrutons une ingénieure ou un ingénieur de recherche et développement au sein de notre Département Sciences des Données. En collaboration avec l’équipe du projet et les équipes de recherche partenaires, vous aurez pour mission principale de développer un outil d'accompagnement à l'analyse et à l'explicabilité de la falsification d'images. Vous concevrez une architecture reposant sur des RAGs multimodaux spécialisés (liés à l'interprétation des filtres du logiciel Tungstène) et assurerez leur synthèse dynamique. Vous mettrez également en place un démonstrateur (PoC) autonome fonctionnant hors réseau et valoriserez ces travaux par la rédaction de livrables techniques et de publications scientifiques. Consultez la fiche de poste détaillée ✔️ Vous avez des compétences en apprentissage automatique, apprentissage profond (PyTorch, Python) et modélisation par RAG. ✔️ Vous avez de l’expérience en développement logiciel sous Linux ou Windows et en gestion de l'expérimentation scientifique. ✔️ Vous faites preuve d'autonomie, d'esprit d'initiative et vous aimez le travail en équipe ✔️ Vous disposez d'une très bonne aisance en communication orale et écrite, en français comme en anglais (indispensable pour les publications). ✔️ La connaissance des sujets d'explicabilité de l'IA constitue un atout apprécié. Le profil recherché devra être titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau Bac +5 ou équivalent (Master 2 ou diplôme d'Ingénieur) en Informatique, Data Science ou Intelligence Artificielle. POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE : Environnement de travail scientifique de premier plan, au sein d'un département à la pointe de la recherche en sécurité des données et IA. Projet applicatif stimulant à fort enjeu technologique (DGA Rapid) combinant recherche fondamentale, IA générative (RAGs/LLMs) et partenariat industriel dynamique. Fortes opportunités de valorisation scientifique (rédaction de publications internationales, participation à des conférences) et autonomie dans la réalisation de vos travaux. items.desc: UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable. Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia. UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems. About the Role UFORCE is looking for an GTM AI Builder to help our go-to-market teams get more done with AI. You’ll focus primarily on Marketing and Military Exercises, with additional support for Sales and Revenue Operations. You’ll identify the most valuable problems to solve, build practical tools and automations, and help teams make them part of everyday work. This is a hands-on role for an AI-native business operator who combines business judgment, fast learning, and the ability to build. You won’t wait for a perfectly defined backlog: you’ll learn how teams work, uncover the underlying problems, and redesign workflows around what AI makes possible. You’ll own small-to-medium solutions independently and partner with our AI team on larger, more complex systems, working within architectural direction from the hiring manager. Your work will span discovery, building, testing, rollout, enablement, and measurement. Success means useful solutions that people actually adopt and that improve capacity, quality, speed, or access to information—not simply more agents, dashboards, or prototypes. Deep software-engineering experience and prior knowledge of UFORCE’s GTM model are not required. What you’ll do Build an AI-first Marketing operating model. Redesign recurring content and campaign workflows so the team can produce more high-quality assets through reusable templates and systems rather than one-off production. Put approved messaging, claims, quality controls, and human approvals at the center of the workflow. Improve how Military Exercises operates. Learn the team’s operating model, identify its highest-friction recurring work, and build AI-enabled workflows where they create meaningful leverage. Opportunities may include planning, coordination, participant and contact capture, preparation, follow-up, after-action insights, and handoffs into GTM systems. Help make GTM intelligence useful in everyday work. Partner with our AI team on UFORCE’s GTM intelligence and People Graph, connecting people across emails, companies, roles, relationships, and interactions. Build appropriate components such as activity capture, account and contact context, engagement signals, CRM enrichment, and follow-up, and help teams adopt the resulting tools. Add hands-on execution capacity for Sales and RevOps. Independently deliver small-to-medium improvements in areas such as reporting, closed-lost analysis, engagement scoring, CRM and data quality, follow-up, workflow automation, and enablement, while supporting—not duplicating—the larger programs already underway. Turn useful solutions into normal ways of working. Own testing, rollout, lightweight training, and adoption reinforcement. Establish clear ownership and measure before-and-after impact in time, quality, capacity, or information access. Reuse shared data and capabilities, avoid tool sprawl, and make sound decisions about when to improve, scale, or stop a solution. Required Skills Hands-on AI building. You use AI deeply in your own work and have personally built useful tools, agents, automations, analyses, or workflows. You can show what you built, how it reached users, what changed after real usage, and the difference it made. Business judgment and rapid learning. You can quickly make sense of an unfamiliar Marketing, Sales, RevOps, or exercise workflow by understanding its users, decisions, data, handoffs, and failure points. You build credibility with functional experts through good questions and useful delivery. Problem discovery and independent ownership. You don’t need a detailed task list to make progress. You identify the underlying problem, challenge initial assumptions when needed, prioritize high-value opportunities, and redesign the work rather than simply automate the request as given. Technical and CRM/data fluency. You can work directly with structured business data and AI-assisted technical tools. You can read and verify AI-generated code or workflows, catch bad assumptions, and recognize when engineering or security support is needed. Adoption, enablement, and cross-functional influence. In turn we will lift you up and encourage you to go further. Onshore or offshore, embark on a journey of opportunities, continuous learning and development. Start your journey with us today. Title: Trainee Engineer - Rigid Pipelines Location: Paris, FR Job Closing Date: 13 nov 2026 Vos responsabilités Le stagiaire sera intégré à l'équipe « Conduites rigides » (Rigid Pipelines) au sein du département « Ingénierie, conception et analyses » (Design & Analyses Engineering) de Subsea 7 GPC (Global Project Centre). Ce département est responsable de l'ingénierie des conduites sous-marines et des systèmes de raccordement pour des projets de construction offshore. Dans les systèmes de conduites sous-marines, il est crucial d'ancrer les extrémités lorsque la dilatation thermique ou le phénomène de « déplacement progressif » (accumulation de déplacements au fil des cycles, ou *pipe walking*) devient trop important. Ces systèmes d'ancrage se composent de fondations fixes ancrées dans le sol, d'un point de connexion sur la conduite, et de chaînes reliant la fondation à ce point de connexion. Les chaînes présentent toujours un certain jeu ; il est donc essentiel de vérifier, après l'installation, que ce jeu se situe bien dans les limites admissibles définies lors de la conception. Les objectifs du stage sont les suivants : Compiler les données relatives au jeu des chaînes issues de projets antérieurs et constituer une base de données regroupant tous les paramètres pertinents. Cela implique l'examen des rapports de conception traitant de l'impact du jeu des chaînes, l'analyse des rapports de relevés effectués en mer après l'installation, ainsi que l'utilisation de logiciels géospatiaux dédiés aux infrastructures sous-marines. Étudier des modèles analytiques permettant d'estimer le jeu des chaînes après installation, en s'appuyant sur les rapports de relevés. Quantifier la précision de cette estimation en tenant compte des diverses tolérances (précision des équipements de mesure, tolérances de fabrication des maillons de chaîne, incertitudes liées à la fabrication des structures). Développer un modèle par éléments finis (EF) sous Abaqus afin de représenter fidèlement les maillons de chaîne et d'évaluer les limites du modèle analytique. Vos principales missions seront les suivantes : Collecter des données issues de projets passés et constituer une base de données des relevés effectués. Développer un modèle analytique pratique permettant d'estimer le jeu des chaînes. Étudier l'impact des tolérances et rechercher des solutions pour en limiter les effets autant que possible. Élaborer un modèle par éléments finis (EF) pour obtenir une représentation précise du jeu des chaînes. Établir une procédure permettant de vérifier le jeu des chaînes à partir des données de relevés. Documenter la méthodologie et formuler des recommandations en vue de son intégration dans les processus d'ingénierie. Profil recherché Étudiant(e) en dernière année d’école d’ingénieurs ou en master, spécialisé(e) en génie mécanique, ingénierie offshore ou modélisation numérique. Esprit analytique, autonomie et approche proactive dans la résolution de problèmes. Compétences en programmation (Python, MATLAB ou équivalent) pour l’automatisation et le traitement de données. Connaissance de l’analyse par éléments finis (par ex. Abaqus, Ansys ou équivalent). Intérêt pour les systèmes offshore, l’analyse de la fatigue et l’intégrité structurelle. items.desc: The Kiel Institute for the World Economy seeks applications for a full-time position (located in Berlin.) as Research Software Engineer / Data Scientist (subject to project approval) . The position is part of a new Leibniz-funded transfer project on AI and structural economic models for economic policy. Your Role You develop research software together with economists and model developers. Your tasks include: backend development (e.g., in Rust, Go or C++); integration of large language models; connecting existing economic model code (e.g., in R and Julia); interfaces, reproducible workflows and deployment; testing and documentation. Your Profile A master’s degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Several years of professional experience in backend development. Very good skills in Rust, Go or a similar compiled, statically typed language (e.g., C++, Swift, Kotlin). Experience with containers (Docker), Linux, CI/CD and automated testing, and with API design (REST/OpenAPI). Experience building applications on large language models. Very good English. German is useful but not required. Experience with R, Julia, Python, MATLAB/Octave or GAMS is an asset. Interest in economic or scientific models is an asset. Experience with deployment and IT security is an asset. Experience maintaining open-source projects and basic frontend skills (TypeScript) are an asset. We are offering The contract runs for the duration of the project (up to 36 months) and starts as soon as possible. The salary follows the German public sector pay scale (TV-L E13, 100%), approximately €56k–€79k gross per year depending on experience, with full social security coverage, including health insurance. Part-time work, flexible working hours and partial remote work are possible. The Institute offers a family-friendly environment, including paid parental leave in line with German law. The Kiel Institute for the World Economy values diversity. We welcome applications regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion/belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. The Kiel Institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy. We promote the professional opportunities of women and strongly encourage them to apply. Women with equivalent qualifications, competence and expertise will be given preference. We are committed to employing persons with recognized disabilities and will therefore give them preference over persons without disabilities if they are equally qualified. For this position, you must either be an EU citizen or hold a work permit that is valid for the entire duration of the contract. Please submit your application online using ID-No. “SHAIRPA_RSE”. items.desc: At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees. Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so. Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us! Role The Analytical Method Development (AMD) team is part of Analytical Development within CMC Product Development. The team develops biochemical and molecular assays that support manufacturing process development, pilot-scale manufacturing and future quality control activities at designated GMP sites. We are looking for a laboratory professional who is genuinely enthusiastic about hands-on experimental work and is motivated to build their expertise in a predominantly lab-based role. The majority of your time will be spent in the laboratory, performing experiments. The remainder of your time will be dedicated to data analysis, interpretation, documentation and discussing results with colleagues. Working alongside scientists and fellow research associates, you will coordinate laboratory activities for multiple projects simultaneously. You will be joining a group of down-to-earth colleagues who value openness, collaboration and a good sense of humour. We work closely together and enjoy supporting one another, while embracing the fact that priorities in drug development can change quickly and no two weeks are exactly the same. We are therefore looking for someone who enjoys a dynamic environment, stays flexible when plans shift, and takes pride in delivering high-quality work. If you enjoy being hands-on in the lab, have a keen eye for detail, and like being part of a supportive team that celebrates successes together, we look forward to receiving your application! Are you interested in developing your skills and gaining valuable experience within an international biotech company? We look forward to receiving your CV and motivation letter. Responsibilities As a Research Associate in AMD , you will join scientists and research associates developing and qualifying new methods, contributing to assay development for one of our clinical candidates. Your work will support our growth ambitions and expanding pipeline of new antibody products. Your responsibilities will include: Working with scientists and research associates to establish new assays and to monitor their performance by proper trending. Conducting experiments, interpreting data and documenting results for assigned studies. Sharing findings with colleagues within the team and across departments. Proactively identifying ways to improve method robustness, efficiency, data quality and scientific relevance, while supporting continuous improvement of team processes. Requirements You are motivated to contribute your current knowledge of molecular biology, protein biochemistry and related techniques to our team. You conduct experiments and document results accurately and precisely. You communicate effectively, take a service-oriented approach and adapt to changing priorities and unexpected workloads. You work well both independently and as part of a team. Specifically, we ask the following of you: You have a BSc (HLO) or MSc degree in a life science-related field and at least one year of relevant hands-on laboratory experience (industry or academia). Knowledge of and experience with some binding assays (ELISA- and SPR-based) and impurity assays (dPCR-, ELISA- and HTRF-based) - primary focus. Knowledge of and experience with at least some biochemical technologies, such as absorbance spectroscopy, capillary electrophoresis (CE-SDS and icIEF) and analytical chromatography (HPLC) - secondary focus, based on priorities. You have basic statistical knowledge (ideally hands-on with GraphPad and/or JMP). You are highly organized and motivated to produce high-quality documentation. You can work on several projects in parallel and adjust priorities appropriately. You are a team player with a proactive attitude and a can-do mentality. You are fluent in English. This is an onsite role in Utrecht. You are currently living in the Netherlands and you are eligible to work in the Netherlands without needing to apply for a permit. This position starts on February 1, 2027, and we are looking for a candidate who can start in Utrecht on that date. The application deadline is …

We are looking for a Graduate Electrical Engineer to join our R&D team in Barcelona. High-speed digital design, computer buses, memory subsystems, and high-speed communication channels. Sensors, precision analog circuitry, and analog signal processing. Good analytical and problem-solving skills and curiosity to understand how complex systems work. Basic programming knowledge in C and/or scripting languages . Basic understanding of electronic components, integrated circuitry, thermal management, and electromagnetic compatibility. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English . Knowledge of other languages is a plus. A proactive mindset, willingness to learn, and ability to progressively work with greater autonomy. Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills , with an interest in collaborating in a multidisciplinary and international environment. items.desc: Buscamos un/a ML Engineer con experiencia en productivización de modelos de Machine Learning, previsión de demanda (Forecasting) y modelos de optimización para incorporarse a un proyecto del sector bancario. La persona participará en la industrialización de modelos ya desarrollados, trabajando para llevarlos a entornos productivos con garantías de robustez, escalabilidad, trazabilidad y mantenibilidad. El objetivo principal será transformar modelos analíticos en soluciones preparadas para producción, colaborando en la mejora de modelos de previsión de demanda basados en series temporales y modelos de optimización aplicados a la toma de decisiones operativas. Analizar y mejorar modelos de forecasting y previsión de demanda basados en series temporales. Diseñar y adaptar pipelines de entrenamiento, inferencia y generación de predicciones. Participar en la optimización de modelos y decisiones operativas, incluyendo la optimización de denominaciones. Integrar modelos con MLflow y herramientas corporativas de gobierno y despliegue. Aplicar buenas prácticas MLOps: versionado, testing, CI/CD, monitorización y trazabilidad. Diagnosticar incidencias en producción y realizar análisis de causa raíz. Colaborar con equipos de Data Engineering, Data Science, Plataforma y Negocio. Documentar soluciones, decisiones técnicas y procedimientos operativos. Experiencia real llevando modelos de Machine Learning a producción. Experiencia con forecasting, series temporales o modelos de previsión de demanda. Conocimientos aplicados de modelos de optimización, programación matemática o heurísticas. Python avanzado aplicado a Machine Learning y productivización. Conocimientos de Machine Learning supervisado y validación de modelos. SQL para consulta, transformación y validación de datos. Experiencia con PySpark / Apache Spark. Experiencia con Azure Databricks o plataformas analíticas equivalentes. Experiencia con MLflow o herramientas similares de gestión y seguimiento de modelos. Git y herramientas de CI/CD como Jenkins o GitHub Actions. Buenas prácticas de desarrollo: modularización, testing, logging, control de errores y documentación. Titulación universitaria en Ingeniería Informática, Matemáticas, Estadística, Física, Data Science o similar. Español fluido e inglés técnico.

items.desc: At Product Madness , we create mobile games that bring entertainment to players around the world. Data plays an important role in understanding player needs, improving gaming experiences, and making informed business decisions. Join our collaborative team, where your ideas and expertise will help us explore new opportunities, solve meaningful challenges, and shape the future of mobile gaming. The Role As a Data Scientist at Product Madness, you will use data analysis, forecasting, and predictive modelling to better understand player behaviour, solve business challenges, and improve gaming experiences. You will contribute to projects dedicated to player involvement, retention, and revenue. You will also help develop analytical tools and machine learning solutions that support informed decisions and create more personalised experiences for our players. Working with a variety of datasets, you will take ownership of clearly defined analytical and modelling tasks while learning from experienced data scientists on more complex projects. You will collaborate with game developers, data analysts, product managers, and game operations teams to translate data into meaningful insights and practical improvements. What You'll Do Explore business challenges, develop hypotheses, choose suitable analytical methods, and deliver data-driven solutions with support from experienced colleagues when needed. Develop, test, and improve predictive algorithms and artificial intelligence techniques to improve player experiences, engagement, retention, and revenue. Apply statistical analysis, forecasting, predictive modelling, and simulation to understand player behaviour and business performance. Support A/B testing and experiments by selecting relevant metrics, analysing results, and sharing findings that guide business decisions. Create analytical models, simulations, and tools that help teams make informed decisions and find opportunities for improvement. Prepare, validate, and explore large datasets to uncover trends, patterns, and insights that support business goals. Work with senior data scientists, Data Engineering, and MLOps teams to develop and integrate analytical models and machine learning solutions into business processes. Share findings with collaborators, explain key insights and limitations, and offer practical recommendations. Contribute to a supportive team environment by documenting your work, participating in peer reviews, sharing knowledge, and developing your technical skills. What We're Looking For MSc or PhD in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field, or possessing equivalent experience. 1+ years of professional experience in data science, machine learning, or quantitative analytics, with practical experience delivering analytical or modelling projects. Strong foundation in statistics, probability, descriptive analysis, and statistical inference. Practical experience in exploratory data analysis, data preparation, and working with large datasets. Experience developing and evaluating predictive or machine learning models, including regression, classification, or clustering. Understanding of statistical modelling, forecasting, and simulation techniques. Familiarity with hypothesis testing, split testing, and experimental analysis. Working knowledge of Python for data analysis and modelling, including common libraries such as pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. Ability to write SQL queries to extract, join, transform, and aggregate data. Basic understanding of software development practices, including version control, testing, and documentation. Experience using AI assistants to support coding, analysis, and other professional tasks, with appropriate validation of outputs. If you’re passionate about demonstrating data science to create exceptional gaming experiences and are ready to lead data products to success, we want to hear from you. Join Product Madness and contribute to the evolution of mobile gaming! Your specific compensation package will be determined by factors such as your skills, experience, qualifications, and location. items.desc: Company description: Scandinavian Airlines System SAS Job description: Data Scientist Focused on Revenue Management & Network Optimization At SAS, we're passionate about transforming aviation with cutting-edge technology. As part of our ongoing Digital & IT transformation, we are expanding our investments in AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, and data-driven decision-making to create smarter customer experiences and stronger commercial performance. As part of our AI Team, you'll shape the future of air travel by creating innovative, data-driven solutions that maximize revenue. You will work on one of the most challenging and rewarding problems in the industry: finding the right price, for the right customer, at the right time. Your work will ensure that the airline's Revenue Optimization remains scientifically robust, operationally scalable, and commercially impactful, directly shaping how revenue is optimized in a dynamic, competitive marketplace. Your responsibilities will center on turning business challenges into well-defined analytical problems and building end-to-end machine learning solutions that deliver measurable impact. You will design, train, and maintain models that power SAS's revenue optimization, ensuring they are accurate, scalable, and production-ready. A priority will be to deliver dynamic pricing, a groundbreaking shift in how SAS competes in the marketplace. At the same time, we are developing AI-driven revenue optimization at scale, ensuring our models continuously learn, adapt, and evolve with industry dynamics. Your work will help SAS unlock the full potential of AI in airline revenue optimization, making smarter pricing and network decisions a reality today. Challenges You Will Work On Machine Learning & Optimization Techniques Build and deploy algorithms that power revenue and network decisions. Among other solutions, you'll develop demand forecasting, purchase probability, and revenue optimization models, leveraging a broad spectrum of AI methods. From classical ensemble methods to deep learning architectures and reinforcement learning frameworks, you'll select the most effective approach for each complex problem. Operations Research Beyond building models, you'll explore new formulations, test novel algorithms and findings that push the boundaries of airline revenue optimization. You will convert advanced research into production-ready optimization and modeling solutions, collaborating with the Operations Research team to embed novel algorithms into initiatives that deliver measurable business impact. MLOps Leverage end-to-end ML infrastructure to take models from research to production at scale. This includes designing reproducible training and inference pipelines, integrating CI/CD workflows for seamless deployment, and ensuring robust monitoring to detect drift and trigger automated retraining, keeping models stable and accurate in production. To be successful we believe you have Master's Degree or higher with strong mathematics focus (Data Science, Statistics, Econometrics, Applied Mathematics, Optimization, Computer Science) or related field. At least 3 years of industry experience within the Data Science domain. Proven record of taking on loosely defined problems and translating them into practical applications. Strong mathematical background (e.g., linear algebra, calculus, statistics, optimization). More than 3 years' experience with Python, SQL and popular machine/deep learning libraries. Proficient with statistical and machine learning models (both supervised and unsupervised learning). Well-versed in cloud computing. Prior experience with Azure is a big plus. We believe you share our passion for data and algorithms. You're self-driven, persistent, creative, and curious, with a strong passion for learning. You seek to understand both the big picture and the intricate details that make it up. Like us, you get excited by commercial opportunities and proactively strive to create business value. Additional information Apply by November 16, 2026. We review applications continuously and encourage you to apply early, as the position may be filled before the closing date. Please note that, due to GDPR regulations, we cannot accept applications via email. This is a full-time position (100%) based at our headquarters in Frösundavik, Solna, Stockholm. We value in-person collaboration, although flexible working arrangements may be available depending on team and business needs. As this role contributes to security-classified systems and business-critical capabilities, a background check will be conducted as part of the final stage of the recruitment process. Please note that applications must be submitted through our careers site, as we are unable to process applications received by email.

As part of our ongoing Digital & IT transformation, we are expanding our investments in machine learning, automation, data platforms, and Generative AI. We design, deploy, and operate production models that support pricing decisions, personalize customer experiences, and make our operations smarter every day. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will play an important role in developing, deploying, and maintaining machine learning solutions that create real business value. You will work closely with data scientists, data engineers, and AI engineers to help bring models from development into production and ensure they perform reliably at scale. If you're passionate about applying machine learning to real-world challenges and want to help shape the future of AI at SAS, this is the role for you! As our Machine Learning Engineer, you will help develop and operationalize machine learning solutions across SAS. In this role, you will work hands-on with deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement of production ML solutions. You will collaborate closely with data scientists to transition models from experimentation to production, help improve deployment processes and contribute to the ongoing development of our ML platform and engineering practices. Key Responsibilities Design, develop, test, deploy and monitor end-to-end pipelines for machine learning models in Azure. Apply MLOps best practices, including version control, continuous integration, continuous delivery, continuous training, testing, and monitoring, to ensure the quality and reliability of the machine learning solutions. Monitor model performance and help identify issues related to model quality, drift, and reliability. Support automation of model training, deployment, and retraining processes. Contribute to best practices for machine learning engineering, testing, documentation, and deployment. Work with Data Engineering and IT teams to ensure solutions are scalable, secure, and reliable. Help develop and improve CI/CD processes for machine learning applications. Participate in troubleshooting and resolving issues in production ML systems. Stay up to date with developments in machine learning, MLOps, and cloud technologies. The Team We are a central AI & Automation function within SAS Digital & IT that develops and operates solutions across machine learning, automation, MLOps, and Generative AI. Our team consists of data scientists, AI engineers, ML engineers, and automation specialists who work together to deliver solutions that create measurable business impact. As SAS continues to strengthen its AI capabilities, we are investing in modern cloud platforms, scalable AI solutions, and engineering practices that enable machine learning to create value across the business. As part of the team, you will contribute to a growing portfolio of machine learning products and collaborate across disciplines to ensure solutions are production-ready, scalable, and valuable to the business. To be successful we believe you have Master's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Machine Learning, Mathematics, or a related field. 2-5 years of experience in Machine Learning Engineering, MLOps, or a related role. items.desc: Job description The AICell Lab (https://aicell.io) in the department of Applied Physics at KTH and Science for Life Laboratory is a new research group funded by the Data-driven Life Science Fellows program. The group, led by Wei Ouyang, focuses on building AI systems for data-driven cell and molecular biology. To expand the team, we are now opening a position for a researcher in privacy-preserving AI for sensitive biomedical data. The researcher will play a key role in developing our platform where AI agents analyse data where it is, so that sensitive data never has to leave the data owner’s environment. This is a unique opportunity to help shape how sensitive data can be shared and used safely in research and healthcare across Europe, and to be part of an enthusiastic and dynamic team. The responsibilities are: Lead research and development of the group’s platform for AI agents and privacy-preserving analysis of sensitive data Represent KTH in EU projects and identify opportunities to use the platform in them Initiate applications for external funding and build collaborations with healthcare, industry and data owners Supervise students and contribute to the supervision of doctoral students in the group Publish research findings in high-quality scientific journals and conferences Qualifications Requirements A doctoral degree in a relevant field such as Physics, Computer Science, Bioinformatics, or other life sciences or an equivalent foreign degree. Extensive experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational biology Collaborative abilities Independence We are looking for someone who is reliable, collaborative, and communicative. You need to be able to work independently, actively contribute to problem solving, and to help move projects forward. It is commendable if you are well organized and thorough. As an employee at KTH, awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality, is required. Preferred qualifications International postdoctoral experience Training in machine learning, information security or data protection Experience of advanced use of AI agents and workflows built on large language models, e.g. multi-agent systems Experience of EU-funded projects and of working with European research infrastructures Experience in a management or leadership role, e.g. head of a unit or platform in academia, a research infrastructure or other R&D work, with responsibility for operations, budget and external collaborations A record of winning external research or innovation funding in open competition, e.g. a personal research grant or fellowship from a national or international funder Knowledge of regulations for sensitive data, e.g. GDPR and the European Health Data Space (EHDS) Scientific publications in the field Good knowledge of Swedish as is required for the day-to day work. Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills. Join us at KTH KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. items.desc: Om rollen I kundsupportteamet “Klientstöd” utvecklar vi hur människor och AI-assistenter arbetar tillsammans. Rollen kommer att jobba nära kollegornas vardag, där analys, gemensamt lärande och ett bra bemötande hänger ihop. Strukturera och utveckla en gemensam kunskapsbank med tillförlitliga data, rutiner och regelverk som är användbara för både kollegor och AI-assistenter. Granska och förbättra AI-svarens saklighet, förklaringar och bemötande. Undersöka om svaren är begripliga och anpassade till mottagarens kunskapsnivå och behov. items.desc: Build the future with breakthrough tech. At Sky, we’re not just keeping up with technology—we’re shaping it. From AI and data to automation and digital products, our Technology Graduate Programme helps you build skills in the technologies shaping the future. The programme combines an immersive bootcamp with two years of rotational experience, giving you the opportunity to build strong foundations before developing your skills across a range of technology teams and projects. Over two years, you’ll rotate through teams working on cutting-edge projects that power millions of customer experiences. Whether it’s building with software, experimenting with GenAI, or delivering in an agile framework, you’ll gain hands-on experience and support with the tools and technologies that are transforming the industry. You don’t need to choose a specialism right away. This programme is designed to help you explore, grow, and find your path—whether that’s in development, networks, broadcast, cyber, AI, or delivery. We’re looking for curious, motivated people who want to build a career in technology. You don’t need a technical background to apply. What matters most is a genuine interest in technology and the impact it can have on our customers. Over two years, we’ll help you develop into a well-rounded technology professional, giving you insight into how our teams create and deliver great customer experiences across Sky’s products and services. As you gain experience across different technology teams, you’ll discover where your strengths and interests lie and have the opportunity to specialise in the areas that excite you most. What you’ll be doing Technology never stands still, and neither do we. From exploring new ideas to delivering solutions used by millions of customers, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful projects from concept through to launch. If you enjoy learning, adapting to change, and solving problems, you’ll thrive at Sky. Throughout the programme, you'll rotate across a range of teams and develop a blend of technical, analytical, and delivery skills while gaining exposure to Sky’s wider technology landscape. You could: Build digital products using technologies like AI, cloud platforms, and modern software development tools. Learn about cyber security, threat modelling, and how we protect customers, systems, and data from emerging risks. Explore network technologies across physical, virtual, and broadcast environments. Help shape the future of new technology solutions as a Product Owner or Technical Product Owner. Use machine learning, large language models (LLMs), and generative AI to solve real-world business and customer challenges. From day one, you'll work on real projects with real impact, supported by experienced mentors and surrounded by people who are passionate about technology. By the end of the programme, you'll have the confidence, experience, and specialist skills needed to take the next step in your career at Sky. What we’re looking for The one essential requirement is that you’re currently in the final year of your undergraduate degree, completing a postgraduate qualification, or have already graduated. Your degree can be in any subject. Skills that will help you thrive: You should be able to demonstrate a capability to learn new technical skills quickly Curious about emerging technologies and how they’re changing the world Passionate about solving problems and building smart, scalable solutions Comfortable learning new tools and working in agile teams Excited to explore areas like AI, data, automation, and cloud platforms. Right to work: Please be aware that Sky do not offer sponsorship for this role, employment is contingent on you having a valid right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme. You can find information on the length of our programmes on the website. Your application journey Here’s what to expect, step by step: Step 1 – Apply online Tell us a bit about yourself — your details, your degree, and anything else you think we should know (like part-time jobs, volunteering, or cool projects you’ve worked on). Once you hit submit, keep an eye on your inbox (and your junk folder!) — we’ll send you a link to start your digital assessments. Please note, you can only apply to one programme per year. Step 2 – Show us your skills You’ll complete two online assessments that help us get to know you better - how you think, what motivates you, how you might fit into the programme. and your technical abilities. Don’t worry — you’ll get a chance to practice first, and we’ll send you tips to help you feel confident. We understand that you might want to utilise AI to support your preparation for taking the assessments – understanding Sky etc. But we ask that you complete the assessments themselves without the assistance of AI. items.desc: The Department of Computer Science invites applications for one-year research assistant positions focused on developing innovative robot control and navigation techniques using simulation-based learning for medical robotic endoscope devices. Project Background This project addresses two critical challenges in the field of medical robotics to improve patient care through advanced simulation and control: Image-Based Navigation: Creating reward functions for scoring navigation policies for medical robotic devices moving inside the human body, relying solely on image information and accounting for environment changes through interaction models. Soft Robot Control: Developing learning-based methods to control a soft robot endoscope via high-level navigation policies to perform clinical procedures inside the human body, including quality assessment of these methods during in-vivo interventions. The successful candidates will join a multidisciplinary and collaborative team renowned for cutting-edge research in medical imaging and simulation technologies, operating within a global network across France, Germany, and Spain. Roles and Responsibilities The successful candidates will play a central role in the project’s technical and scientific success. While the level of autonomy will vary by position, both roles will share the following core responsibilities: Technical Development & Implementation : Designing and implementing machine learning methods for motion planning and control. This includes integrating simulation-based learning frameworks and demonstrating the resulting systems on real robotic hardware and soft robot endoscopes. Research & Scientific Contribution : Contributing to the project’s core objectives by producing impactful research outputs. This includes writing high-quality papers for peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at international conferences. Collaboration & Knowledge Exchange : Facilitating collaborations with industrial partners and academic collaborators to ensure that the developed methodologies are meaningful and translatable to real-world clinical practice. Professional Growth & Mentorship : Engaging in a high-growth research environment. The positions can be extendable and towards a PhD depending on the future funding status. The project has a trackrecord of landing members in top PhD program and faculty positions. Interdisciplinary Integration : Actively participating in team discussions and workshops to integrate expertise across medical imaging, physics simulation, and robotics control. Profile We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience: Essential experience and skills MSc in the fields mentioned above. You have a strong foundation and track record in robotics simulation, robot control, computer vision and/or machine learning for physical systems. You are highgly experienced in numerical optimization algorithms, preferably applied to motion planning or reinforcement learning. Hands-on experience on real robots especially soft robot systems is a plus. Proficient scientific computing and programming (C++/Python) and experience with libraries such as PyTorch, JAX, Warp, Taichi, or ROS. Excellent communication skills and a high level of motivation to work in a multidisciplinary, international research environment. Desireable experience and skills Experience in publishing peer-reviewed research in top-tier robotics or AI venues. Familiarity with physics simulation such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Newton Physics, SOFA etc. Terms of employment The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year. The starting date is 15 February or after agreement Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. Questions Further information on the Department is linked at https://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to kenny@di.ku.dk and hayi@di.ku.dk. Application procedure Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format Motivated letter of application (max. one page). CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. A certified/signed copy of a Master of Science certificate. List of publications. items.desc: Do you thrive in the unknown and love to build from scratch? At JENSEN-GROUP, we offer a unique opportunity to be part of something from the very beginning, helping us build a modern, scalable software platform for the future. You’ll play a key role in shaping the technical direction and helping define the tools and technologies we’ll build on. We also strongly believe that LLMs and AI in general can, and should, play an active role in modern software development, and we’re excited to explore that together with you. Location: Denmark What you’ll be doing: Design and build a distributed data platform running across laundries worldwide Translate business needs and ideas into concrete, working solutions with a short real world feedback loop Contribute to recruiting, onboarding, and growing the future software team Lay the foundation for a healthy engineering culture, including code quality, documentation, and DevOps practices What you’ll bring: A master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or similar At least five years of professional experience, covering some of (and interest in most of) the following: Docker, databases, backend development, data analysis & AI, distributed systems, observability, test automation, and CI/CD You work independently, methodically, and know when to ask for help You thrive in an environment where not everything is defined up front and where direction may change as we learn You think long-term in architecture and patterns, but aren’t afraid of temporary solutions when they make sense You contribute hands-on to implementation, both leading the way and backing up the rest of the team You’re driven by curiosity and engagement, and the kind of person who thinks: “If it needs to be built, I’ll learn how” — whether it’s infrastructure, dataflows, or frontend A Danish work permit and proximity to Odense as the team works in-office. Mezcada Mezcada is JENSEN-GROUP’s next-generation software platform for industrial laundries worldwide, a hybrid MES/SCADA system that gives laundries full visibility into performance, bottlenecks, and energy consumption. It provides the data foundation needed to predict maintenance, optimize flow, and make better decisions on the laundry floor. That said, you don’t need experience with industry, SCADA, or MES. In fact, we’re looking for someone who brings a fresh perspective and dares to question the assumptions the rest of us might take for granted. The platform uses distributed edge computing and is continuously delivered to customer sites on-prem, as well as to the cloud for analysis and support. Machine and sensor data is collected via OPC-UA and MQTT and made available through a well-designed API, both to the customer and to the frontend. JENSEN-GROUP & INWATEC — The LAUNDRYNERDS JENSEN-GROUP is a global leader in industrial laundry technology with a strong R&D focus that keeps the company ahead of the curve. The Mezcada team is based at the innovation hub in Odense, together with the subsidiary Inwatec that delivers cutting-edge tech for sorting, automation, and smarter laundry processes. Together, we’re looking forward to moving into beautiful new offices on Hvidkærvej in 2026. We’re a fast-growing engineering company, and our team is creative, dynamic, and deeply dedicated. We love our informal work culture, where every idea is taken seriously, and everyone is treated equally. And yes, we also have fun together: on Fridays, we meet up in the office bar for beers and a game of ping pong amongst many other things. Join us on this exciting journey of innovation and development — where every line of code you write makes a difference. If you are passionate about software engineering and eager to be part of a dynamic team, this opportunity is perfect for you! Let’s build the future of laundry together! Sounds good? What are you waiting for? now at www.inwatec.dk/job. Please upload your documents in PDF format.

items.desc: À propos de nous Premier pôle européen de recherche, de soins et d’enseignement sur les maladies génétiques créé en 2007 au cœur du campus de l’Hôpital Necker-Enfants malades. Sa mission ? Mieux comprendre les maladies génétiques pour mieux les guérir. L’Institut Imagine est un endroit unique au monde qui rassemble chercheurs, patients, médecins et personnels de santé dans une architecture créatrice de synergies au service d’une même ambition : changer la vie des familles touchées par les maladies génétiques. Mission Marie-Louise Frémond, chercheuse dans le laboratoire du Pr Yanick Crow à l'Institut Imagine (Paris) recrute un(e) ingénieur(e) d’étude pour le projet SABLE. Ce projet étudie l'inflammation pulmonaire dans le SAVI et le syndrome COPA à l'aide de modèles cellulaires, notamment des cellules endothéliales et épithéliales pulmonaires dérivées de cellules iPS humaines. https://www.institutimagine.org/fr/yanick-crow-180 Créé à l’initiative des chercheurs et médecins de l’Hôpital Necker, l’Institut des maladies génétiques Imagine (Institut Hospitalo-Universitaire (IHU), INSERM U1163) développe des programmes scientifiques fondés sur une continuité entre recherche fondamentale, recherche clinique et soins innovants sur les maladies génétiques et les prédispositions génétiques aux maladies fréquentes, de l’enfance à l’âge adulte. Imagine est un institut internationalement reconnu qui assure une recherche de haute qualité en termes de formation pluridisciplinaire et de taux de publication. Contexte scientifique : Le laboratoire de neurogénétique et neuroinflammation dirigé par Yanick Crow identifie et étudie les bases moléculaires et cellulaires des interféronopathies de type I, des maladies génétiques caractérisées par une production chronique d’interférons de type I. L’étude de ces maladies a montré que deux d’entre-elles, le SAVI (STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy) et le syndrome COPA présentent une inflammation pulmonaire sévère responsable de fibrose et d’une mortalité élevée. De façon intéressante, le rôle de l'interféron de type I comme médiateur de l'inflammation pulmonaire a été récemment mis en évidence. Dans un travail supervisé par Marie-Louise Frémond, nous avons montré que la protéine COPA, qui est mutée dans le syndrome COPA, a un rôle dans le trafic de la protéine STING au sein du système Golgi – réticulum endoplasmique (Lepelley et al. J Exp Med 2020, PMID: 32725128). Ce lien mécanistique explique le chevauchement clinique et histologique observé entre le SAVI et le syndrome COPA (Frémond & Crow. J Clin Immunol 2021, PMID: 33532887). Cependant, les mécanismes de la fibrose induite par l’inflammation pulmonaire restent inconnus. Au sein de l’équipe, Marie-Louise Frémond (PU-PH, HDR, Université Paris Cité) s’intéresse aux mécanismes de l’inflammation pulmonaire observée dans les interféronopathies de type I. Missions : L'ingénieur(e) d'étude participera au développement et à l'utilisation de modèles cellulaires pulmonaires pour étudier la réponse inflammatoire dans le SAVI et le syndrome COPA. Il/elle travaillera en particulier sur des modèles 2D dérivés d'iPSC humaines (déjà générées), différenciées en cellules endothéliales et épithéliales. Activités principales : Culture et entretien de cellules primaires, de lignées cellulaires et d'iPSC humaines / Constitution et gestion des banques cellulaires ; Différenciation des iPSC en cellules pulmonaires, notamment endothéliales et épithéliales, en modèles 2D (organ-on-a-chip, co-cultures) ; Caractérisation des cellules différenciées et contrôle qualité des différenciations ; Stimulations et traitements cellulaires, y compris l'évaluation de molécules thérapeutiques ; Analyse de la réponse inflammatoire : expression de gènes (extraction d'ARN, RT-qPCR, préparation d'échantillons pour RNAseq bulk), expression protéique (western blot, ELISA, cytométrie en flux) et immunofluorescence et microscopie confocale ; Mise au point et optimisation de protocoles. Activités associées : Analyse, mise en forme et présentation des résultats en réunion d'équipe ; Rédaction et mise à jour des protocoles ; Participation aux tâches communes du laboratoire (par exemple : commandes, gestion des stocks, entretien des équipements) ; Respect des règles d'éthique, d'hygiène et de sécurité de l'Institut Imagine. Marie-Louise Frémond, a researcher in Pr Yanick Crow's laboratory at the Institut Imagine (Paris), is recruiting a research engineer for the SABLE project. The project studies lung inflammation in SAVI and COPA syndrome using cellular models, in particular endothelial and epithelial lung cells derived from human iPSCs. The Institut Imagine (IHU, ‘Institut Hospitalo-Universitaire’, INSERM U1163) is a recent research structure located within Necker Children’s Hospital (Paris). Its research labs are focused on understanding the molecular mechanisms of genetic diseases that affect the adaptive and innate immune systems, the nervous system, stem cell …

items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Institut de biologie de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure Type de Contrat IT en contrat CDD Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 75230 PARIS 05 Durée du contrat 6 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration Selon expérience – Entre : 2 571€ et 3 817€ Date limite de candidature : vendredi 27 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Les Missions Développer des méthodes de traitement et d’analyse des signaux EEG enregistrés pendant l’anesthésie, à partir des enregistrements provenant de Dan Longrois. Étudier les signatures EEG associées à la S-kétamine et les asymétries entre hémisphères droit et gauche. Contribuer au développement d’indicateurs et de modèles pour le suivi et, à terme, le pilotage de l’anesthésie dans un cadre de recherche. L'Activité Structurer les enregistrements EEG et les métadonnées disponibles ; documenter leur qualité et leur synchronisation avec les événements anesthésiques. Développer des chaînes reproductibles de prétraitement : filtrage, détection et correction des artéfacts, segmentation et contrôle qualité. Réaliser des analyses spectrales et temps-fréquence ; caractériser les signatures associées à la S-kétamine selon les informations disponibles sur son administration. Quantifier les asymétries droite–gauche sur des dérivations homologues, en contrôlant les effets du montage, de la référence et des artéfacts. Développer et évaluer des indicateurs de suivi et des prototypes de modèles destinés à la recherche sur le pilotage de l’anesthésie. Documenter le code, assurer la traçabilité des analyses et présenter les résultats à l’équipe scientifique et clinique. Compétences attendues : Traitement du signal, analyse de séries temporelles, statistiques et modélisation numérique. Programmation Python, notamment MNE et les bibliothèques scientifiques ; gestion de versions et analyses reproductibles. Connaissances en EEG, neurosciences et prétraitement des données neurophysiologiques. Apprentissage automatique apprécié ; capacité à évaluer les modèles et leurs limites. Rigueur, autonomie, travail avec des chercheurs et des cliniciens, anglais scientifique. Votre Profil Compétences Mathématiques / physique / informatique / EEG neuroscience/ Simulations / analyse de données / python Compétences relationnelles : interactions avec les partenaires biologiques Votre Environnement de Travail L’Institut de biologie de l’ENS (IBENS) est un centre de recherche fondamentale qui mène des recherches originales visant à décrypter les mécanismes fondamentaux au cœur des processus biologiques. Unité mixte ENS-CNRS-INSERM, l’IBENS accueille plus de 300 personnes regroupées en 30 équipes autonomes conduisant une recherche hautement collaborative et multidisciplinaire qui allie approches expérimentales et théoriques. L’activité de recherche couvre des champs thématiques variés : Neurosciences, Biologie du développement, Génomique fonctionnelle, Écologie et biologie de l’évolution. Plusieurs plateformes technologiques, notamment en imagerie, génomique, protéomique et bio-informatique sont à la disposition des chercheurs. Les recherches menées à l’IBENS bénéficient des interactions avec d’autres disciplines présentes à l’ENS (physique, chimie, sciences cognitives, mathématiques). L’IBENS est activement impliqué dans la formation des étudiants et jeunes chercheurs à tous les niveaux. L’équipe d’accueil Mathématiques appliquées et Biologie computationnelle, dirigée par David Holcman comprend une dizaine de d’étudiants et chercheurs tous confondus. L’objectif de l’équipe est de comprendre et de quantifier les mécanismes sous-jacents de la biologie computationnelle. Contraintes et risques Travail sur écran et manipulation de données de santé ; respect de la confidentialité, des autorisations d’accès et des règles de sécurité applicables au projet. Les développements de pilotage seront évalués dans un cadre de recherche ; toute utilisation clinique nécessitera une validation et un cadre adaptés. Déplacements ou présence au bloc : à confirmer. Rémunération et avantages Rémunération Selon expérience – Entre : 2 571€ et 3 817€ Congés et RTT annuels 44 jours Pratique et Indemnisation du TT Pratique et indemnisation du TT Transport Prise en charge à 75% du coût et forfait mobilité durable jusqu’à 300€ À propos de l’offre Référence de l’offre UMR8197-VALHER-265 Secteur d’activité Sciences du vivant, de la terre et de l'environnement Emploi type Ingenieur biologiste en traitement de donnees (H/F) À propos du CNRS Le CNRS est un acteur majeur de la recherche fondamentale à une échelle mondiale. Le CNRS est le seul organisme français actif dans tous les domaines scientifiques. Sa position unique de multi-spécialiste lui permet d’associer les différentes disciplines pour affronter les défis les plus importants du monde contemporain, en lien avec les acteurs du changement.
