items.desc: Job Description: Are you our next Product Application Engineer – Emergency Lighting? Are you passionate about emergency lighting, technology, and turning technical expertise into real customer value? We’re looking for a Product Application Engineer to help drive the adoption and growth of our Emergency Lighting portfolio across Sweden. In this role, you’ll combine technical expertise with a strong commercial mindset. You’ll work closely with our sales teams, consultants, customers, partners, and offer management to shape solutions, influence specifications, develop opportunities, and build a strong pipeline for Emergency Lighting. What you’ll do Act as the technical expert for Emergency Lighting , supporting the sales organisation throughout the sales process. Provide hands-on support in customer opportunities , from early discussions and specification through product selection, system design and final solution. Work closely with sales teams, consultants/specifiers and customers to develop the right technical solutions. Provide continuous technical engagement throughout specification and sales cycles, helping us strengthen our position in the Emergency Lighting market. Develop Emergency Lighting competence within the sales organisation through training, coaching and day-to-day technical support . Help build strong Emergency Lighting expertise internally and reduce dependency on external technical support. What we’re looking for Strong technical knowledge of Emergency Lighting systems and solutions . Previous experience within Emergency Lighting is highly desirable. Experience supporting sales and customer projects , rather than only working with products internally. Understanding of the consultant/specification process and how technical solutions are specified in projects. Ability to translate technical knowledge into practical solutions for customers and sales teams . Proactive, customer-oriented and commercially minded, with an interest in developing and growing the business. This is not only a product expert role. We’re looking for someone who enjoys working closely with sales and customers and can provide continuous, hands-on technical support throughout the specification and sales process. Our Emergency Lighting portfolio You’ll work across our Emergency Lighting offer, including: Emergency luminaires, including anti-panic lighting and exit signs Self-contained Emergency Lighting systems DiCub Central Battery Systems, including AC/AC and AC/DC solutions Essential for the role Excellent knowledge of Emergency Lighting principles, products, systems, and applications. Strong ability to translate technical knowledge into clear customer and business value. Ability to influence and engage different stakeholders with empathy and credibility. Genuine passion for technology, innovation, and continuous development. A proactive mindset and willingness to challenge the status quo. Ability to learn quickly and become a trusted point of reference within the organisation. A strong business development mindset with an interest in identifying and developing opportunities. Comfortable working collaboratively with sales teams, customers, consultants, partners, and other internal stakeholders. Location and Language requirements The role is based in our Stockholm office in Sweden. Ability to work effectively across different customers, partners, and internal teams within these markets. Why Schneider Electric? Work with technologies and solutions that contribute to safer and more sustainable buildings. Take on a highly visible role combining technical expertise, customer engagement, and business development. Hybrid work model and flexible hours. Inclusive, supportive and diverse work culture with a people-first approach. Global career development opportunities. Competitive compensation and benefits tailored to the region. Schneider Electric is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and identities. Where can I find out more? items.desc: Infrastructure / SRE Engineer Inviso is partnering with one of our clients to find an experienced Backend / Platform Engineer to join their team working remotely. Inviso is managing the recruitment and placement process for this opportunity. This is a remote, direct-hire permanent employee position for our client that is a global multi-billion dollar software conglomerate. The Infrastructure / SRE Engineer is responsible for designing, building, and operating the cloud, infrastructure, deployment, observability, and reliability capabilities that allow platform teams to ship safely and consistently. This role focuses on landing zones, infrastructure-as-code, Kubernetes, CI/CD, observability, incident response, cost optimization, and production readiness. The Engineer treats infrastructure and reliability as products, building repeatable systems that reduce toil, improve delivery speed, and support mission-critical customer environments. The ideal candidate is hands-on, automation-minded, calm under pressure, and comfortable owning systems in production. Experience & Skills Required Experience building and operating production cloud infrastructure with reliability ownership. Strong experience with infrastructure-as-code, landing zones, networking, identity, security, and environment management. Experience with Kubernetes, containerized workloads, CI/CD pipelines, and automated deployment practices. Experience establishing observability using metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerting, and actionable operational signals. Experience defining or supporting SLOs, reliability practices, incident response, postmortems, and on-call operations. Ability to automate operational tasks and reduce manual toil through scripts, tools, runbooks, and platform services. Experience preparing software for customer-controlled, hybrid, BYOC, on-premises, or edge environments preferred. Strong understanding of cost and capacity optimization, including expensive compute such as GPU workloads. Strong communication and collaboration skills for client-facing consulting environments. Pragmatic mindset with the ability to balance speed, safety, automation, cost, and operational quality. Desired Qualifications Experience with Azure, Kubernetes, Terraform, Bicep, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or related infrastructure and delivery tools. Experience with Azure Arc, fleet management, pull-based deployment patterns, or version/configuration drift management. Experience supporting regulated, air-gapped, edge, or mission-critical delivery environments. Experience supporting AI/ML platforms, model-serving infrastructure, GPU workloads, or AI development lifecycle operations. Experience building enterprise-scale infrastructure supporting multiple teams, products, or customers. Experience using AI-assisted development tools while maintaining strong review, testing, and operational discipline. Success Criteria Success in this role is measured by reliable platform operations, repeatable delivery, strong observability, reduced operational toil, and the ability to help client teams ship safely into complex customer environments. Infrastructure / SRE Engineers are expected to improve speed and stability at the same time.

items.desc: We are looking for a talented and experienced scientist to join our Technology Development team and help deliver innovative crop biotechnology projects through high-quality experimental science. Our Technology Development team works across molecular biology, gene editing, plant transformation and assay development to support Tropic’s crop improvement programmes and accelerate research into real-world impact. Job Purpose In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of key R&D programmes through technology optimisation, in particular the development of protoplast cell assays, including gene editing, RNAi implementation and plant regeneration. You will drive and lead experimental design and execution, generate high-quality data, communicate results effectively and help shape project direction through scientific insight, innovation and effective collaboration. Responsibilities Design and deliver laboratory experiments independently with scientific rigour and creativity. Plan experiments, manage risk, troubleshoot effectively and interpret results to inform project decisions. Identify and apply new methods and technologies that support innovation and business goals. Maintain accurate, traceable records and contribute high-quality data and documentation. Communicate progress, risks and recommendations clearly to colleagues and stakeholders. Collaborate across teams and support a culture of shared learning and continuous improvement. Champion safe laboratory practice, quality standards and scientific excellence. Show initiative to contribute to wider team performance and the training of others. Requirements You will bring proven scientific expertise, hands-on laboratory excellence and the drive to apply your skills in crop biotechnology and deliver real-world impact from your work. Technical PhD in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Plant Biotechnology or a related discipline. Strong technical expertise in experimental design, in particular in protoplast-based gene editing and regeneration. Troubleshooting, data analysis and delivery of high-quality scientific outputs. Ability to design, interpret and optimise complex laboratory experiments and workflows. Expertise in areas relevant to plant biotechnology including advanced molecular biology, gene editing, tissue culture, assay development and bioinformatics. Experience with rice transformation is desirable, but not essential Transferable Proven ability to take ownership of complex research activities and deliver against objectives. Able to manage competing priorities, solve problems effectively and adapt in a fast-paced environment. Scientifically curious, proactive and innovative, with strong critical thinking skills. Clear and confident communicator, able to share progress and recommendations with different audiences. Highly organised, with strong attention to detail in record-keeping, data handling and reporting. Collaborative and supportive, with a positive approach to team-working and continuous improvement. About Us Tropic is a pioneering tropical seeds company dedicated to the development of healthier, more robust, high-performing varieties of tropical crops. The company’s current core crop portfolio focuses on banana and rice, which together provide a source of livelihood to billions of people worldwide. Tropic utilises its proprietary GEiGS® platform and other cutting-edge gene editing technologies to develop improved crops with increased disease resistance, higher yields, and environmentally sustainable traits. By harnessing the power of advanced genetic engineering, Tropic is committed to addressing global agricultural challenges and providing innovative solutions that benefit farmers, consumers, and the environment. Why Join Tropic? Diverse workforce operating in a dynamic working environment Excellent learning and career development opportunities Social events throughout the year Competitive compensation and benefits including: Private Medical Care, Medical Cash Plan, 25 days annual leave and Life Assurance Further Information Job Location – Norwich UK Time Requirement – Full Time Contract – 3 year Fixed Term Closing date – 23/11/2026 If you are looking to work in a dynamic company, striving towards a real-world impact, then consider joining our team and apply here!

items.desc: This is a Band 6 Specialist Biomedical Scientist role in Blood Sciences at Guy’s and St Thomas’ laboratories specialising in Core Chemistry This is a 24/7 shift working opportunity within the Synnovis Essential Services Laboratories in the heart of London The Blood Sciences department is an innovative and progressive department that delivers analytical services to two prominent London teaching hospitals, Guy’s and St Thomas Hospital, as well as supporting the Synnovis Hub. It offers an extensive repertoire of tests in Chemistry and also supports clinical services such as first trimester screening and intraoperative PTH testing in theatres. This department is actively engaged in training activities, ranging from IBMS registration and specialist portfolios to presentations and lectures. The in-house training is well-structured, featuring monthly CPD sessions, clear training plans supported by UKAS, Synnovis training opportunities, and the option to attend external conferences. This position follows a 24/7 shift pattern. You will be expected to rotate through all areas of Core Chemistry, working across both the Guy’s and St Thomas’ sites with extensive exposure to the interesting caseloads put through the laboratory. Synnovis is committed to training and development through the organisation's Scientific Learning and Development fund, allowing permanent members of staff the opportunity to apply for funding for a variety of qualifications and CPD activities. As a Specialist Biomedical Scientist, the post holder will be responsible for the delegated tasks required for the delivery of a fit-for-purpose medical laboratory service to achieve the objectives of efficient and effective patient care, and resource management within the Blood Sciences Laboratory. They will be required to undertake their responsibilities within any of the core sub-units of Core Chemistry. You will be HCPC registered having completed the IBMS Specialist Portfolio in Clinical Chemistry or be able to demonstrate equivalent knowledge and experience. The laboratories are UKAS accredited to ISO 15189 standards and are accredited with IBMS as training laboratories for both Registration and Specialist Portfolios. This should give you the confidence that your development is in safe hands. The laboratory is based on two sites St. Thomas’ and Guys both of which have a very diverse culture. There is a wide breadth of clinical specialties associated with a prestigious teaching hospital including a distinct children’s hospital on site, The Evelina. For you, this makes for varied and interesting, and sometimes challenging work; no two days are ever the same! Due to the variety and complexity of some of our patients the work can be very challenging but rewarding as you will gain invaluable scientific experience. The laboratories are equipped with Abbott Alinity analysers which are integrated to the EPIC electronic patient record system used throughout the Trust. Your development and learning You will have access to a comprehensive suite of learning opportunities through The Synnovis Way Development Programme, a cornerstone across Synnovis designed to help you unlock your potential, acquire new skills, and achieve your professional goals. Your development will be actively supported and tailored in collaboration with your line manager, ensuring alignment with your personal ambitions and career aspirations. Technical To safely handle, use and dispose of blood or other body fluids or hazardous chemicals. To plan and organise their work within the demands of the team. items.desc: COMPANY & ROLE OVERVIEW Kodiform Therapeutics is a discovery-stage spin-out from the Institute of Cancer Research and the University of Oxford, based on the pioneering research of our Founders, Professors Terry Rabbitts and Angela Russell. We develop small-molecule inhibitors of hard-to-drug proteins, including intrinsically disordered proteins, using our intracellular domain antibody (iDAb) platform. Our technology finds new functional binding sites on these proteins and opens new routes to target them with small molecules. We are based at the Scale Space science Innovation Hub in White City, London. The role. We are looking for an experienced cell biologist with substantial hands-on experience in medium- to high-throughput screening of small molecules to join our small, multidisciplinary laboratory team. Working hand in hand with colleagues in pharmacology and on the iDAb platform, you will develop, optimise and run robust, automation-ready assays, mostly cell-based but also biochemical (e.g. HTRF). These assays underpin both the functional validation of our intracellular antibodies and the screening and characterisation of small-molecule binders/libraries. You will apply your expertise in cell and molecular biology to design, execute and interpret experiments, and you will play a key role in building our screening and R&D capabilities. You will ideally already have a broad understanding of the drug discovery process, acquired preferably in a biotech or pharma setting, with strong hands-on experience in assay development, optimisation and QC preferably for medium/high throughput screens lab automation and small-molecule screening, as well as target validation and target engagement/mechanism-of-action studies. You are organised, keep meticulous records and are an effective team player, keen to share your expertise with colleagues and to contribute to our inclusive company culture. We offer a competitive salary and pension. PURPOSE & MISSION This role will deliver robust, screening-ready assays and high-quality screening data to support Kodiform's intracellular antibody (iDAb) platform and small-molecule discovery programmes. The postholder will independently, or under guidance develop, optimise, miniaturise and run assays, mostly cell-based (e.g. reporter gene, BRET/NanoBRET, high-content imaging) as well as biochemical formats such as HTRF/TR-FRET. These assays will be used to functionally validate newly identified iDAbs in cells and to screen, triage and profile small molecules. The data generated will drive hit identification, hit validation and progression decisions across our programmes. DIMENSIONS & STAKEHOLDERS Line manager - TBD. Scientists team: cell biology/pharmacology and protein sciences colleagues Interact with suppliers of reagents, cell lines, assay kits and consumables, as well as lab-automation collaborators, managers of shared facilities and service engineers. Kodiform Laboratory Manager and Biological Safety Officer: laboratory operations, equipment, genetic modification (GM), biosafety and COSHH compliance. No direct reports and no budget responsibility; you may help train colleagues on screening workflows and equipment. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES Small molecules / iDAbs screening Plan and run medium- to high-throughput small-molecule screening campaigns end to end (primary screen, hit confirmation, dose-response and counter-screens) in 96- to 1536-well formats. Set up, programme and run lab automation: prepare compounds for acoustic compound dispensing (e.g. Echo), liquid and cell dispensers/handlers, plate washers and multimode plate readers. Prepare and manage assay-ready compound plates, dilution series, plate maps and associated metadata. Monitor screen performance using plate QC metrics and apply agreed acceptance criteria. Analyse and interpret screening data (curve fitting, IC50/EC50). Develop and run iDAb-guided screening assays, e.g. cellular BRET or biochemical HTRF competition/displacement formats. Assay development Independently or with guidance design, develop and optimise cell-based assays to functionally validate newly identified iDAbs, including intracellular expression, target binding, functional readouts, and mechanism-of-action studies (e.g. downstream signalling,): reporter assay, BRET/NanoBRET protein-protein interaction, RT-qPCR gene expression, immunofluorescence and flow cytometry, proliferation assays. Generate and characterise engineered cell models: transient and stable (including inducible) expression of iDAbs and tagged targets by lentiviral transduction, CRISPR knock-out/knock-in and shRNA knock-down, clonal selection and validation (e.g. Western blot, RT-qPCR, imaging). Develop biochemical assays as primary or orthogonal formats, e.g. HTRF/TR-FRET, AlphaLISA or fluorescence polarisation, using recombinant proteins and iDAbs from the protein science team. Miniaturise assays and transfer them from the bench to automated 384/1536-well formats. Manage cell lines …

items.desc: Overview of the role Bestway Healthcare is a growing healthcare businesses, operating across both pharmaceutical wholesale and community pharmacy sectors and employing over 6500 colleagues nationwide. The Cyber Cloud Security Engineer is responsible for designing, implementing, monitoring, and continually improving the organisation's cloud and cyber security posture across on-premise, hybrid, and cloud environments. The role will work closely with infrastructure, networking, application, DevOps, and business teams to ensure security is embedded into all technology services and projects. Main Responsibilities Design and maintain secure architectures and technical controls across Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, AWS, hybrid and approved Cloud services. Deliver secure configuration and designs, investigation findings, vulnerability remediation plans, monitoring improvements, documented standards and playbooks, risk assessments, audit evidence and management summaries. Play a key role in protecting our AWS and Azure cloud environments, ensuring security controls, configurations and services remain aligned to best industry practise, internal standards and PCI DSS, CE+ requirements. Works collaboratively with IT Security, Infrastructure, Networks, Architecture, Applications, Digital, DevOps, Data Protection, Audit and external security or cloud suppliers. Provides technical evaluation and recommendations that influence security tooling, cloud service and supplier expenditure. Decides the technical severity and priority of findings, appropriate containment and remediation actions, required security controls, and when material risk or exceptions must be escalated. As a trusted cloud security specialist, you will champion secure-by-design principles, provide expert guidance to stakeholders, and maintain clear documentation and reporting to demonstrate compliance, highlight risks and drive continuous improvement across our cloud estate. Act as a cloud security subject matter expert. Provides technical direction and constructive challenge but has no direct reports. The Ideal Candidate The successful candidate will have previous experience protecting business critical systems and data, reducing cyber risk, supporting compliance initiatives, and ensuring cloud technologies are deployed securely in line with best industry practice and regulatory requirements Desirable certifications include Microsoft AZ-500, SC-200, SC-300 or SC-100, plus CISSP, CISM, CCSP Security+ or ISO27001 Lead Implementor/Auditor Hands on experience securing MS Azure, MS365, AWS in a medium or large organisation, including Entra ID, Conditional Access, PIM, Defender, Sentinel and Intune. Bestway Healthcare is proud to be a diverse and inclusive employer. If you have any specific requirements, we'll do everything we can to support you. Whether it is to find a pharmacy that is accessible, or if it is a part time position you are looking for, we can help find the role that is right for you. If you need us to make any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process, we will be happy to accommodate you . Please be aware that due to the high number of applications we receive it may not be possible for us to provide an outcome to all applicants. If you are not contacted within 28 days of your submission unfortunately you will have been unsuccessful. About The Company For over 70 years, we’ve been looking after the health and wellbeing of communities across the UK. Well Pharmacy (part of Bestway Healthcare) is the second largest pharmacy chain in the UK with c.760 pharmacies and a team of around 7,000 colleagues based across our Community Pharmacies, Online Pharmacy, Healthcare Services Centre, Community Drivers, Bestway Medhub & Wardles team and our Support Centre team. Our mission is to be here for the wellbeing of our patients and customers, to provide the best community pharmacy experience in the UK for everyone, for our patients, our customers, our people, and our NHS. The pharmacy of the future will look very different from the one we know today. It will play a huge role in transforming primary healthcare and we will play a central role in bringing it to life. We will use our clinical expertise and technological ambition to take advantage of the potential this future has to offer us. Making medicines, advice, services and care available in the places and spaces that people need and want it most. We want to be a great business. To be recognised as delivering a community pharmacy experience that is the best there is. To do this we want our teams to feel proud about the positive impact they make, feel valued as part of a close-knit and expert community, and feel confident in their role in a business that is stable, innovative, and caring. ‘Together we make a difference’

items.desc: About WhatWorked Education WhatWorked Education helps teachers find out what works through micro-randomised controlled trials (micro-RCTs): small, rigorous trials run in their own classrooms. Our platform guides them through each trial and produces automated analysis and instant impact reports. We now plan to extend the model beyond education, starting with health within the next 12 months. About the role You will be our first in-house engineer, leading the move of platform development from our current development partner. AI makes it realistic for a compact team to do work that once needed a larger team, and we want that engineer close to our users, trials and funders. You will set up an AI-assisted way of working, design the platform to support trials across domains such as health, and explore new uses of AI. The engineering strategy is not fixed: we want you to help shape it. Our current stack includes PHP/ Symfony, React, PostgreSQL and AWS. Key responsibilities Lead the handover from our development partner, including an audit of code, AWS hosting, database and third-party APIs. Keep the platform secure and reliable, and own the quality of everything released, including AI-generated code. Set up an AI-assisted development pipeline with automated testing and human review. Design the platform to support trials in new domains, starting with health. Act as part-time product manager, working with colleagues and practitioners to turn their needs into improvements. Protect personal data, including children's data and, in future, health data. Person specification Essential Extensive full-stack experience building non-trivial products, with strong architectural judgement. Actively uses AI tools in development and can critically evaluate AI-generated code. Works well with non-technical colleagues and explains technical ideas clearly. An entrepreneurial, enabling mindset suited to a small, early-stage organisation. Genuine interest in evidence, education or health, and randomised controlled trials. Understands data protection and the handling of sensitive data. Able to work from our Durham office at least three days a week. Desirable Experience of AI-first workflows or building AI integrations (for example MCP servers). Experience with PHP (Symfony), React, PostgreSQL, AWS and third-party APIs. Experience of taking over a codebase from an external supplier. What success looks like in your first year By the end of your first year, the platform will be running reliably under our ownership, your AI-assisted pipeline will be delivering improvements, and first steps towards health trials will be underway. What we offer The opportunity to become a key senior leader in the company, shaping its direction as well as its technology. The chance to build our technology and engineering approach from the ground up. Work with real-world impact, helping practitioners find out what works for the people they serve. A starting salary of £60,000 plus a performance bonus, with hybrid working from Durham. A 10% employer pension contribution. A flexible annual leave policy, with at least 25 days plus bank holidays. Please submit your CV and a covering letter (max. 2 pages) via Indeed. In your letter, tell us about a difficult problem you solved creatively and how you use AI in your work. items.desc: Job Description Strategy Consultant Accenture Commodity Markets & Trading Location: London, UK About Accenture CEO Advisory Accenture CEO Advisory works with chief executives, boards and their leadership teams on the decisions that set enterprise direction: where to compete, what to own, how to fund a shift in the portfolio, and what the operating model has to become to support it. The work sits upstream of execution but is judged on whether it survives contact with it, so we pair industry depth with the quantitative, technology and delivery capability to pressure-test an answer before a client commits capital behind it. About Accenture Commodity Markets Accenture Commodity Markets (ACM), part of Accenture CEO Advisory, is a global practice operating across multiple industries. It is one of the few global strategy practices offering breadth of cross-industry exposure alongside genuinely global project experience, working with organisations focused on commodity production, trading, logistics and marketing.We combine industry knowledge across energy, chemicals, soft commodities, agriculture, metals, mining, utilities, transportation and consumer goods with analytics-led core strategy consulting, digital and AI capability. Within Accenture we are known for the variety and complexity of the problems we take on, a close-knit global team, early responsibility for our people, rapid career progression and international exposure, having delivered projects in over 25 countries. Our solution areas Investment and Asset Portfolio Optimisation: portfolio strategy, capital allocation, long-term market modelling, M&A support, and integrated optimisation across physical and financial positions. Trading and Market Optimisation: trading strategy, positioning and risk management through advanced analytics, real-time insight, hedging, algorithmic trading and P&L attribution. Commodity Markets Decision Platforms, Ecosystem and Execution: AI-enabled decision platforms, CTRM/ETRM selection, ecosystem partners (Salesforce, Palantir and others), data architecture, AI model development and automation. Enterprise Activation and Operational Readiness: operating model design, go-live strategy and capability build-out, so organisations can operate, trade and optimise from day one. Commodity Sourcing and Exposure Management: sourcing, hedging and supplier strategy for commodity-exposed industries, optimising cost, risk and resilience under market volatility. The Role As a Strategy Consultant, you will be a core member of our engagement teams, owning defined workstreams and the analysis behind them. You will work closely with Managers, Senior Managers, and Managing Directors to turn complex, ambiguous client questions into structured, evidence-based recommendations, and you will build the quantitative, industry and client skills to progress rapidly towards leading workstreams and teams. Key Responsibilities Client delivery Own and deliver workstreams within client engagements, structuring problems, building the analysis and drawing out clear, actionable insights, with guidance from the engagement Manager.Build and maintain models and analytical tools, including market, financial and valuation models, and apply analytics, data science and AI techniques where they add value.Develop high-quality client materials and present findings and recommendations clearly, including in client interviews and workshops.Work on topics such as corporate and portfolio strategy, trading and risk management capability set-up, operating model design, commercial optimisation, investment valuation, energy market liberalisation, the energy transition, and numerical modelling of energy and commodity markets. Client relationships Build credible working relationships with client counterparts, understanding their needs and working style.Take fresh, well-evidenced ideas to clients and contribute to a culture of constructive challenge. Team and development Support and mentor Analysts sharing knowledge and giving practical feedback as you gain experience.Take ownership of your own development, seeking feedback and building depth in one or more of our solution areas. Firm contribution Support business development by running industry and company research (competitor and market scanning, market fundamentals, financials, customers) and building proposal materials.Contribute to ACM UK, global ACM and the wider CEO Advisory community, including offerings, assets and thought leadership. items.desc: If you’re looking for a career that will help you stand out, join HSBC, and fulfil your potential - whether you want a career that could take you to the top, or simply take you in an exciting new direction, HSBC offers opportunities, support and rewards that will take you further. HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world, with operations in 64 countries and territories. We aim to be where the growth is, enabling businesses to thrive and economies to prosper, and, ultimately, helping people to fulfil their hopes and realise their ambitions. We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Site Reliability Engineer. We are looking for an enthusiastic and collaborative Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) to join our growing strategic team. You’ll contribute to the stability, scalability, and automation of our cloud-based production environments and play a key role in ensuring our services are reliable and high-performing. You’ll support system availability, monitoring, alerting, SLOs/SLIs and incident response; deploy and manage containerised applications, contribute to CI/CD and Kubernetes GitOps practices; automate processes, and work closely with development, QA and operations teams to resolve complex issues and improve services. As an HSBC employee in the UK, you will have access to tailored professional development opportunities and a competitive pay and benefits package. This includes private healthcare for all UK-based employees, enhanced maternity and adoption pay and support when you return to work, and a contributory pension scheme with a generous employer contribution. In this role you’ll: Maintain and support production systems to ensure high availability, reliability and scalability. Implement SRE practices, including monitoring, alerting, SLOs, SLIs and incident response. Deploy, configure and manage containerised applications using Docker and Kubernetes. Develop and enhance CI/CD pipelines to improve software delivery and deployment processes. Automate operational tasks using Python, Bash, Go or comparable scripting languages. Collaborate with development, QA and operations teams to resolve issues and improve services. Participate in the on-call support rota and respond to production incidents promptly. Document procedures, system configurations and post-incident reviews to support continuous learning and improvement. To be successful in this role you should meet the following requirements: Hands-on experience in SRE, DevOps or production support. Practical knowledge of GCP, AWS or Azure environments. Experience with Docker and Kubernetes; knowledge of Helm or Istio is advantageous. Ability to use tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Jaeger or Datadog. Familiarity with Jenkins, GitLab CI, ArgoCD, FluxCD or Tekton. Proficiency in Python, Bash, Go or comparable languages. Strong analytical skills and the ability to resolve complex production issues. Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Ansible, plus exposure to microservices and high-availability environments. Role overview: Enterprise Supply Chain Services (ESCS) is part of the Leidos UK solution responsible for sourcing and procurement, inventory, planning and order management. The team is developing a new supply chain management system, initially as a technical demonstrator, with the aim of developing it into a production-ready solution. Apply systems engineering across the ESCS lifecycle, translating business and operational needs into coherent, traceable system requirements, interface specifications and model artefacts. The Systems Engineer will support the definition, analysis, integration and verification of ESCS capabilities, working across architecture, software, data, cloud, test and supplier teams to maintain the technical integrity of the end-to-end solution. Support system integration and verification by ensuring requirements, interfaces, dependencies and acceptance evidence remain coherent throughout delivery. What will I be doing? Elicit, analyse, decompose and manage functional and non-functional system requirements, maintaining traceability through design, integration, verification and acceptance. Develop and maintain system models, functional and logical views, interface definitions and Interface Control Documents (ICDs). Analyse end-to-end system interactions, data flows, dependencies, constraints and behaviours across ESCS capabilities and external systems. Undertake system-level analysis and modelling of non-functional characteristics, including availability, reliability, performance, capacity, resilience and recoverability. Work with architects, software, data, cloud, security, test and supplier teams to ensure designs and implementations remain aligned with system requirements and defined interfaces. Support verification and validation activities, including definition of acceptance criteria against requirements and requirements-to-verification traceability, and verification through the means of analysis and inspection techniques. Identify, analyse and manage technical risks, assumptions, dependencies, issues and opportunities within assigned areas. Contribute engineering evidence to technical reviews, design reviews, integration readiness and capability acceptance. Maintain systems engineering artefacts under appropriate configuration and change control. Required skills and capabilities Systems engineering across the engineering lifecycle Requirements engineering, decomposition and traceability for both functional and non-functional domains System architecture and functional analysis Interface definition and production of interfaces specifications (Interface Control Documents) System modelling and Model-Based Systems Engineering principles Functional and non-functional requirements analysis Availability, reliability, performance and capacity analysis Application and planning of verification and validation methods for requirements Technical risk, assumption and dependency management Strong use of engineering best practice, including engineering methodologies, expert configuration and change control and secure systems engineering principles. Clear and proficient written and verbal communication Required experience Systems engineering experience on complex, software-oriented systems self-hosted within public and private cloud platforms. Experience developing and managing system requirements in line with INCOSE best practice and maintaining traceability to design and verification compliance evidence throughout the engineering lifecycle. Experience defining interfaces between systems, applications or services and producing associated interface documentation. Experience applying modelling or analytical techniques to understand system behaviour, dependencies or non-functional characteristics. Experience supporting system integration, verification and technical assurance in a multidisciplinary engineering environment. Ability to work independently within an assigned engineering scope and collaborate effectively with architects, software engineers, test engineers, suppliers and other engineering disciplines. Desired experience Solutions hosted across hyperscaler platforms; preferably AWS. Complex systems integration programmes that include enterprise SaaS and Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) systems. Supply chain, procurement, order management, logistics or ERP-related systems. Model-Based Systems Engineering and appropriate modelling notation/tooling, such as SysML 1.6, SysML 2.0 or Archimate. items.desc: Automation Engineer | Home Made Join our technology team and build tools that make everyday work simpler, smarter and more effective. The Role A renter hasn’t been followed up, a listing has the wrong price, or a team is spending hours checking information across systems. Your role is to understand what’s going wrong and build a reliable way to fix it. You’ll create automations, integrations and internal tools that help our leasing, marketing and operations teams work more effectively. That means getting close to the people doing the work, understanding their needs and taking solutions all the way from an initial idea to something they use every day. Working directly with our Technical Lead, who sets the overall architectural direction, you’ll own implementation and delivery. You’ll scope, build, test and deploy solutions, train colleagues to use them, and keep improving them based on performance, cost and feedback. If you enjoy untangling a messy process, building something useful and seeing the difference it makes, you’ll enjoy this role. Working with us Home Made is a lettings proptech company on a mission to fix renting for good. We combine technology with a high-performing team to make the rental experience better, safer and fairer for renters and property owners. Our culture is built on driving change, working with integrity and making space for different perspectives. We want people to ask questions, contribute ideas and take ownership, with everyone having the opportunity to be heard. You’ll work closely with colleagues across the business and see the impact of what you build in their day-to-day work. There’s plenty to improve, room to contribute and the opportunity to help shape how we use technology as we grow. Role and Opportunities Understand the problem and plan the solution Work with teams to understand their processes, spot recurring problems and identify opportunities for automation. Turn broad requests into clear requirements, manageable scopes and practical technical designs. Agree what success looks like before building, whether that’s time saved, fewer errors, faster follow-up or better conversion. Prioritise work based on business value, effort and ongoing maintenance. Build tools that make a difference Develop automations, APIs and integrations across multiple ecosystems. Join and reconcile operational data so that tools and decisions are based on reliable information. Build straightforward, user-friendly web interfaces for internal tools. Use LLM APIs where useful for tasks such as extracting information, summarising calls and drafting recommendations. Write maintainable code and contribute reusable components that make future delivery easier. Test, launch and help people use what you build Test accuracy, reliability and behaviour when data is missing or systems fail. Manage deployment with appropriate monitoring and clear documentation. Train colleagues and explain how tools work, when to use them and where their limitations lie. Check adoption and understanding after launch, gathering feedback and addressing anything that gets in the way. Improve and maintain Monitor performance, usage and running costs, and make improvements based on evidence. Troubleshoot failures and keep integrations reliable as systems and processes change. Measure results against the original goal and identify where further changes are needed. Review implementations, share knowledge and support less experienced colleagues. About You A practical problem-solver: You enjoy understanding how things work and finding a sensible way to improve them. An owner: You spot problems, take action and follow through, including after a tool has launched. Commercially aware: You can distinguish between an interesting technical project and something that will make a meaningful difference to the business. A clear communicator: You’re comfortable talking to non-technical colleagues, asking questions and explaining decisions without unnecessary jargon. Thoughtful about the details: You know that incorrect data or an unreliable integration can create more work than it saves. Adaptable and collaborative: You can balance competing priorities, respond to feedback and work within an existing stack. Curious: You’re keen to learn, test new approaches and share what you discover. Experience you’ll already have A track record of independently delivering and maintaining production software, integrations or automation in a commercial environment. Strong TypeScript and Node.js skills, including APIs, background jobs and integrations. Strong SQL skills and experience investigating and reconciling data across systems. Experience building straightforward web interfaces using React, Next.js or similar tools. Familiarity with testing, version control, deployment and monitoring. items.desc: About Us At Travel Counsellors, our customers, communities and colleagues are at the heart of what we do. For more than 30 years, we’ve supported independent travel professionals to build successful businesses and create personal connections with their customers. Today, more than 2,200 Travel Counsellors around the world are supported by a team of over 400 colleagues in our Support Offices. We’re continuing to grow and invest in technology that helps our people deliver exceptional service. Travel Counsellors was named Best Place to Work in Travel in 2022 and featured in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work in 2023, 2024 and 2025. We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our technology team. About the Role As a Software Engineer, you’ll build and improve the digital services that help Travel Counsellors serve their customers and run their businesses. You’ll join a strategic engineering team and work in the domain where your skills can make the greatest difference. You’ll develop dependable C# and .NET software, working with engineers, product colleagues and domain specialists to understand customer and operational needs. You’ll contribute throughout the delivery lifecycle, from exploring requirements and shaping solutions to testing, release and production support. We use modern engineering practices and AI development tools to help teams work effectively. You’ll use your judgement to choose where AI can help, provide clear context, and review and test its output. You’ll remain responsible for the quality, security and maintainability of the software you deliver. What You’ll Do Build, test and support software that meets customer, product and operational needs. Develop and maintain C# and .NET services, APIs and integrations. Work with colleagues to understand requirements, explore options and deliver changes incrementally. Contribute throughout the delivery lifecycle, including production support. Write automated tests, take part in peer reviews, follow secure coding practices and help monitor services. Use AI coding tools such as Cursor, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot where they’re useful. Provide context, review and test their output, and take responsibility for what you ship. Learn about the team’s domain, architecture and operational needs, and share useful knowledge with colleagues. Communicate progress and raise questions, risks and dependencies early. What You’ll Bring You’ll have a sound foundation in software development, with professional experience—typically around three years or more—and good knowledge of C# and .NET, or equivalent practical experience and progression. You’ll also have experience or be developing your capability in areas such as APIs, data stores, automated testing and cloud services. Our teams work with AWS, SQL Server and CI/CD processes, and may use document databases such as MongoDB. You don’t need to know every part of our technology stack; curiosity and a willingness to learn matter. You’ll work well with others, communicate clearly and be open to feedback. You’ll be comfortable using modern development tools, including AI tools, with care and sound judgement. A degree or formal qualification is welcome, but equivalent practical experience is equally valued. Travel industry experience isn’t required. Our Benefits Competitive salary and annual bonus Flexible hybrid working Career development opportunities 25 days’ holiday, increasing to 28 after five years Enhanced maternity and paternity pay One paid charity day Company events and incentives Death in service benefit of three times your salary Pension scheme Private Medical Insurance or Healthcare Cash Plan Free breakfast and beverages Inclusive Recruitment at Travel Counsellors We’re committed to building an inclusive workplace and welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, disability or any other protected characteristic. If you need an adjustment during the recruitment process, please let us know. We’ll work with you to make the process accessible. If this role interests you but you don’t meet every requirement, we’d still encourage you to apply. For more information about this role or other opportunities at Travel Counsellors, contact our Talent Acquisition team at talentacquisition@travelcounsellors.com.

The successful candidate will contribute to the delivery and development of high-quality inpatient and outpatient surgical services, supporting routine, cancer and elective activity. This role offers the opportunity to develop a specialist interest within General Surgery, contribute to service improvement and take an active role in the leadership and development of the department. We are seeking an experienced General Surgeon with a minimum of five years’ experience at Registrar level within the UK NHS, who is committed to delivering excellent, patient-centred care and working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team. Key Duties include : Deliver high-quality inpatient and outpatient General Surgical services, contributing to elective, cancer and waiting-list activity targets. Support the continued development of elective surgical services and, where required, contribute to the management of surgical emergencies. Support the teaching, supervision and professional development of junior and middle-grade medical staff. Work collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to improve patient pathways, service efficiency and the quality of care. As part of this collaborative approach, there may be a requirement for you to work across both the Kettering and Northampton hospital sites, depending on the needs of the service. items.desc: The Band 5 Scrub Practitioner delivers safe, high-quality, evidence-based perioperative care across the Trust’s General operating theatres, assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating care while managing an allocated caseload. The role supports a diverse range of elective and emergency surgical activity, including robotic surgery, urology, breast surgery, gynaecology, gynaecological oncology, colorectal surgery and upper gastrointestinal surgery. Main responsibilities include maintaining aseptic technique; preparing, checking and managing surgical instruments, implants, medical devices and specialist equipment; providing scrub assistance for procedures across these specialties; completing instrument, needle and swab counts and the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist; supporting safe patient positioning, transfer and theatre preparation; anticipating and responding to intraoperative needs; communicating effectively with patients, carers and the multidisciplinary team; safeguarding dignity and safety; maintaining accurate records; complying with professional, Trust, infection prevention, information governance and risk-management standards; reporting and supporting the investigation of incidents; contributing to audit, service improvement and research-based practice; undertaking mandatory training and continuing professional development; and supervising, teaching and supporting learners, new staff and less experienced colleagues while acting as a professional role model. Clinical Responsibilities / Key Responsibilities Maintain aseptic technique and provide safe, effective scrub assistance for elective and emergency procedures across robotic surgery, urology, breast surgery, gynaecology, gynaecological oncology, colorectal surgery and upper gastrointestinal surgery, working within assessed competence. Prepare, check, manage and account for surgical instrumentation, implants, prostheses, medical devices and equipment appropriate to the procedure and specialty. Accurately perform and document instrument, needle and swab counts, and actively participate in all relevant stages of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist and associated perioperative safety checks. Anticipate the needs of the surgical team, respond appropriately to intraoperative changes and escalate concerns promptly to maintain patient safety. Support safe patient positioning and transfer, and prepare, check and restore the theatre environment before and after surgery in accordance with local procedures and assessed competence. items.desc: Why might this job interest you? We have an exciting opportunity for a Pharmacy Technician Higher Level at East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust to join the Pharmacy Department at William Harvey Hospital in Ashford or Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother Hospital in Margate. You will be responsible for working closely with Pharmacists and other healthcare professionals within the multi-disciplinary team in the Emergency Department to deliver high-quality, patient-focused medicines management services. You will manage the compilation and verification of patient drug histories by communicating with patients, carers, GPs, and other health professionals, ensuring any discrepancies are resolved or appropriately referred. You will also support the team by checking and documenting specified blood results, interpreting medical and nursing notes for medicines reconciliation, and identifying patient-drug or drug-disease interactions, referring as necessary to ensure safe and effective patient care. As a Pharmacy Technician Higher Level, you will be responsible for documenting patients’ allergies and reactions to medicines, ensuring accurate records are maintained. You will be managing reviews of patients’ own drugs to assess suitability during their hospital stay and supporting discharge planning in collaboration with ward staff and other healthcare professionals across secondary and primary care. You will be responsible for giving out medication to patients, providing counselling on correct usage, dosages, side effects, and device administration, while addressing any questions or concerns. You will also administer medicines within your competence, considering prescriptions, patient conditions, observations, and blood results, document consultations appropriately, and help minimise delays in discharge by ensuring timely availability of medications. Responsibilities of this job role To dispense prescriptions when required, ensuring all medications are prepared accurately and in accordance with trust guidelines. You will also check for completeness and appropriateness of prescriptions prior to dispensing. To assist with the management and movement of medicines between wards, including controlled drugs, to maintain efficient supply chains. You will also identify medicines needing safe return or disposal and coordinate with the pharmacy team. To provide medicines-related information and guidance to external healthcare organisations, such as GP surgeries and community pharmacies, to support admission and discharge processes. You will also suggest improvements to communication pathways to enhance patient care. To support the training, mentoring, and competency assessment of pre-registration trainee pharmacy technicians, junior pharmacy technicians, and pre-registration pharmacists. You will act as a role model and contribute to the development of staff through guidance, education, and feedback. To contribute to quality management and service improvement by reviewing procedures, suggesting enhancements, and participating in audits. You will also assist in the writing and maintenance of standard operating procedures for the pharmacy team. To maintain professional registration with the General Pharmaceutical Council and actively engage in continuous professional development (CPD). This includes completing mandatory training, local accreditations, and participating in meetings or learning sessions to ensure up-to-date knowledge and compliance with best practices. To be successful in applying for this role you will need: NVQ Level 3 in Pharmacy Services or BTEC in Pharmaceutical Science (or equivalent). Registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC). Accredited in medicines management and accuracy checking pharmacy technician (ACPT). Experience with NHS systems (e.g., PAS, RIS) and Microsoft packages. Desirable: hospital pharmacy experience or Medicines Optimisation Programme competence. items.desc: Job Description Ramboll is looking for an Electrical Design Engineer to join our growing Life Science & Pharma team. You will work as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team delivering technically demanding projects across the life sciences, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, laboratory and research sectors . Projects may range from new-build laboratories and research facilities through to refurbishment, retrofit and complex modifications within existing operational environments. The role offers the opportunity to develop strong technical expertise while working closely with electrical, mechanical, public health, sustainability and other specialist disciplines. You will contribute throughout the design process, from early feasibility and concept design through detailed design, procurement, construction and commissioning. Your key responsibilities As an Electrical Design Engineer, you will: Develop electrical building-services designs for laboratories, research facilities, pharmaceutical and other technically complex buildings . Undertake design and specification of: HV and LV electrical distribution systems Transformers and main switchgear Standby generation and UPS systems Small power and specialist power supplies General and emergency lighting Earthing and lightning protection Fire alarm and life-safety interfaces ICT, security and other ELV systems Prepare electrical calculations, technical specifications, drawings, schedules and reports. Undertake electrical load assessments and contribute to resilient and maintainable electrical infrastructure strategies. Carry out lighting calculations, cable sizing, voltage-drop, fault-level and protection studies using appropriate engineering software. Work with project BIM/Revit models and coordinate electrical services with the wider building design. Coordinate with mechanical engineers and specialist designers on equipment power requirements, controls and interfaces. Support the development of design solutions for laboratories and controlled environments where resilience, business continuity and reliability of electrical supplies are important design considerations. Undertake surveys and assessments of existing buildings and electrical infrastructure, including projects involving refurbishment and retrofit. Participate in design workshops, coordination meetings and technical reviews. Review contractor proposals, technical submissions and shop drawings against the design intent. Attend construction sites, undertake inspections and support testing, commissioning and witnessing activities. Assist with resolving technical issues during construction. Contribute to project documentation and quality-assurance processes. Work collaboratively with clients, architects, contractors, equipment suppliers and other engineering disciplines. About you We are looking for someone who is fundamentally a technically strong electrical engineer , with an interest in developing expertise within the Life Science & Pharma sector. You will ideally have: A degree, HNC/HND or equivalent qualification in Electrical Engineering, Building Services Engineering or a related discipline . Experience in electrical building-services design within a consultancy, contractor or similar engineering environment. A sound understanding of LV electrical distribution and building electrical systems. Familiarity with relevant UK electrical and building-services standards, particularly BS 7671 / IET Wiring Regulations . Experience producing electrical calculations and technical design information. An understanding of engineering design through RIBA design stages. Experience using engineering design software such as Amtech/Trimble ProDesign, EOM, Dialux or equivalent . Experience working with Revit and BIM environments , or a willingness to develop these skills. Good written and verbal communication skills. An organised and methodical approach to engineering design. The ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary project team. Life Science & Pharma experience Previous experience of laboratories or pharmaceutical projects would be advantageous, but it is not essential . Experience in any of the following would be particularly relevant: Research and development laboratories Containment laboratories CL2/CL3 environments Pharmaceutical manufacturing GMP facilities Cleanrooms and controlled environments Universities and research institutions Healthcare or other critical environments Mission-critical or high-resilience electrical infrastructure We are particularly interested in engineers who are curious about how these environments operate and want to understand the relationship between scientific processes, specialist equipment, building services and electrical infrastructure . You will be someone who enjoys getting into the detail of an electrical design while retaining an understanding of the wider project. In Life Science & Pharma projects, that means thinking beyond simply providing …

items.desc: As a Locum Consultant in Palliative Medicine at Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, you will join one of England’s best ‑ performing and most highly rated NHS organisations, providing high ‑ quality specialist care across two main hospital sites—Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital—as well as a network of community ‑ based services. You will be part of a multidisciplinary environment that serves a diverse population and delivers award ‑ winning services, including complex medical, cancer, and supportive care pathways. In this role, you will provide expert palliative and end ‑ of ‑ life care, collaborating closely with acute teams, community partners, and specialist services to support patients with complex symptom management and holistic needs. You will contribute to high ‑ quality clinical care, leadership, teaching, and service development within a Trust that continually invests in its facilities—including major expansions in critical care and diagnostic services—to enhance patient experience and clinical outcomes. You will join a motivated, well ‑ supported workforce of more than 6,000 staff who are PROUD to Care and who consistently recommend the Trust as an excellent place to work and receive treatment. Please note: Some roles may require weekend shifts at multiple sites. Please refer to the attached job description document for a detailed list of the main duties of the job. Our Trust is one of England's top-performing and safest trusts. We operate two main acute hospital sites—Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital—along with award-winning clinics across North West London. Our nearly 7,500 staff care for a diverse population of 1.5m, providing full clinical services including maternity, A&E and children’s services, plus specialist HIV and sexual health care. The CQC rates us Good in safety, effectiveness, care and responsiveness, and Outstanding in leadership and resource use. We continually invest in our facilities, including a £30m expansion of critical care at Chelsea and an £80m Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre at West Mid. We are delivering sustainable healthcare through our Green Plan. In line with Greener NHS ambitions, we aim for net zero carbon emissions by 2045. Achieving this requires collective effort. We encourage staff to reduce their impact on carbon, waste and pollution wherever possible. Every action counts to create a healthier, more sustainable future. We are committed to equal opportunities and believe diversity drives innovation and excellence. We welcome applications from the global majority, veterans and underrepresented communities, valuing the perspectives they bring. Provide an efficient and responsive clinical service for patients requiring supportive and palliative care. Deliver high ‑ quality specialist palliative care within the hospital and community settings. Work as part of a multidisciplinary team to support patients and relatives across the palliative care pathway. Develop and maintain strong working relationships with key colleagues across community and hospital services. Participate in cross ‑ clinical cover within other areas of the specialist palliative care service, including liaison with hospital teams. Contribute to strategic development and service improvement initiatives across the palliative care service. Participate in rota arrangements for the palliative care service as required. Provide clinical leadership and guidance within the palliative care team. Support education, training, and development opportunities for colleagues within the service. Contribute to the coordination and delivery of a 7 ‑ day visiting and on ‑ call service, if the department has such arrangement in place. Engage in service ‑ wide quality improvement, innovation, and integrated models of care. Provide specialist advice and support to other healthcare professionals managing palliative care needs. Participate in multidisciplinary meetings to review patient needs and optimise care planning. Ensure continuity and safety of patient care through effective documentation and communication. Promote a compassionate, person ‑ centred approach to end ‑ of ‑ life care across all clinical interactions.

items.desc: Date: 5 Nov 2026 Location: Bracknell, GB Company: Honda Motor Europe Ltd At Honda we embrace inclusion in our various policies, so whilst our contracts state that the hours are as required to fulfil the role with a minimum of 35 hours per week, we offer flexibility for when you work. The regular office hours are 08:00 – 16:00 Monday to Thursday with a half hour lunch break & 08:00 – 13:00 on a Friday. However, we offer flexibility of when you work with our daily flex-time start of between 07:00 and 11:00 providing that there is no business requirement. Whilst there is no contractual right to work from home, the flexibility we offer is that you can request to work from home 2 days per week, again providing there is no business requirement to attend the office. Role: Honda Motor Europe is offering an undergraduate the opportunity to join the newly created Digital and Data Division as part of the Connectivity Solutions team for a 12-month placement starting in July 2027. The Division has been established to accelerate Honda Europe’s adoption of AI, strengthen the data foundations of the company and unlock new value from data for customers and the business. The Connectivity Solutions team plays a key role in this ambition. Data generated by Honda products, including cars, motorcycles and power products such as lawnmowers, creates new possibilities to improve customer experiences, support business decision-making and develop new services. The team is also supporting the development and European readiness of Honda’s next-generation connectivity solution, GC5.0, planned to launch in March 2028. The undergraduate will contribute across this wider agenda, working with teams across Honda Europe and supporting practical delivery. Key activities will include helping to prepare for GC5.0 through cross-functional coordination and solution testing; supporting data value-realisation projects with other divisions; monitoring competitor, technology and market developments; and reporting on the performance of current connectivity solutions, including customer activations, subscriptions and wider engagement. As part of the preparation for GC5.0, testing will need to be done on new vehicles far in advance of their launch. The role provides broad exposure to connected products, data-led innovation and the delivery of Honda’s digital future. Main Responsibilities: Reporting and business insight Prepare regular reports and dashboards showing how Honda’s current connectivity solutions are performing, including customer activations, subscriptions, usage and engagement. Analyse results by European market, identify trends or issues and help the team turn findings into clear actions and recommendations. Support cost, revenue and supplier reporting, gaining practical experience of how a European business monitors performance and makes decisions. Testing and next-generation connectivity readiness Support testing of new connected features, vehicle models and app updates, including planning test activities, recording results and following up issues with delivery teams. This involves hands on time with new vehicles yet to be launched into the European market. Contribute to European readiness for Honda’s next-generation GC5.0 connectivity solution, planned to launch in March 2028. Support with coordination of User Acceptance Testing working with other under grads, supervised by the connectivity solution team. Support assessment of connected-services and vehicle-data regulatory requirements, working with specialist teams and assisting with updates to customer terms and privacy policies under team guidance and legal dept review. Market sensing and competitor monitoring Research competitor connected services, pricing, technology and emerging market trends across Europe. Summarise findings in clear presentations and reports to help identify opportunities for new services and improvements to Honda’s existing solutions. items.desc: Industry leader? Well, how about an industry creator?! WalkMe, an SAP company, pioneered the world's leading Digital Adoption Platform, helping organizations navigate change across any application or system. Today it is the platform that drives AI adoption across the enterprise. Enterprise work stays fragmented across applications, and that fragmentation compounds as AI advances. Traditional training and vendor-provided help leave organizations managing change one application at a time. WalkMe guides people through change, brings AI into the flow of work, automates tasks and shows executives how workflows perform. Global leaders including IBM, Nestlé, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and the U.S. federal government trust WalkMe. WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance. So, if you’re an expert in your field, and looking for an opportunity to work, collaborate, and innovate with some of the most talented people out there, WalkMe is the place for you! As a Technical Architect at WalkMe, you’ll sit between Solution Architecture and Account Management, helping customers deploy, integrate and get the most out of our platform. You’ll own the technical side of delivery for complex organizations: infrastructure, deployment, integration and long-term technical strategy. Your job is to make sure customers have the right foundation in place to succeed with digital adoption. You’ll be both the technical expert and the quarterback, leading customers through complex deployments with confidence, clarity and care. You’ll work closely with customers to understand their environments and requirements, give hands-on guidance, and partner with Product, Engineering, Support and the Customer Success team so technical decisions line up with customer goals and our product roadmap. You’ll communicate proactively, move with urgency, and stay adaptable when things move fast or aren’t clear. *** Working Days - Monday to Friday What you'll own Customer onboarding and technical readiness: Lead new customer onboarding and make sure environments are ready for deployment, including network configuration. Deployment and integration: Deploy and integrate WalkMe into customer environments. That includes connecting identity providers, configuring browser extensions, setting up API integrations and making sure workflows run smoothly end to end. Technical advisory: Act as the main technical advisor for your accounts. Talk through different architecture setups and their trade-offs, and give best-practice guidance on deployment, performance and reliability. Troubleshooting and escalations: Troubleshoot deployment issues, including browser/OS compatibility and performance. Join high-severity cases as a product expert and customer advocate. Ownership and risk management: Take full ownership of your work, push things forward, clear roadblocks, and flag risks or blockers early. Strategic direction: Plan and advise on solutions and enhancements that support the customer’s business needs and long-term technical continuity. Cross-functional liaison: Be the link between customers, Product, Engineering, Support and the Customer Success team. Close gaps, run the conversations and keep everyone aligned on features, technical hurdles and the roadmap. Customer education: Help customers understand how the platform works technically, including infrastructure, privacy and security. Documentation: Write and maintain technical documentation such as installation guides, configuration guides and troubleshooting materials. Relationships: Build trust with customers, know them well, and speak up for them inside WalkMe. *** Working Days - Monday to Friday What you need to succeed Technical Skills Experience with web technologies (JavaScript, HTML, CSS) and building with APIs Knowledge of Chromium-based extension APIs and permissions Hands-on software deployment experience across Windows, macOS and VDI, including mass deployment tools and policies Experience with Identity and Access Management, including setting up identity provider integrations and working with SAML, OAuth, OIDC, SSO and MFA Working understanding of SaaS architecture, cloud delivery models and IT infrastructure (servers, databases, networking, compute) Familiarity with tools like JIRA and internal knowledge bases Professional Skills Strong communicator who sets expectations, shares updates proactively, listens with empathy, and adjusts the message for C-level, technical and business audiences Strong project management skills and a track record of running several deployments at once and delivering on time Comfortable with ambiguity and able to solve open-ended problems when there’s no set process Able to turn customer needs into technical requirements Customer-service mindset; IT helpdesk or customer-facing technical experience is a plus Driven and fast-moving: you follow through quickly and don’t let blockers slow you down Collaborative: we’re one team, and we support each other ** Native or bilingual …

Support Practitioner - Dispersed Services Have you had experience working as a housing support worker? Do you hold the necessary skills to empower, coach and inspire people to move forward positively with their lives? As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People.
